udhaar.title: Udhaar (credit)
udhaar.body: The customer takes the item now and pays later, all or part of it. The app keeps what is left on his khata until he pays. In English software this is called "credit".
udhaar.example: Phone Rs. 50,000. He pays Rs. 20,000 now → Rs. 30,000 udhaar on his khata.

khata.title: Khata (account)
khata.body: One page per person (customer, dealer, other shop) with every bill and payment between you. It shows how much you will get from him or have to give him.
khata.example: Bilal's khata: bought on udhaar Rs. 30,000, paid Rs. 10,000 → you will get Rs. 20,000.

cost.title: Buying price
cost.body: What the shop paid for the item. Only the owner and the manager see it. Profit is worked out from it.
cost.example: You bought a phone for Rs. 45,000: the buying price is Rs. 45,000.

asking.title: Selling price
asking.body: The price you plan to sell at. It may not be lower than the buying price. At the counter you can still change it, and only the owner or manager can sell at a loss.
asking.example: Bought for Rs. 45,000, selling price Rs. 52,000.

profit.title: Profit
profit.body: Selling price minus buying price. "Profit after expenses" also takes away rent, bills, salaries and other expenses of that time.
profit.example: Sold for Rs. 52,000, bought for Rs. 45,000 → profit Rs. 7,000.

pta.title: PTA status
pta.body: PTA approved: the phone is registered in Pakistan and any SIM works. Non-PTA: not registered, a SIM works only for a short time. JV / patched: the phone has been changed to get around PTA; risky to buy and sell.
pta.example: An iPhone from abroad without PTA tax is Non-PTA.

imei.title: IMEI
imei.body: A 15-digit number that only that one phone has. Dial *#06# on the phone or look on the box. The app uses it to find the phone's history and to warn about stolen phones.

idcheck.title: ID card check
idcheck.body: When you buy a used phone from a customer, keep a photo of his CNIC and his face. If the phone turns out to be stolen, you can show who sold it to you. You may skip it for a person you know.
idcheck.example: Front and back of the CNIC, the seller's photo and a photo of the phone.

opening.title: Old stock
opening.body: Phones that were already in the shop before you started the app. Add them once so the stock is complete. No money is paid now, so the day's hisaab does not change.
opening.example: On the first day you add the 25 phones already on the shelf.

cut.title: Shop's cut on a return
cut.body: When a customer brings a phone back, the shop may keep part of the money and hand back the rest. What the shop keeps counts as income.
cut.example: Sold for Rs. 100,000, gives back Rs. 90,000 → the shop's cut is Rs. 10,000.

inHand.title: Left in hand
inHand.body: All money that came in minus all money that went out in that time (sales, payments, expenses, stock bought, refunds). Money spent on stock is now phones in the shop, so it is not a loss.
inHand.example: Came in Rs. 800,000, went out Rs. 750,000 → Rs. 50,000 left in hand.

warranty.title: Warranty
warranty.body: How long the shop will repair or replace the item if it has a fault. It is printed on the receipt.
warranty.example: 1 month warranty: any fault within a month is the shop's responsibility.

tid.title: TID
tid.body: Transaction ID: the number in the bank app or SMS after an online payment. Writing it helps you find the payment if there is a question later.

cheque.title: Cheque
cheque.body: Payment by a bank cheque. The money reaches the account only when the cheque clears, so the app keeps cheques in their own "Cheques" account.

remittance.title: Money from abroad
remittance.body: The buyer's family sends the money from another country (Western Union, bank and so on). Write how much came in their currency and the rate; the app works out the rupees.

void.title: Cancel a bill
void.body: Cancels a bill made by mistake. Nothing is deleted: the app adds an opposite entry, so the history and the hisaab stay correct.
void.example: A sale entered twice: cancel one of them.

audit.title: Shop audit
audit.body: One place to read the whole business for any period: what was sold and bought, the real profit, where the money came from and went, who owes whom, and the phones in stock. Balances show the start and the end of the period (or a chosen day); every tile opens the list behind the number.
audit.example: Pick "Last month": sales 1,250,000, profit 180,000, cash & bank 300,000 at the start and 410,000 at the end, people owe 95,000.

netSales.title: Net sales
netSales.body: All sales of the period after discounts and customer returns. The % beside it compares with the same number of days just before.
netSales.example: Sold 3 phones for Rs. 1,20,000, gave Rs. 2,000 discount, one Samsung A15 came back for Rs. 38,000 → net sales Rs. 80,000.

realProfit.title: Real profit (after expenses)
realProfit.body: Net sales minus the buying price of what was sold, minus expenses (rent, bills, salaries), plus repair and other income. Money the owner took home is not an expense. Red means a loss.
realProfit.example: Net sales Rs. 5,00,000, buying price Rs. 4,20,000, expenses Rs. 45,000, repair income Rs. 10,000 → real profit Rs. 45,000.

attention.title: Needs a look now
attention.body: Things to deal with today, counted as of now (not for the chosen period): ID checks not cleared, stock alerts, late installments and len-den return dates. Tap a chip to open the list.
attention.example: Chips show "ID checks not cleared 2" and "Late installments 1 · Rs. 8,000" → check those 2 phones and call that one customer.

idChecks.title: ID checks not cleared
idChecks.body: Phones in stock whose seller's ID check is still pending or was flagged as suspicious. Flagged ones are shown in red.
idChecks.example: You bought a used iPhone 13 and did not finish the CNIC check → it counts here as 1 until you clear it.

lateInstallments.title: Late installments
lateInstallments.body: Installment plans where at least one monthly payment is past its date, and the total of those late payments.
lateInstallments.example: Ali's Infinix Hot 40 plan: Rs. 5,000 was due on the 5th and not paid; Bilal is late Rs. 3,000 → 2 plans, Rs. 8,000.

lendingLate.title: Len-den late
lendingLate.body: People you lent money to (no bill) whose promised return date has passed, and how much they still owe.
lendingLate.example: Gave Rs. 20,000 to Usman, he promised to return it by the 10th; today is the 15th → late 1 · Rs. 20,000.

lendingWeOwe.title: Len-den to give back
lendingWeOwe.body: Money the shop borrowed (no bill) that must be returned within 3 days or is already late.
lendingWeOwe.example: Borrowed Rs. 50,000 from a Hall Road dealer, to return on the 12th; today is the 10th → 1 · Rs. 50,000.

dueToday.title: Installments due today
dueToday.body: Installment plans whose next monthly payment falls today (and none is late yet).
dueToday.example: Sana's Samsung A15 plan has Rs. 4,000 due today → 1. Remind her before closing.

dead_stock.title: Dead stock
dead_stock.body: Phones lying in stock longer than your last age band (90 days unless you changed the thresholds). Money is stuck in them.
dead_stock.example: An Oppo A57 came in 120 days ago and is still unsold → it is dead stock; think of a lower price.

high_value_slow.title: High value, slow
high_value_slow.body: An expensive phone (cost at or above your high-value limit, Rs. 50,000 by default) that has stayed longer than the "normal" band (30 days by default).
high_value_slow.example: iPhone 13 bought for Rs. 1,40,000, 45 days in stock → shown here, because a lot of money is waiting.

low_margin.title: Thin margin
low_margin.body: The asking price is so close to the buying price that the expected profit is under your thin-margin limit (5% by default).
low_margin.example: Bought a Vivo Y20 for Rs. 30,000, asking Rs. 31,000 → margin about 3% → shown here.

missing_cost.title: No cost
missing_cost.body: A phone in stock with no buying price saved, so its profit cannot be worked out.
missing_cost.example: Old stock Redmi Note 12 added without a buying price → profit on it would show wrong; add the cost.

missing_asking.title: No asking price
missing_asking.body: A phone in stock with no selling (asking) price set, so staff do not know what to ask.
missing_asking.example: A Tecno Spark 20 was bought but no asking price was written → set e.g. Rs. 32,000.

verification_pending.title: ID check pending
verification_pending.body: A used phone in stock whose seller's ID check was not finished yet.
verification_pending.example: Bought a used Samsung A32 from a walk-in seller, CNIC photo not saved → 1 pending.

verification_flagged.title: ID check flagged
verification_flagged.body: A phone whose ID check was marked as suspicious (for example the IMEI or the seller looked wrong). Do not sell it until cleared.
verification_flagged.example: IMEI on the box did not match the phone, staff flagged it → 1 flagged; check before selling.

repeat_returns.title: Came back more than once
repeat_returns.body: A phone in stock that customers have returned two or more times. It may have a hidden fault.
repeat_returns.example: The same Infinix Note 30 was sold and returned twice → shown here; test it properly.

inPeriod.title: In this period
inPeriod.body: What happened during the chosen days only: stock bought, expenses, money in and money out. "Before" is the same number of days just before.
inPeriod.example: Period "This month" (1–30 Nov): money in Rs. 9,00,000; Before (1–31 Oct) Rs. 7,50,000.

purchases.title: Stock bought
purchases.body: Total of the purchase bills in the period, minus what you returned to suppliers. Below it: how many bills and phones.
purchases.example: Bought 10 phones for Rs. 4,00,000 on 3 bills, returned one for Rs. 35,000 → Rs. 3,65,000.

expenses.title: Expenses
expenses.body: Rent, electricity, salaries, tea and other shop expenses of the period. What the owner took home is not counted here.
expenses.example: Rent Rs. 40,000 + bill Rs. 12,000 + tea Rs. 3,000 = Rs. 55,000; owner took Rs. 30,000 home (not included).

moneyIn.title: Money in
moneyIn.body: All money that came into the galla, bank and wallets in the period: sales paid now, udhaar received, repairs and so on. Money moved between your own accounts is not counted.
moneyIn.example: Counter sales Rs. 3,00,000 + udhaar received Rs. 50,000 + repairs Rs. 10,000 → Rs. 3,60,000.

moneyOut.title: Money out
moneyOut.body: All money that left the galla, bank and wallets in the period: stock paid for, payments to dealers, expenses, refunds. Moves between your own accounts are not counted.
moneyOut.example: Stock paid Rs. 2,50,000 + dealer payment Rs. 40,000 + expenses Rs. 55,000 → Rs. 3,45,000.

transfers.title: Moved between own accounts
transfers.body: Money you moved from one of your accounts to another (galla to bank, bank to Easypaisa). It is not income or expense, so it is kept out of money in / out.
transfers.example: Deposited Rs. 1,00,000 from the galla into the bank → shown here as Rs. 1,00,000, not as money in or out.

balances.title: Balances
balances.body: What you had at the start of the period (Start), at its end (End) and today (Now). If you pick an "As of" day, the big number is that day's balance.
balances.example: Cash & bank: Start Rs. 2,00,000, End Rs. 2,80,000, Now Rs. 3,10,000 → Rs. 80,000 more in the period.

cashBank.title: Cash & bank
cashBank.body: Money in the galla, bank accounts and wallets (Easypaisa, JazzCash) together. Below: each account's own balance.
cashBank.example: Galla Rs. 60,000 + Meezan Bank Rs. 1,80,000 + Easypaisa Rs. 40,000 → Rs. 2,80,000.

stock.title: Phones in stock
stock.body: How many phones, tablets and watches were in stock, and what they are worth at buying price (owner / manager only) and at asking price. Accessories are not in this count.
stock.example: 25 phones in stock: bought for Rs. 9,00,000, asking Rs. 10,20,000 → about Rs. 1,20,000 profit waiting.

receivable.title: People owe us
receivable.body: The total udhaar customers and others still have to pay the shop, from their khatas (len-den included). Below: what was received in the period and how many people owe.
receivable.example: Ali owes Rs. 30,000, Bilal Rs. 15,000, Kamran Rs. 5,000 → Rs. 50,000 from 3 people.

payable.title: We owe people
payable.body: The total the shop still has to pay dealers, suppliers and others, from their khatas (len-den included). Below: what was paid in the period and to how many people.
payable.example: Hall Road dealer Rs. 1,20,000 and a supplier Rs. 30,000 still unpaid → Rs. 1,50,000 to 2 people.

moneyByKind.title: Money by account type
moneyByKind.body: The circle splits your cash & bank balance at the end of the period (or the chosen day) by type: cash, bank, Easypaisa, JazzCash and so on.
moneyByKind.example: Cash Rs. 60,000, bank Rs. 1,80,000, Easypaisa Rs. 40,000 → bank is the biggest part of the circle.

checks.title: The books check out
checks.body: The app checks its own sums: cash start + in − out = end, every entry balances, each khata matches the ledger, stock start + in − out = end, payments are not more than bills. Green ticks mean all is right; a red cross means tell support.
checks.example: Cash: start Rs. 2,00,000 + in Rs. 3,60,000 − out Rs. 2,80,000 = end Rs. 2,80,000 → green tick.

limitations.title: Not shown, and why
limitations.body: Some things are not entered in the app, so the audit cannot show them: due dates on most bills (so debt age counts from the bill date), tax on purchases, and remittance fees.
limitations.example: A bill from 1 Oct with no promise date is shown as "30 days old" on 31 Oct, not as "overdue".

pnl.title: Profit & loss
pnl.body: How the period's sales turn into real profit, line by line: sales, discounts, returns, buying price, expenses, other income. The number in brackets is the period before.
pnl.example: Net sales Rs. 5,00,000 (4,50,000) → this period sold Rs. 50,000 more than the period before.

cash.title: Cash & bank
cash.body: Where money came from and where it went in the period, for the galla, each bank and each wallet, from start to end.

expenses.title: Expenses
expenses.body: The shop's expenses of the period by category, the biggest ones, and who spent from which account. What the owner took home is shown apart.
expenses.example: Rent Rs. 40,000, salaries Rs. 60,000, bills Rs. 12,000 → expenses Rs. 1,12,000.

tax.title: Tax
tax.body: Sales tax charged on the period's sale bills, for a shop registered with FBR. It belongs to the government, not to the shop.
tax.example: 2 bills with 18% tax: Rs. 1,00,000 + Rs. 18,000 tax → tax collected Rs. 18,000.

series.title: Profit by day / week / month
series.body: Each bar is the real profit of one day (or week, or month for long periods). Staff who cannot see costs see net sales instead.
series.example: Bars for 1, 2, 3 Nov: Rs. 8,000, Rs. 12,000, Rs. 3,000 → the 2nd was the best day.

salesVsProfit.title: Net sales vs real profit
salesVsProfit.body: Two lines over the period: what you sold (green) and what you really earned after costs and expenses (dark). A wide gap is normal; a falling dark line needs a look.
salesVsProfit.example: Week 1: sales Rs. 1,50,000, profit Rs. 15,000; week 2: sales Rs. 1,60,000, profit Rs. 5,000 → sold more but earned less.

grossSales.title: Sales before discounts
grossSales.body: What the sale bills came to before any discount and before customer returns.
grossSales.example: Sold an iPhone 13 at Rs. 1,60,000 and a Samsung A15 at Rs. 40,000 → Rs. 2,00,000.

discounts.title: Discounts given
discounts.body: Money taken off the price on sale bills in the period. It lowers sales and profit.
discounts.example: Asking Rs. 42,000 for a Samsung A15, sold for Rs. 40,000 → Rs. 2,000 discount.

salesReturns.title: Returned by customers
salesReturns.body: The value of items customers brought back in the period. It is taken off sales; the phone goes back into stock.
salesReturns.example: A customer returned an Infinix Hot 40 sold for Rs. 35,000 → Rs. 35,000 here.

cogs.title: Buying price of what was sold
cogs.body: What the shop had paid for the items it sold in the period (returns give that cost back). Only owner and manager see it.
cogs.example: Sold a Samsung A15 for Rs. 40,000 that you bought for Rs. 34,000 → Rs. 34,000 here.

grossProfit.title: Profit on sales
grossProfit.body: Net sales minus the buying price of what was sold, before rent and other expenses.
grossProfit.example: Net sales Rs. 5,00,000 − buying price Rs. 4,20,000 → Rs. 80,000.

opExpenses.title: Expenses
opExpenses.body: The shop's running expenses of the period (rent, bills, salaries, tea). Owner's drawings are not included.
opExpenses.example: Rent Rs. 40,000 + electricity Rs. 12,000 + salary Rs. 25,000 → Rs. 77,000.

operatingProfit.title: Profit after expenses
operatingProfit.body: Profit on sales minus expenses, before repair and other income is added.
operatingProfit.example: Profit on sales Rs. 80,000 − expenses Rs. 77,000 → Rs. 3,000.

otherIncome.title: Repair & other income
otherIncome.body: Money earned apart from selling: repair jobs and other income such as the part the shop keeps when a customer returns a phone.
otherIncome.example: Repairs Rs. 8,000 + kept Rs. 2,000 on a return → Rs. 10,000.

taxCollected.title: Tax collected
taxCollected.body: Sales tax charged on the period's sale bills. It is the government's money, so it is not in sales or profit.
taxCollected.example: Bill Rs. 1,18,000 with 18% tax → Rs. 18,000 tax, sales Rs. 1,00,000.

ownerTook.title: Owner took out
ownerTook.body: Money the owner took from the shop for himself. It lowers the cash but it is not a shop expense, so profit stays the same.
ownerTook.example: Owner took Rs. 30,000 for home → cash is Rs. 30,000 less, profit unchanged.

cashOpening.title: Start
cashOpening.body: Money in all your accounts (galla, banks, wallets) together at the start of the first day of the period.
cashOpening.example: On 1 Nov morning: galla Rs. 50,000 + bank Rs. 1,50,000 → start Rs. 2,00,000.

cashIn.title: Money in
cashIn.body: Everything that came into your accounts in the period, by reason. On this tab it also includes money moved in from your own other account.
cashIn.example: Sales Rs. 3,00,000 + udhaar received Rs. 50,000 + Rs. 20,000 moved from galla to bank → Rs. 3,70,000.

cashOut.title: Money out
cashOut.body: Everything that left your accounts in the period, by reason. On this tab it also includes money moved out to your own other account.
cashOut.example: Stock Rs. 2,00,000 + expenses Rs. 60,000 + Rs. 20,000 moved from galla to bank → Rs. 2,80,000.

cashClosing.title: End
cashClosing.body: Money in all your accounts at the end of the period (or of the chosen day). "Now" below is today's balance.

cameIn.title: Where money came from
cameIn.body: Money in split by reason. The bar shows each reason's share of the total.
cameIn.example: Sales Rs. 3,00,000 and udhaar received Rs. 50,000 of Rs. 3,50,000 → sales is the long bar.

wentOut.title: Where money went
wentOut.body: Money out split by reason. The bar shows each reason's share of the total.
wentOut.example: Stock Rs. 2,00,000, expenses Rs. 60,000, refunds Rs. 20,000 of Rs. 2,80,000 → stock is the long bar.

sales_now.title: Sales paid at the counter
sales_now.body: Money paid on the sale bill itself (cash, bank, wallet), including the cash part of an exchange. Udhaar paid later is not here.
sales_now.example: Sold a phone for Rs. 50,000, customer paid Rs. 30,000 now → Rs. 30,000 here, Rs. 20,000 goes to udhaar.

udhaar_received.title: Udhaar received
udhaar_received.body: Payments people made later against their khata (old bills).
udhaar_received.example: Ali paid Rs. 20,000 of his old udhaar on Easypaisa → Rs. 20,000 here.

borrowed.title: Len-den taken
borrowed.body: Money the shop borrowed from someone with no bill.
borrowed.example: Took Rs. 50,000 from a friend's shop to buy stock → Rs. 50,000 here.

repairs.title: Repairs
repairs.body: Money received for repair jobs: advances and final bills.
repairs.example: Screen change: Rs. 1,000 advance + Rs. 3,500 on delivery → Rs. 4,500.

refund_from_supplier.title: Refunds from suppliers
refund_from_supplier.body: Money suppliers paid back when you returned stock to them.
refund_from_supplier.example: Returned a faulty Vivo Y20 to the dealer, he paid back Rs. 30,000 → Rs. 30,000 here.

transfer_in.title: Moved in from own account
transfer_in.body: Money that came from another of your own accounts. Not income.
transfer_in.example: Moved Rs. 1,00,000 from galla to bank → the bank shows Rs. 1,00,000 here.

opening.title: Opening
opening.body: The starting balance typed in when an account was set up in the app.
opening.example: Started the app with Rs. 25,000 in the galla → Rs. 25,000 opening.

other_in.title: Other in
other_in.body: Money in that fits none of the reasons above.
other_in.example: An entry of Rs. 500 with no bill type → shown as other in.

stock_now.title: Stock paid at purchase
stock_now.body: Money paid on the purchase bill itself when you bought stock. What you owe for later is not here.
stock_now.example: Bought 5 phones for Rs. 2,00,000, paid Rs. 1,50,000 now → Rs. 1,50,000 here, Rs. 50,000 owed.

paid_to_people.title: Paid to people (udhaar)
paid_to_people.body: Payments you made later to dealers and others against their khata.
paid_to_people.example: Paid the Hall Road dealer Rs. 40,000 of the old balance → Rs. 40,000 here.

lent.title: Len-den given
lent.body: Money the shop lent to someone with no bill.
lent.example: Gave Rs. 10,000 to a neighbour shopkeeper → Rs. 10,000 here.

expenses.title: Expenses
expenses.body: Expenses paid from this money: rent, bills, salaries, and what the owner took out.
expenses.example: Rent Rs. 40,000 paid from the bank → Rs. 40,000 here.

refunds.title: Refunds to customers
refunds.body: Money paid back to customers on returns and exchanges.
refunds.example: Customer returned a Samsung A15, you gave back Rs. 36,000 → Rs. 36,000 here.

repair_parts.title: Repair parts
repair_parts.body: Money spent on parts or outside work for repair jobs.
repair_parts.example: Bought a screen for Rs. 2,500 for a customer's repair → Rs. 2,500 here.

fees.title: Software fee
fees.body: The fee paid for this app.
fees.example: Paid the monthly app fee of Rs. 2,000 → Rs. 2,000 here.

transfer_out.title: Moved to own account
transfer_out.body: Money sent to another of your own accounts. Not an expense.
transfer_out.example: Moved Rs. 1,00,000 from galla to bank → the galla shows Rs. 1,00,000 here.

other_out.title: Other out
other_out.body: Money out that fits none of the reasons above.
other_out.example: An entry of Rs. 300 with no bill type → shown as other out.

reversal.title: Reversal
reversal.body: A cancelled entry: when a bill or payment is cancelled, the app adds an opposite entry. It shows under the reason it undoes.
reversal.example: A Rs. 5,000 expense was entered by mistake and cancelled → "Reversal: Expenses Rs. 5,000" under money in.

perAccount.title: Each account
perAccount.body: Every account on its own: start + in − out = end, the part moved between your own accounts, and the reasons as small chips.

channels.title: By channel (account type)
channels.body: Money in and out grouped by the type of account it landed in: cash, bank, Easypaisa, JazzCash, cheque, from abroad. Own transfers are left out.

channelsIn.title: Money in by channel
channelsIn.body: The circle shows how customers paid in the period: how much came as cash, bank, Easypaisa and so on. Tap it to open the accounts.
channelsIn.example: In Rs. 4,00,000: cash Rs. 2,50,000, bank Rs. 70,000, Easypaisa Rs. 80,000 → most still pay cash.

paymentsByMethod.title: Khata payments by method
paymentsByMethod.body: Only stand-alone payments (udhaar received or paid, len-den) by the method written on them, with how many payments.
paymentsByMethod.example: Easypaisa +30,000 / −0 (4) → 4 customers paid Rs. 30,000 of udhaar on Easypaisa.

international.title: From abroad (remittances)
international.body: Payments sent from another country (Western Union, bank and so on): the foreign amount, the rate and the rupees, per currency and per payment.
international.example: Customer's brother sent 200 SAR at 74 → Rs. 14,800 counted for the bill.

expTotal.title: Expenses
expTotal.body: All shop expenses of the period, with how many entries and the period before. What the owner took out is shown apart and not in this total.

expSeries.title: Expenses by day / week / month
expSeries.body: Each bar is the expenses of one day (or week or month for long periods).
expSeries.example: 1st of the month: rent Rs. 40,000 → tall bar; other days Rs. 1,000–3,000.

expCats.title: Expenses by category
expCats.body: Each category with its total, how many entries, a bar for its share and the period before. Tap to open the expenses.
expCats.example: Salaries (2) Rs. 60,000 of Rs. 1,12,000 → about half the bar; before Rs. 55,000.

largest.title: Largest expenses
largest.body: The biggest single expense entries of the period, with date, who entered it and from which account.
largest.example: Rent Rs. 40,000 on 1 Nov by the owner from Meezan Bank → at the top.

expByWho.title: Who spent, from where
expByWho.body: Expenses by the person who entered them and by the account they were paid from.
expByWho.example: Owner Rs. 80,000 (3), Ahmed Rs. 32,000 (9); galla Rs. 32,000, bank Rs. 80,000.

taxedBills.title: Taxed bills
taxedBills.body: How many sale bills of the period had tax on them, out of all sale bills.

taxable.title: Taxable sales
taxable.body: The total of the taxed bills without the tax.
taxable.example: 6 taxed bills total Rs. 3,54,000 with Rs. 54,000 tax → taxable Rs. 3,00,000.

taxOnBills.title: Tax collected
taxOnBills.body: The tax written on the period's sale bills, before any returns.
taxOnBills.example: 6 bills with 18% tax on Rs. 3,00,000 → Rs. 54,000.

taxNet.title: Tax net of returns
taxNet.body: Tax collected minus the tax given back on returns. This is what you owe the government for the period.
taxNet.example: Collected Rs. 54,000, one taxed phone came back with Rs. 9,000 tax → Rs. 45,000.

taxRows.title: Taxed bills list
taxRows.body: Every taxed sale bill: customer, date, amount before tax, the rate, whether the price included the tax (incl.) or tax was added (excl.), and the tax.
taxRows.example: Bill S-120 · 1,00,000 @ 18% excl. → tax Rs. 18,000, customer paid Rs. 1,18,000.

sales.title: Sales
sales.body: Every sale bill of the period: how much was billed, how it was paid (at the counter or on credit), by which employee and to which customer.
sales.example: 40 bills, Rs. 12,00,000: Rs. 9,00,000 paid at the counter, Rs. 3,00,000 on credit.

purchases.title: Purchases
purchases.body: Every purchase bill of the period: how much stock was bought, how much was paid at once, what is still owed and to which supplier.
purchases.example: 8 bills, 20 phones, Rs. 8,00,000: paid Rs. 6,00,000, owe Rs. 2,00,000.

paid.title: Fully paid
paid.body: Bills with nothing left to pay today. Tap the card to list only these bills; tap again to clear.
paid.example: Bill Rs. 45,000, paid Rs. 45,000 → fully paid.

partial.title: Part paid
partial.body: Bills where some money was paid and some is still due today. "due" is what is left.
partial.example: Bill Rs. 60,000, paid Rs. 40,000 → part paid, due Rs. 20,000.

unpaid.title: Not paid
unpaid.body: Bills where nothing has been paid yet; the whole amount is udhaar.
unpaid.example: Bill Rs. 35,000 for an Infinix Hot 40, nothing paid → not paid, due Rs. 35,000.

returned.title: Returned
returned.body: Sale bills whose items were all brought back by the customer.
returned.example: Sold a Samsung A15, customer returned it the next day → the bill is returned.

userFilter.title: Filter by employee
userFilter.body: Tap a name to see only that employee's bills and figures; "All" shows everyone again.
userFilter.example: Tap "Ahmed" → only Ahmed's 12 bills of Rs. 3,50,000 are shown.

billed.title: Billed
billed.body: The total of the period's sale bills as written on them (after discount, tax included). Below: bills, items sold and the profit on them. The % compares with the period before.

atCounter.title: Paid at the counter
atCounter.body: Money paid on the bills at the time of sale (cash, bank, wallet). Below: how many bills were paid in full at the counter.
atCounter.example: Bill Rs. 50,000, customer paid Rs. 30,000 on the spot → Rs. 30,000 counts here.

onCredit.title: On credit
onCredit.body: The part of the bills that was not paid at the time of sale (udhaar). "due" is what is still unpaid today, after later payments.
onCredit.example: On credit Rs. 3,00,000 on 10 bills; customers have since paid Rs. 1,00,000 → due Rs. 2,00,000.

discounts.title: Discounts
discounts.body: Total discount given on the period's sale bills.
discounts.example: Rs. 1,000 off one bill and Rs. 2,500 off another → Rs. 3,500.

returned.title: Returned by customers
returned.body: The value returned on the period's sale bills.
returned.example: One phone from a bill of this month came back for Rs. 38,000 → Rs. 38,000.

avgBill.title: Average bill
avgBill.body: Billed amount divided by the number of bills.
avgBill.example: Rs. 12,00,000 on 40 bills → average bill Rs. 30,000.

salesSeries.title: Sales by day / week / month
salesSeries.body: Each bar is the amount billed in one day (or week or month). Tap a bar to see how much of it was on credit.
salesSeries.example: Saturday bar Rs. 2,00,000, on credit Rs. 50,000 → a busy day with some udhaar.

byUser.title: By employee
byUser.body: Each employee's bills in the period: how many, the total, and on sales also discounts, credit, returns and profit. Tap a sales row to filter by that person.
byUser.example: Ahmed: 12 bills, Rs. 3,50,000, discounts Rs. 4,000, on credit Rs. 60,000.

byCustomer.title: By customer
byCustomer.body: Who bought the most in the period: bills, total and what each still owes on those bills. "Walk-in" is sales with no customer name.
byCustomer.example: Ali Traders: 5 bills, Rs. 2,40,000, due Rs. 40,000.

bills.title: Bills
bills.body: Every bill of the period that matches the filters above (status card, employee, search). Tap a bill to open it. Paid and due are today's figures.
bills.example: Tap "Not paid" and search "Ali" → only Ali's unpaid bills show, e.g. S-118 due Rs. 35,000.

bought.title: Bought
bought.body: The total of the period's purchase bills, with how many bills, phones and other items. The % compares with the period before.
bought.example: 8 bills, 20 phones, 50 covers → Rs. 8,00,000; +12% on last month.

paidNow.title: Paid at purchase
paidNow.body: Money paid to suppliers on the purchase bills at the time of buying.
paidNow.example: Bought stock for Rs. 2,00,000 and paid Rs. 1,50,000 on the spot → Rs. 1,50,000 here.

purchaseCredit.title: On credit (purchases)
purchaseCredit.body: The part of the purchase bills not paid at the time of buying. "still owed" is what the shop has to pay today, after later payments.
purchaseCredit.example: Rs. 50,000 left on credit with a dealer, Rs. 20,000 paid since → still owed Rs. 30,000.

returnedToSupplier.title: Returned to suppliers
returnedToSupplier.body: How many returns you made to suppliers in the period and their value.
returnedToSupplier.example: Sent back 2 faulty phones worth Rs. 60,000 → 2 · Rs. 60,000.

purchaseSeries.title: Purchases by day / week / month
purchaseSeries.body: Each bar is the amount bought in one day (or week or month). Tap a bar to see how many phones.
purchaseSeries.example: Monday bar Rs. 3,00,000 · 8 phones → the big buying day.

bySupplier.title: By supplier
bySupplier.body: Who you bought from in the period: bills, phones, total and what you still owe them on those bills.
bySupplier.example: Hall Road dealer: 4 bills, 12 phones, Rs. 5,00,000, still owed Rs. 1,00,000.

udhaar_given.title: Udhaar given on sales
udhaar_given.body: The unpaid part of the period's sale bills that went onto customers' khatas.
udhaar_given.example: Sold for Rs. 50,000, got Rs. 30,000 → Rs. 20,000 udhaar given.

received.title: Received from people
received.body: Payments people made into their khata in the period.
received.example: Three customers paid Rs. 10,000 each → Rs. 30,000.

sale_returns.title: Returns credited
sale_returns.body: Returns that lowered what a customer owes (the item came back instead of money).
sale_returns.example: Customer owed Rs. 40,000, returned the phone → Rs. 40,000 credited, he owes nothing.

udhaar_taken.title: Udhaar taken on purchases
udhaar_taken.body: The unpaid part of the period's purchase bills that the shop owes suppliers.
udhaar_taken.example: Bought for Rs. 1,00,000, paid Rs. 70,000 → Rs. 30,000 udhaar taken.

paid.title: Paid to people
paid.body: Payments the shop made into suppliers' and others' khatas in the period.
paid.example: Paid the dealer Rs. 25,000 of the old balance → Rs. 25,000.

purchase_returns.title: Returns to suppliers
purchase_returns.body: Stock returned to suppliers that lowered what the shop owes them.
purchase_returns.example: Owed the dealer Rs. 60,000, returned a phone worth Rs. 30,000 → now owe Rs. 30,000.

lent.title: Len-den given
lent.body: Money lent to people with no bill in the period. It goes onto their khata.

borrowed.title: Len-den taken
borrowed.body: Money borrowed from people with no bill in the period. The shop owes it back.
borrowed.example: Borrowed Rs. 50,000 from a dealer → Rs. 50,000.

repairs.title: Repair bills
repairs.body: Repair charges left unpaid on a customer's khata in the period.
repairs.example: Repair bill Rs. 4,000, customer paid Rs. 1,000 → Rs. 3,000.

other.title: Other / opening
other.body: Other khata changes, mainly opening balances typed when a person was added.
other.example: Added an old customer with Rs. 12,000 already owed → Rs. 12,000.

ofLending.title: Of which len-den
ofLending.body: The part of the udhaar above that is len-den (money given or taken with no bill). It is inside the totals, not extra. Tap to open len-den.
ofLending.example: People owe us Rs. 1,00,000, of which len-den Rs. 20,000 → Rs. 80,000 is from bills.

movement.title: Udhaar in this period
movement.body: How the khatas moved in the period: udhaar given and received, returns, len-den, repairs and opening balances.
movement.example: Given Rs. 2,00,000, received Rs. 1,50,000 → people owe Rs. 50,000 more than at the start.

overdue.title: Overdue
overdue.body: Only bills with a promise (due) date can be late. Bars show how many days past the date, and how much. "Not yet due" and "No promise date" are shown apart.
overdue.example: Bill due on 1 Nov, today 20 Nov, Rs. 25,000 unpaid → in the 8-30 days bar.

age.title: Age of the debt
age.body: How old each person's udhaar is, counted from their oldest unpaid bill: 0-7, 8-30, 31-60, 61+ days. Old udhaar is harder to collect.
age.example: Bilal's oldest unpaid bill is from 70 days ago, Rs. 15,000 → in the 61+ bar.

owesUs.title: People who owe us
owesUs.body: Each person who owes the shop, biggest first: days since the oldest bill (or late days), and when they last paid. Tap to open their khata.
owesUs.example: Ali · 45 days · last paid 2 Nov → Rs. 30,000.

weOwe.title: People we owe
weOwe.body: Each person the shop owes, biggest first, with the age of the oldest unpaid bill and the last payment.
weOwe.example: Hall Road dealer · 20 days · last paid 25 Oct → Rs. 1,20,000.

phones.title: Phones on unpaid bills
phones.body: Phones sold or bought on bills that are not fully paid, with the bill, its age and what is left on that bill. A bill with several phones shows the bill's remaining amount on each phone.
phones.example: iPhone 13 sold to Ali on S-110, 25 days ago, bill still has Rs. 40,000 → they owe 40,000.

plans.title: Installments
plans.body: The part of "people owe us" that is on installment plans. It is already inside the udhaar above, not extra.
plans.example: People owe Rs. 2,00,000, of which Rs. 80,000 on 4 installment plans.

plansOpen.title: Open plans
plansOpen.body: Installment plans that are still running.

plansLeft.title: Still to come
plansLeft.body: Money still to be paid on all open plans.
plansLeft.example: 4 plans with Rs. 20,000 each left → Rs. 80,000.

plansLate.title: Late plans
plansLate.body: Plans with at least one monthly payment past its date.
plansLate.example: Ali missed the 5 Nov payment → 1 late plan.

plansLateAmount.title: Late amount
plansLateAmount.body: The total of the monthly payments that are past their date.
plansLateAmount.example: Two missed payments of Rs. 5,000 → Rs. 10,000.

what.title: Len-den
what.body: Money given to or taken from a person with no bill (hand loan). It sits in the person's one khata, so it is part of the udhaar, not extra.
what.example: Lent Usman Rs. 20,000 and he also owes Rs. 10,000 on a bill → his khata shows Rs. 30,000.

owedToShop.title: People owe us (len-den)
owedToShop.body: Len-den money people still have to return to the shop today (or on the chosen day), and how many people.
owedToShop.example: Usman Rs. 20,000 + Kashif Rs. 5,000 → Rs. 25,000 from 2 people.

shopOwes.title: We owe people (len-den)
shopOwes.body: Len-den money the shop still has to give back today (or on the chosen day), and to how many people.
shopOwes.example: Borrowed Rs. 50,000 from a dealer, returned Rs. 20,000 → Rs. 30,000 to 1 person.

lent.title: Given in the period
lent.body: Len-den money the shop gave in the period, with the number of entries and the period before.

borrowed.title: Taken in the period
borrowed.body: Len-den money the shop took in the period, with the number of entries and the period before.

adjusted.title: Adjusted against bills
adjusted.body: Len-den money that was later settled against the person's bills, so it is no longer open len-den. This counts all entries so far, not only this period.
adjusted.example: Lent Kashif Rs. 10,000, then sold him a phone and took the Rs. 10,000 off his bill → Rs. 10,000 adjusted.

voided.title: Cancelled entries
voided.body: How many len-den entries of the period were cancelled. Nothing is deleted; a cancelled entry stays in the history.
voided.example: An entry of Rs. 5,000 was typed twice and one was cancelled → 1.

series.title: Given and taken
series.body: Each bar is len-den given plus taken in one day (or week or month). Tap a bar to see each part.
series.example: 10 Nov bar Rs. 60,000: given Rs. 10,000 · taken Rs. 50,000.

byMethod.title: How it moved
byMethod.body: Len-den given and taken in the period by how the money moved: cash, bank, Easypaisa and so on.
byMethod.example: Cash: given Rs. 10,000 · taken 0; Easypaisa: given Rs. 25,000 · taken Rs. 50,000.

due.title: Return dates
due.body: Len-den with a return date, late first: Late, Today, In 3 days, Later. For money lent, remind the person; for money borrowed, the shop has to pay.
due.example: Usman · they owe · 10 Nov · 5 days late → Rs. 20,000; send a WhatsApp reminder.

people.title: Len-den by person
people.body: Each person's len-den: given and taken in the period, their whole khata, and on the right the len-den still open today (they owe / we owe / clear).
people.example: Usman: given 20,000 · taken 0 · khata 30,000 → they owe 20,000.

entries.title: Entries
entries.body: Every len-den entry of the period: number, date, who entered it and the note. Minus is money given, plus is money taken.

full.title: Complete shop audit report
full.body: One report for the chosen period: tick the sections you want, choose summary or detailed, then print / save as PDF or download Excel (one sheet per section). The numbers are the same as on the screens.
full.example: Tick Summary, Profit & loss and Udhaar for "Last month" → a 3-section PDF for your accountant.

summary.title: Executive summary
summary.body: The main figures on one page: net sales, profit, expenses, cash & bank, udhaar, stock, with what is not recorded.
summary.example: Net sales Rs. 12,00,000 · profit Rs. 1,10,000 · cash Rs. 2,90,000 · people owe Rs. 1,00,000.

insights.title: Business insights
insights.body: Short plain sentences the app reads from your figures, marked good, watch or info. Nothing is guessed.
insights.example: "Sales are 12% higher than last month" (good) · "5 phones older than 90 days" (watch).

sales.title: Sales
sales.body: Sale bills of the period: billed, at the counter, on credit, by employee, and in detail every bill.

purchases.title: Purchases
purchases.body: Purchase bills of the period: bought, paid at purchase, still owed, by supplier.
purchases.example: 8 bills, Rs. 8,00,000; Hall Road dealer Rs. 5,00,000, owed Rs. 1,00,000.

pnl.title: Profit & loss
pnl.body: Sales down to real profit, line by line, with the period before and a day / week / month series.
pnl.example: Net sales Rs. 5,00,000 − cost Rs. 4,20,000 − expenses Rs. 45,000 + other Rs. 10,000 = Rs. 45,000.

cash.title: Cash & bank
cash.body: Each account start, in, out and end, money in and out by reason, and payments from abroad.

expenses.title: Expenses
expenses.body: Expenses by category against the period before, and in detail the largest ones.

tax.title: Tax
tax.body: Taxed bills, taxable sales, tax collected and tax after returns; in detail each taxed bill.

customers.title: Top customers
customers.body: Customers ranked by sales and by profit, and the largest amounts owed to the shop.

suppliers.title: Top suppliers
suppliers.body: Owner / manager only: suppliers ranked by what you bought from them and by the profit made on their phones, plus the largest amounts the shop owes.
suppliers.example: 1. Hall Road dealer Rs. 5,00,000 bought; profit on his phones Rs. 45,000.

udhaar.title: Udhaar
udhaar.body: People owe us and we owe people: start, end, movement in the period, age of the debt and the people.
udhaar.example: People owe Rs. 1,00,000 at the end; Bilal Rs. 15,000 for 70 days.

lending.title: Len-den
lending.body: Money given and taken with no bill: open amounts, the period's entries, people and return dates.
lending.example: Given Rs. 35,000, taken Rs. 50,000; Usman owes Rs. 20,000, 5 days late.

inventory.title: Inventory valuation
inventory.body: Phones in stock on the as-of day, their value at cost and at asking, expected margin, and counts by condition, PTA and ID check.
inventory.example: 25 phones, cost Rs. 9,00,000, asking Rs. 10,20,000, margin Rs. 1,20,000.

ageing.title: Stock ageing
ageing.body: How long phones have been in stock (fresh, normal, slow, attention, dead) and the stock alerts.

products.title: Product performance
products.body: Each model: units sold, share, average price, days to sell, returns, in stock, and top / average / low.
products.example: Samsung A15: 12 sold, 25% of units, avg Rs. 40,000, 8 days → top.

invoices.title: Invoice statistics
invoices.body: How many documents of each kind (sale, purchase, payments, returns), their amount, how many were voided, and by employee.

verification.title: ID checks
verification.body: ID checks saved in the period and the skipped checks ("I know this person"), with who skipped and why.
verification.example: 18 checks saved; Ahmed skipped 3 of his 10 intakes → unusual.

checks.title: Reconciliation checks
checks.body: The app's own sum checks (cash, entries, khatas, stock, payments) with left side, right side and any difference.

staff.title: Employee activity
staff.body: What each employee sold, bought, received and spent in the period.
staff.example: Ahmed: 12 sale bills Rs. 3,50,000, received Rs. 40,000, spent Rs. 3,000.

security.title: Security & fraud
security.body: Owner only: voids, sales under asking or cost, price changes, stock adjustments, skipped checks, wrong PINs, by employee.
security.example: 2 sales under cost by Ahmed, 1 void → worth a look.

repairs.title: Repairs & labs
repairs.body: Phones taken in and given back, repair income, parts, lab charges, profit, and every lab's record.
repairs.example: This month: 40 in, 36 back, profit Rs. 70,000; Zain Lab 90% fixed.

mode.title: Summary or detailed
mode.body: Summary gives the totals and the top 10 rows of each list. Detailed adds the lists in full (up to 100 rows each), such as every bill.
mode.example: Sales in Summary: totals and top 10 customers; in Detailed: also all 40 bills.

individual.title: Individual reports
individual.body: Single reports to download as PDF, Excel or CSV. Those marked "for the chosen period" follow the period above; khata, people and stock lists are as of today.
individual.example: Download "Expenses" for last month as Excel, or "Stock list" for what is in the shop today.

summary.title: Stock tab
summary.body: Everything in stock right now (or on the day you picked under "As of"): how many phones, tablets and watches, what they cost, what you ask for them, and how they split by condition, PTA, ID check, type, brand and supplier. Accessories are not counted here.
summary.example: 42 phones in stock, bought for Rs. 9,50,000, asking Rs. 10,60,000 → you expect about Rs. 1,10,000 profit when all are sold.

ageing.title: Age of stock tab
ageing.body: How many days each phone in stock has been sitting in the shop, grouped into your own age bands, with the phones that need a look today. Always "now", not the chosen period.
ageing.example: Samsung A15 came in on 1 September, today is 15 October → 44 days → band "Slow" (31–60 days).

idChecks.title: ID checks tab
idChecks.body: The ID / stolen-phone checks of your phones: how many in stock are checked, pending or flagged, how many checks were saved in the period, and every check that was skipped with "I know this person" — by whom and why.
idChecks.example: This month: 18 checks saved, 2 phones still pending, 1 check skipped by Bilal with the reason "regular customer".

inStock.title: In stock
inStock.body: How many phones, tablets and watches are in the shop now (or on the chosen day). The small line tells how many of them still have no asking price.
inStock.example: 42 phones in the shop, 3 of them with no price written yet → "42 · 3 without asking price".

atCost.title: At cost
atCost.body: What the phones in stock cost you: the purchase price of each one, added up. Only the owner and the manager see it.
atCost.example: Samsung A15 Rs. 38,000 + iPhone 13 Rs. 1,45,000 + Infinix Hot 40 Rs. 30,000 → at cost Rs. 2,13,000.

atAsking.title: At asking
atAsking.body: What the phones in stock would bring if each one sold at its asking price, added up. A phone with no asking price adds nothing.
atAsking.example: Samsung A15 asking Rs. 42,000 + iPhone 13 Rs. 1,60,000 + Infinix Hot 40 Rs. 34,000 → at asking Rs. 2,36,000.

expectedMargin.title: Expected margin
expectedMargin.body: The profit you expect if the stock sells at the asking prices: asking price minus cost, for the phones that have both. The % is that profit out of the cost. Owner and manager only.
expectedMargin.example: At asking Rs. 2,36,000 − at cost Rs. 2,13,000 → expected margin Rs. 23,000, which is 10.8% of the cost.

byCondition.title: Stock by condition (chart)
byCondition.body: The phones in stock split by condition: box pack, open box, used, patched. Tap a slice to open those phones in Stock.
byCondition.example: 42 phones: Used 25, Box pack 12, Open box 4, Patched 1 → tap "Used" to see the 25 used phones.

byVerification.title: Stock by ID check (chart)
byVerification.body: The phones in stock split by their ID / stolen-phone check: checked, pending, flagged, or no check needed. Tap to open the stock list.
byVerification.example: 42 phones: ID checked 30, no check needed 6, pending 5, flagged 1 → the 1 flagged phone must not be sold.

condition.title: Condition card
condition.body: Each line is one condition: how many phones · their cost (owner and manager only) · their asking value. Tap a line to open those phones.
condition.example: "Used 25 · 9,50,000 · 10,60,000" → 25 used phones, bought for Rs. 9,50,000, asking Rs. 10,60,000 in total.

pta.title: PTA card
pta.body: The phones in stock by PTA status: approved, non-PTA, JV or unknown — count · cost · asking value. One phone shows up once here and once in every other card.
pta.example: "Non-PTA 8 · 2,40,000 · 2,72,000" → 8 non-PTA phones in stock worth Rs. 2,72,000 at asking.

verification.title: ID check card
verification.body: The phones in stock by ID check result — count · cost · asking value. Tap a line to open the stock list.
verification.example: "ID check pending 5 · 1,50,000 · 1,70,000" → 5 phones worth Rs. 1,70,000 still waiting for their check.

category.title: Type card
category.body: The stock by device type: phone, tablet or watch — count · cost · asking value.
category.example: "Tablet 3 · 1,20,000 · 1,38,000" → 3 tablets in stock, Rs. 1,38,000 at asking.

byBrand.title: By brand
byBrand.body: How many phones of each brand are in stock (the 12 biggest). Tap or hold a bar to see the asking value of that brand.
byBrand.example: Samsung 15, Infinix 10, Apple 6 → the Samsung bar is the tallest; its hint shows Rs. 6,00,000 at asking.

bySupplier.title: Stock by supplier
bySupplier.body: Whose phones are sitting in your stock: the person or shop you last bought each phone from, with the count and (owner / manager) the cost. Phones that came as a trade-in or as opening stock show as "No supplier". Tap a name to open that person.
bySupplier.example: "Ali Traders 12 phones · at cost 4,80,000" → 12 phones in stock were bought from Ali Traders, Hall Road.

statusCounts.title: Where every device is
statusCounts.body: All the devices the shop has ever recorded, counted by where each one is now: in stock, sold, on loan, with a customer, in repair, faulty or returned to the supplier.
statusCounts.example: "In stock 42 · Sold 340 · On loan 2 · In repair 1" → 2 phones are out with another shop on loan.

topCost.title: Most expensive (cost)
topCost.body: The 5 phones in stock that cost you the most. Your biggest money is tied up in these.
topCost.example: iPhone 13 Pro Rs. 1,95,000 at the top → if it sits for months, that is Rs. 1,95,000 not working for you.

topAsking.title: Most expensive (asking)
topAsking.body: The 5 phones in stock with the highest asking price.
topAsking.example: Samsung S23 Ultra asking Rs. 2,40,000 is first → it is the most expensive phone a customer can buy from you today.

topMargin.title: Highest expected profit
topMargin.body: The 5 phones in stock with the biggest gap between asking price and cost, with that gap as a % of the cost.

lowMargin.title: Thinnest margin
lowMargin.body: The 5 phones in stock with the smallest gap between asking price and cost. A minus means the asking price is below what you paid.
lowMargin.example: Samsung A15: cost Rs. 38,000, asking Rs. 38,500 → "500 (1.3%)" — almost no profit; check the price.

bands.title: Age bands (chart)
bands.body: How many phones in stock fall in each age band. Age counts from the day the phone came in on its current round (bought, or returned by a customer). The hint on a bar is its cost (owner / manager) or its asking value. Tap a bar or a chip to list only those phones.
bands.example: Default bands: Fresh ≤15 days, Normal 16–30, Slow 31–60, Attention 61–90, Dead over 90. A phone bought 70 days ago is in "Attention".

fresh.title: Fresh
fresh.body: Phones that came in recently — up to the first age limit (15 days unless you changed it). Nothing to worry about.
fresh.example: Infinix Hot 40 bought 6 days ago → Fresh.

normal.title: Normal
normal.body: Phones older than the first limit up to the second (16–30 days by default). A normal time to sell.
normal.example: Samsung A15 in the shop for 22 days → Normal.

slow.title: Slow
slow.body: Phones past the second limit up to the third (31–60 days by default). Selling slower than usual; think about the price or show it more.
slow.example: Oppo A78 in the shop for 45 days → Slow.

attention.title: Attention
attention.body: Phones past the third limit up to the last one (61–90 days by default). Money is getting stuck; act before it becomes dead stock.
attention.example: Vivo Y17s in the shop for 75 days → Attention.

dead.title: Dead
dead.body: Phones older than the last limit (over 90 days by default). Each one also shows in "Needs attention" as dead stock.
dead.example: Tecno Spark 10 in the shop for 120 days → Dead.

thresholds.title: Change thresholds
thresholds.body: Opens Settings, where you set your own limits: the 4 age-band days, the "high value" price, the thin-margin %, the top / low product rules and the skipped-ID-check rules.
thresholds.example: Change the bands from 15/30/60/90 to 10/20/40/60 → a phone 45 days old moves from Slow to Attention.

alerts.title: Needs attention
alerts.body: Phones in stock that need a look today, most serious first: flagged ID check, dead stock, high value and slow, pending ID check, missing cost or asking price, thin margin, came back more than once. One phone can appear under two reasons. Tap a row to open the phone.
alerts.example: iPhone 13 cost Rs. 1,45,000, 40 days in the shop → "High value, slow"; if its asking is Rs. 1,48,000 it also shows "Thin margin" (2.1%).

deadStock.title: Dead stock
deadStock.body: The phone has been in the shop longer than your last age limit (90 days by default).
deadStock.example: Tecno Spark 10 bought 95 days ago → Dead stock. Rs. 28,000 has been stuck for 3 months.

highValueSlow.title: High value, slow
highValueSlow.body: An expensive phone (cost at or above your "high value" price, Rs. 50,000 by default) that is past the Normal band (over 30 days) but not yet dead.
highValueSlow.example: iPhone 13 cost Rs. 1,45,000, 40 days in the shop → High value, slow. A Rs. 30,000 phone of the same age is not listed.

lowMargin.title: Thin margin
lowMargin.body: The asking price is only a little above the cost: (asking − cost) ÷ cost is below your thin-margin % (5% by default). Only phones with both prices.
lowMargin.example: Cost Rs. 40,000, asking Rs. 41,500 → 1,500 ÷ 40,000 = 3.75% → Thin margin.

missingCost.title: No cost
missingCost.body: The phone has no purchase price recorded, so its profit cannot be worked out. Usually opening stock entered without a cost. Owner and manager only.
missingCost.example: Old Samsung A12 entered as opening stock with no cost → when it sells for Rs. 22,000 the whole Rs. 22,000 would look like profit. Add the cost.

missingAsking.title: No asking price
missingAsking.body: No selling price is written on the phone, so staff do not know what to ask and its value is missing from "At asking".
missingAsking.example: Infinix Note 30 bought for Rs. 45,000 with no asking price → write e.g. Rs. 49,500 on it.

verificationPending.title: ID check pending
verificationPending.body: A used phone (or one bought from a person, not a supplier) whose ID / stolen-phone check is not done yet.
verificationPending.example: Used iPhone 11 bought from a walk-in for Rs. 70,000 yesterday, check not done → ID check pending.

verificationFlagged.title: ID check flagged
verificationFlagged.body: The check found a problem (for example the IMEI is reported stolen or the seller's ID did not match). Do not sell this phone.
verificationFlagged.example: Samsung S21 bought for Rs. 85,000, check says stolen → flagged; keep it aside and do not sell it.

repeatReturns.title: Came back more than once
repeatReturns.body: The phone was sold and returned by a customer 2 or more times. "×3" means it came back 3 times — check it for a fault.
repeatReturns.example: Oppo A57 sold, returned, sold again, returned again → "×2".

clear.title: ID checked
clear.body: Phones whose ID / stolen-phone check came out clean. The big number is phones in stock now; "all time" counts every phone ever recorded.
clear.example: 30 in stock · all time 410 → 410 phones have been checked clean since you started, 30 of them are still in the shop.

pending.title: ID check pending
pending.body: Phones still waiting for their ID check — used phones and phones bought from a person. Big number: in stock now; "all time": every phone.
pending.example: 5 in stock · all time 7 → 5 phones in the shop still need checking; 2 more were sold or moved without a finished check.

flagged.title: Stolen? Do not sell
flagged.body: Phones whose check found a problem. Big number: in stock now; "all time": every phone ever flagged. A flagged phone in stock should be kept aside.
flagged.example: 1 in stock · all time 3 → one flagged Samsung S21 is in the shop; do not sell it.

notRequired.title: No check needed
notRequired.body: Box-pack phones bought from a supplier do not need an ID check. Big number: in stock now; "all time": every such phone.
notRequired.example: 12 new box-pack Infinix Hot 40 from the distributor → 12 in "No check needed".

checksInPeriod.title: Checks saved in the period
checksInPeriod.body: How many ID checks were saved between the period's dates, by their result: clear, pending or flagged. A skipped check is not counted here.
checksInPeriod.example: This month: "ID checked 18 · pending 2 · flagged 1" → 21 checks were saved.

bypasses.title: Skipped ID checks
bypasses.body: Every time someone in the period marked a phone as checked by choosing "I know this person" instead of doing the check. Each person's line shows: skipped · how many of those were flagged phones · their phones bought (intakes) · skipped as a % of intakes. The list below shows each skip with who, when, from whom and the reason.
bypasses.example: Bilal: "4 skipped · 10 intakes · 40%" → he bought 10 phones this month and skipped the check on 4.

unusual.title: Unusual (skipped checks)
unusual.body: A person is marked "unusual" when they skipped the check on a flagged phone, or skipped at least the minimum number (3 by default) and at least the set share of their own intakes (50% by default). Change these in Settings.
unusual.example: Bilal skipped 4 of 6 phones he bought = 67% (4 ≥ 3 and 67% ≥ 50%) → unusual. Asad skipped 2 of 20 → not unusual.

products.title: Products
products.body: What sold in the period, read from the sale bills (voided bills left out): per model, per brand or per type, with units, money, profit and a Top / Average / Low class. Accessories appear only in "By model", under their own name.
products.example: By model, this month: Samsung A15 12 sold, Infinix Hot 40 8, Tecno Spark 10 1. By brand the same sales show as Samsung 12, Infinix 8, Tecno 1.

unitsSold.title: Units sold
unitsSold.body: Pieces sold in the period that were not returned. In "By brand" and "By type" only phones, tablets and watches are counted.
unitsSold.example: Sold 50 phones and 30 chargers, 2 phones came back → By model: 78 units; By brand: 48.

sales.title: Net sales (products)
sales.body: The money from the bill lines sold in the period that were not returned, added up. Voided bills are left out.
sales.example: Sold 3 phones for Rs. 1,20,000, one came back (Rs. 40,000) → net sales Rs. 80,000.

profit.title: Profit on sales
profit.body: Sale price minus cost, for the lines sold in the period and not returned. Owner and manager only.
profit.example: Samsung A15 sold Rs. 42,000, cost Rs. 38,000; Infinix Hot 40 sold Rs. 34,000, cost Rs. 30,000 → profit Rs. 8,000.

classes.title: Top · average · low
classes.body: How many rows (models, brands or types) fall in each class. Low = sold no more than the low limit (1 piece by default); Top = at least the top share of all units (20% by default); everything else is Average.
classes.example: 50 phones sold: A15 12 (24%) → Top; Spark 10 1 → Low; Hot 40 8 (16%) → Average → shows "1 · 1 · 1".

soldVsBought.title: Sold vs bought (chart)
soldVsBought.body: Each bar is a day, week or month of the period. The green bars are units sold; the amber bars below are units bought (purchase lines not returned, accessories included). Hold a green bar to see its money.
soldVsBought.example: Week 2: sold 14, bought 20 → you are buying faster than you sell; stock is growing.

classFilter.title: Show by class
classFilter.body: Show only the rows of one class — Top, Average or Low — or All.
classFilter.example: Tap "Low" → only the models that sold 1 piece or fewer, like Tecno Spark 10 with 1 sale.

top.title: Top
top.body: Sold more than the low limit and at least the top share of all units sold in the period (20% by default).
top.example: 50 units sold in all, Samsung A15 sold 12 → 12 ÷ 50 = 24% → Top.

average.title: Average
average.body: Sold more than the low limit but less than the top share.
average.example: 50 units in all, Infinix Hot 40 sold 8 → 16%, under 20% → Average.

low.title: Low
low.body: Sold no more than the low limit (1 piece by default) in the period — even if that is a big share of very few sales.
low.example: Tecno Spark 10 sold 1 → Low. In a week with only 3 sales, a model with 1 sale (33%) is still Low.

thresholds.title: Class limits
thresholds.body: The two limits behind the classes, as set in Settings: the top share in % and the low number of units. "Change thresholds" opens Settings.
thresholds.example: "Top = 20% of units or more · Low = 1 unit(s) or fewer" → set Low to 2 and every model that sold 2 also becomes Low.

rowFigures.title: What each row shows
rowFigures.body: Units sold · money; the bar and "% of units" = its share of all units; profit (and % of cost); avg price per piece; avg days to sell (from the day it came in to the day it sold); returned = pieces that came back; in stock = same model in the shop now. Tap a row to open it in Stock.
rowFigures.example: "Samsung A15 12 · 5,04,000 · 24% of units · profit 48,000 (10.5%) · avg price 42,000 · avg days to sell 18 · in stock 4".

bills.title: Documents in the period
bills.body: Every document made between the period's dates: sale bills, purchase bills, payments received and given, and returns. Voided documents are not in this total; they are listed at the bottom.
bills.example: 120 sale bills + 15 purchase bills + 40 payments + 5 returns → 180 documents.

sale.title: Sale bills
sale.body: Sale bills in the period that are not voided, with their total. "· 2 voided" tells how many were cancelled. Tap to open the list.
sale.example: 122 bills made, 2 voided → shows 120 and their total Rs. 48,00,000 · 2 voided.

purchase.title: Purchase bills
purchase.body: Purchase bills in the period that are posted (not voided), with their total. Owner and manager only.
purchase.example: 15 purchases from Hall Road suppliers, total Rs. 9,80,000.

paymentIn.title: Payments received
paymentIn.body: Payments taken in the period as their own document — for example a customer paying off udhaar — not the cash paid on a bill at the counter.
paymentIn.example: Ahmed pays Rs. 5,000 of his udhaar by Easypaisa → 1 payment received, Rs. 5,000.

paymentOut.title: Payments given
paymentOut.body: Payments you made in the period as their own document — for example paying a supplier what you owe. Owner and manager see the amount.
paymentOut.example: Paid Ali Traders Rs. 50,000 by bank transfer → 1 payment given, Rs. 50,000.

saleReturn.title: Returns from customers
saleReturn.body: Return documents in the period for goods customers brought back, with their amount.
saleReturn.example: A customer returned a Samsung A15 sold for Rs. 42,000 → 1 return, Rs. 42,000.

purchaseReturn.title: Returns to suppliers
purchaseReturn.body: Return documents in the period for goods you sent back to a supplier. Owner and manager see the amount.
purchaseReturn.example: Sent back a faulty Infinix Hot 40 bought for Rs. 30,000 → 1 return, Rs. 30,000.

byStatus.title: Sale bills by status
byStatus.body: The period's sale bills (voided ones too) grouped by where they stand today: paid, part paid, nothing paid, returned or voided — count · total · and for unpaid ones the amount still due (total − paid).
byStatus.example: 10 part-paid bills worth Rs. 3,00,000, Rs. 2,20,000 received → "10 · 3,00,000 · due 80,000".

byUser.title: Bills by employee
byUser.body: For each person, the documents they made in the period: sale bills and their total, purchase bills, payments, and how many of the documents they made are now voided.
byUser.example: Bilal: "45 sales · Rs. 18,00,000 · 3 purchases · 12 payments · 2 voided".

voided.title: Voided documents
voided.body: Every sale bill, purchase bill or payment of the period that was cancelled: its number, date, who voided it and the reason. The amount is struck through because it no longer counts. Tap to open it.
voided.example: Sale bill S-0142 Rs. 35,000 voided by Bilal, reason "wrong IMEI" → the phone went back to stock and a new bill was made.

people.title: People
people.body: Your customers, suppliers and other shops for the period: how many there are, and the top 20 by the measure you pick. Tap a person to see everything they ever did with you.
people.example: Pick "Customers by sales" → Ahmed first with Rs. 1,30,000 this month; tap him to see all his bills and payments.

metric.title: Rank by
metric.body: Pick what to rank people by. The dark card shows the total of that measure for everyone and how many people have it; each row shows the person's value and their share of that total.
metric.example: Total Rs. 10,00,000 from 85 customers; Ahmed Rs. 1,30,000 → his share is 13%.

customersSales.title: Customers by sales
customersSales.body: Each named customer's sale bills in the period, minus what they returned (voided bills left out). Walk-in bills with no name are not counted.
customersSales.example: Ahmed: 3 bills Rs. 1,50,000, returned one charger set Rs. 20,000 → Rs. 1,30,000.

customersBills.title: Customers by bills
customersBills.body: How many sale bills (not voided) each named customer had in the period — who comes back most often.
customersBills.example: Usman bought 7 times this month, Ahmed 3 times → Usman first with 7.

customersProfit.title: Customers by profit
customersProfit.body: The profit you made on each customer in the period: sale price minus cost of the items they kept. Owner and manager only.
customersProfit.example: Ahmed bought an iPhone 13 for Rs. 1,60,000 that cost Rs. 1,45,000 → profit Rs. 15,000.

suppliersPurchases.title: Suppliers by purchases
suppliersPurchases.body: What you bought from each supplier in the period: their purchase bills minus what you returned to them (voided bills left out).
suppliersPurchases.example: Ali Traders: bills Rs. 5,00,000, returned one phone Rs. 30,000 → Rs. 4,70,000.

suppliersDevices.title: Suppliers by phones
suppliersDevices.body: How many phones, tablets and watches you bought from each supplier in the period (returned ones left out).
suppliersDevices.example: Bought 20 phones from Ali Traders, sent 1 back → 19.

suppliersProfit.title: Suppliers by profit on their phones
suppliersProfit.body: The profit on the phones sold in the period, grouped by the supplier you bought each phone from — whose phones earn you the most. Owner and manager only.
suppliersProfit.example: 3 phones from Ali Traders sold this month with profits of Rs. 4,000, 5,500 and 3,000 → Rs. 12,500.

receivable.title: Largest amounts owed to us
receivable.body: People whose khata shows they owe you, on the last day of the period (or the "As of" day), biggest first.
receivable.example: Usman's khata: bills Rs. 80,000, paid Rs. 55,000 → he owes Rs. 25,000 and is listed.

payable.title: Largest amounts we owe
payable.body: People whose khata shows you owe them, on the last day of the period (or the "As of" day), biggest first.
payable.example: Ali Traders: bought Rs. 4,70,000, paid Rs. 3,90,000 → you owe Rs. 80,000.

customer.title: Customers
customer.body: Big number: customers saved in the app up to the end of the period. "new" = added during the period; "dealt" = how many had at least one sale bill in the period.
customer.example: "250 · new 18 · dealt 85" → 250 customers on the books, 18 added this month, 85 bought something this month.

supplier.title: Suppliers
supplier.body: Big number: suppliers saved up to the end of the period. "new" = added during the period; "dealt" = how many you bought from in the period.
supplier.example: "30 · new 2 · dealt 9" → you bought from 9 of your 30 suppliers this month.

shop.title: Other shops
shop.body: Other mobile shops saved in the app (for loans and give-and-take between shops), up to the end of the period, and how many were added in the period.
shop.example: "6 · new 1" → 6 Hall Road shops on the books, 1 added this month.

security.title: Security
security.body: Owner only. One list of everything in the period that bent a price or a rule — price changes, sales under asking or cost, discounts, voids, reversals, stock adjustments, opening balances, skipped ID checks, wrong PINs, admin actions, money moved — with who, when, before → after, reason and who approved. Nothing here can be edited or deleted.
security.example: "Sold under asking · Samsung A15 · Bilal · 42,000 → 40,000 · −2,000 · approved: Owner".

kinds.title: Kinds of record
kinds.body: Each chip is one kind of record with how many happened in the period. Tap a chip to see only that kind; "All" shows everything. Only kinds that happened are shown.
kinds.example: "All · 37 · Discount · 20 · Voided · 4" → tap "Voided" to see the 4 cancelled documents.

askingChanged.title: Asking changed
askingChanged.body: Someone changed the asking price of a phone. The row shows old → new and the difference.
askingChanged.example: Samsung A15 asking changed 42,000 → 39,000 by Bilal → −3,000.

belowAsking.title: Sold under asking
belowAsking.body: A phone was sold for less than its asking price. The row shows asking → sold price, the difference and who approved it.
belowAsking.example: iPhone 13 asking 1,60,000 sold for 1,55,000 → −5,000, approved by the owner with the PIN.

belowCost.title: Sold under cost
belowCost.body: A phone was sold for less than it cost you — a loss. The row shows cost → sold price and the loss.
belowCost.example: Infinix Hot 40 cost 30,000 sold for 28,500 → −1,500 loss.

discount.title: Discount
discount.body: A sale bill with a discount. The row shows the bill before discount → after, and the discount.

void.title: Voided
void.body: A sale bill, purchase bill or payment was cancelled. A finished bill cannot be edited; a mistake is voided and made again.
void.example: Bilal voided bill S-0142 (Rs. 35,000), reason "wrong IMEI".

reversal.title: Reversed
reversal.body: A khata / account entry was undone with an opposite entry, with a reason. Nothing is erased; the correction is a new entry.
reversal.example: A Rs. 10,000 payment posted to the wrong customer was reversed, reason "wrong person".

stockAdjust.title: Stock adjusted
stockAdjust.body: Someone changed the count of an accessory or item by hand, with a reason.
stockAdjust.example: Chargers adjusted from 20 to 18, reason "2 found broken".

openingBalance.title: Opening balance
openingBalance.body: An old balance was entered on a person's khata (money they owed you, or you owed them, from before the app).
openingBalance.example: Opening balance Rs. 15,000 entered for Usman → he owes Rs. 15,000 from the old register.

bypass.title: ID check skipped
bypass.body: A phone was marked as checked with "I know this person" instead of a real ID check.
bypass.example: Bilal bought a used Vivo Y17s for Rs. 25,000 and skipped the check, reason "neighbour".

pinWrong.title: Wrong PIN
pinWrong.body: A wrong owner PIN was typed when asking approval for a price (for example selling under asking). Login failures are not listed here.
pinWrong.example: Staff tried 3 wrong PINs to sell an iPhone 13 under asking → 3 rows.

delete.title: Deleted
delete.body: A brand or model name was removed from your list. Only names no phone uses can be deleted.
delete.example: The unused model "Galaxy A0" typed by mistake was deleted by the manager.

admin.title: Admin action
admin.body: A change to the account itself: a password set by the admin or reset by OTP, support access by the provider, a new branch, or the modules or plan changed.
admin.example: The manager's password was reset by OTP on 3 November → 1 admin action.

transfer.title: Money moved
transfer.body: Money moved between your own accounts — galla, bank, JazzCash, Easypaisa.
transfer.example: Rs. 50,000 moved from the galla to Meezan Bank at closing → 1 row.

byUser.title: By employee
byUser.body: For each person, how many records of each kind are theirs in the period. A red "flagged" tag shows when a count reaches its limit.
byUser.example: "Bilal — flagged: Voided · Discount 6 · Voided 3 · Sold under asking 1".

flagged.title: Flag limits
flagged.body: A person is flagged for a kind when their count in the period reaches its limit: voided 3, sold under asking 3, sold under cost 2, discount 5, wrong PIN 3, asking changed 5, ID check skipped = your shop's minimum (3 by default).
flagged.example: Bilal sold 2 phones under cost this month → 2 ≥ 2 → flagged for "Sold under cost".

staff.title: Staff
staff.body: One card per person for the period: what they sold, bought, received, paid out and spent. The owner also sees each person's voids, price changes, skipped checks and other security counts. Tap the sales box to see their bills.
staff.example: Bilal's card: sold Rs. 18,00,000 in 45 bills, discounts 12,000, 2 purchases, payments 12 / 3, expenses 4.

total.title: Sales by the team
total.body: The total of all sale bills in the period (not voided), how many people appear below, and the total discount everyone gave.
total.example: Bilal Rs. 18,00,000 + Asad Rs. 12,00,000 → Rs. 30,00,000 · 2 people · discounts 20,000.

sold.title: Sold
sold.body: The total of the sale bills this person made in the period (after discount; voided bills left out; returns shown apart).
sold.example: Bilal made 45 bills adding up to Rs. 18,00,000 → Sold Rs. 18,00,000.

bills.title: Bills
bills.body: How many sale bills this person made in the period (voided ones left out).

discount.title: Discounts given
discount.body: The discounts on this person's sale bills in the period, added up.
discount.example: Bilal gave Rs. 500 on 10 bills and Rs. 1,000 on 7 → Rs. 12,000.

profit.title: Profit on sales
profit.body: Sale price minus cost on the items this person sold that were not returned. Owner and manager only.
profit.example: Asad sold phones for Rs. 12,00,000 that cost Rs. 10,80,000 → profit Rs. 1,20,000.

onCredit.title: On credit
onCredit.body: The part of this person's bills that was not paid at the counter when the bill was made — given as udhaar.
onCredit.example: Bill Rs. 60,000, customer paid Rs. 40,000 cash at the counter → Rs. 20,000 on credit.

returns.title: Returns
returns.body: How many customer returns this person recorded in the period.
returns.example: Bilal took back 2 phones from customers this month → 2.

purchases.title: Purchases
purchases.body: How many purchase bills this person made in the period and their total. Owner and manager only.

payments.title: Payments in / out
payments.body: How many payments this person recorded in the period: received / given (voided ones left out).
payments.example: "12 / 3" → Bilal took 12 udhaar payments from customers and paid suppliers 3 times.

expenses.title: Expenses
expenses.body: How many expenses this person entered in the period and their total.
expenses.example: Asad entered tea Rs. 600, rickshaw Rs. 400, bill Rs. 3,000 → "Expenses 3 · 4,000".

security.title: Security counts
security.body: Owner only. This person's records from the Security list for the period, by kind. A kind in red has reached its flag limit. Tap to open the Security list.
security.example: "Discount 6 · Voided 3 · Sold under asking 1" with Voided in red (limit 3).

flag.title: Flag
flag.body: The kinds where this person reached the flag limit in the period (voided 3, under asking 3, under cost 2, discount 5, wrong PIN 3, asking changed 5, skipped ID checks = your minimum). A reason to look, not proof of wrongdoing.
flag.example: Bilal voided 3 bills this month → flag "Voided".

came.title: Taken in
came.body: Repair jobs opened in the period (customers' phones and your own).
came.example: 15 phones came in for repair this week.

given.title: Given back
given.body: Jobs closed with the bill (handed back to the customer) in the period.

notFixed.title: Could not fix
notFixed.body: Phones returned to the customer without repair in the period.

openNow.title: Open now
openNow.body: Jobs not yet closed today, whatever the period.
openNow.example: 7 phones still in the shop or at labs.

readyNow.title: Ready, not collected
readyNow.body: Fixed phones waiting for the customer. Call them.
readyNow.example: 3 ready: call Ahmed, Bilal and Sana.

lateNow.title: Late now
lateNow.body: Open jobs past the day promised to the customer.

atLabNow.title: At a lab now
atLabNow.body: Phones with outside labs right now.

lateAtLab.title: Late at a lab
lateAtLab.body: Phones still at a lab after its promised day.

income.title: Repair income
income.body: Repair bills of the period (parts + work charge − discount).

parts.title: Parts cost
parts.body: What the parts used on those bills cost the shop.

labCustomer.title: Lab charges
labCustomer.body: Outside labs' charges for customers' phones that came back in the period.

profit.title: Repair profit
profit.body: Repair income − parts cost − lab charges.

labStock.title: Lab charges on own phones
labStock.body: Labs' charges for the shop's own stock phones. Not in repair profit: they are added to those phones' cost.
labStock.example: Used A54 bought Rs. 40,000 + lab Rs. 3,000 → cost Rs. 43,000.

series.title: Taken in by day
series.body: Phones taken in for repair on each day (or week / month); the tip shows how many were given back.

labs.title: Repair labs in the period
labs.body: Each lab that got phones in the period: sent, fixed, not fixed, average days, fixed % and charges.

needsLook.title: Needs a look now
needsLook.body: Phones late at a lab and jobs past the customer's promised day. Tap one to open it.
needsLook.example: iPhone 11 at Ali Lab 4 days; Ahmed's A54 2 days late.

faults.title: Most common problems
faults.body: Which problems came in most in the period: keep those parts in stock.

bulk.title: Bulk Excel
bulk.body: Instead of typing one phone or one person at a time, you fill a sheet in Excel and upload it. The app checks every row and tells you, in plain words, what is wrong. Nothing is saved until you press Import, and then either every good row is saved or nothing is.
bulk.example: 50 old phones in stock: write them in the sheet in 20 minutes, upload once, done.

name.title: Name
name.body: The person's or shop's name as you call them. It shows on bills, the khata and WhatsApp messages.

phone.title: Mobile number
phone.body: The person's mobile number. It finds them quickly and is used for WhatsApp bills and reminders.
phone.example: 0321 5550002 — type it once; next time just search 0321555.

cnic.title: CNIC (ID card)
cnic.body: The 13-digit number on the person's ID card. Keep it when you buy a used phone, so you know who sold it.

address.title: Address
address.body: Where the person or shop is. Optional; useful for dealers and for delivery.

notes.title: Note
notes.body: Anything you want to remember about this entry. Only your shop sees it.
notes.example: "Will pay the rest on Friday" or "box has a scratch".

amount.title: Amount
amount.body: How much money, in rupees. Type only the number; the app adds commas.

date.title: Date
date.body: The day this happened. It is today unless you change it; reports count it on this day.
date.example: You forgot to enter yesterday's sale: set yesterday's date and it counts in yesterday's hisaab.

method.title: How it was paid
method.body: Cash, online (bank app / Easypaisa / JazzCash), cheque or from abroad. It decides which account the money goes into.
