method.example: Customer sends Rs. 10,000 on Easypaisa: choose Online → Easypaisa; it lands in the Easypaisa account, not the galla.

account.title: Account (galla / bank / wallet)
account.body: Where the shop keeps money: the galla (cash drawer), a bank account, Easypaisa or JazzCash. Each has its own balance.
account.example: Galla Rs. 40,000 + HBL Rs. 2,00,000 + Easypaisa Rs. 15,000 = Rs. 2,55,000 in all.

discount.title: Discount
discount.body: Money taken off the price for the customer. It lowers the bill and your profit.
discount.example: Phone Rs. 32,000, discount Rs. 500 → customer pays Rs. 31,500.

tax.title: Tax (sales tax)
tax.body: Government sales tax added on top of the price, if your shop is registered. It is collected for the government, not your income.
tax.example: Bill Rs. 10,000 with 18% tax → customer pays Rs. 11,800; Rs. 1,800 is tax.

paid.title: Paid now
paid.body: The money given at the counter right now. Whatever is not paid stays as udhaar on the khata.
paid.example: Bill Rs. 50,000, paid now Rs. 20,000 → Rs. 30,000 udhaar.

remaining.title: Remaining (baqi)
remaining.body: What is still to be paid on this bill or khata after everything paid so far.
remaining.example: Bill Rs. 30,000, paid Rs. 18,000 → remaining Rs. 12,000.

qty.title: Quantity
qty.body: How many pieces. Items bought by the dozen or box are still counted in pieces.

period.title: Period
period.body: Which days the screen counts: today, this week, this month, a custom from–to, and so on. Every figure on the screen is for these days only.
period.example: "This month" on 15 March counts 1 to 15 March; "Last month" counts all of February.

asOf.title: As of a day
asOf.body: Shows balances (stock, udhaar, cash) as they were at the end of that day, not today.
asOf.example: As of 31 January: how much udhaar people owed on that night, even if they paid later.

download.title: Print / Excel
download.body: Print this screen or save it as a PDF, or download it as an Excel sheet to keep or send to your accountant.
download.example: End of month: Excel → send to the accountant on WhatsApp.

search.title: Search
search.body: Type part of a name, mobile number, IMEI or bill number; the list shows only what matches.
search.example: Type 4512 to find the phone whose IMEI ends in 4512.

page.title: Super admin
page.body: Your own page as the software owner: every customer shop with its package, fee and days left, fee payments to check, and opening new shops. Shopkeepers never see it.
page.example: Star Mobiles (Hall Road) asks for the app: open the shop here, send the login on WhatsApp, and approve his Rs. 2,000 fee when the screenshot comes.

business.title: Business console
business.body: Opens your business view: monthly income (MRR), money received by month and by channel, fees coming and overdue, who is using the app now, and the license keys.
business.example: 3 shops pay Rs. 2,000 a month → the console shows MRR Rs. 6,000.

appLink.title: Android app link
appLink.body: The download link of the shop app for Android phones. It always gives the newest version, so the same link works for every shop.
appLink.example: A new shop asks for the app: tap WhatsApp, pick the owner; he opens the link on his Infinix Hot 40 and installs.

fees.title: Software fees
fees.body: Fee payments shop owners report to you, with amount, transaction ID and screenshot. Received extends that shop's plan by the months it paid for; Reject sends your reason back to the shop owner.
fees.example: Ali Mobiles sends Rs. 6,000 on Easypaisa for 3 months → you see it in your Easypaisa, tap Received · +3 months → his plan runs 3 more months.

feesMonth.title: This month · to check
feesMonth.body: This month: total of the fees you approved since the 1st of this month (by the day you approved them). To check: payments shops reported that you have not approved or rejected yet.
feesMonth.example: You approved Rs. 2,000 and Rs. 4,000 this month and 1 screenshot is waiting → This month Rs. 6,000 · 1 to check.

billing.title: Billing settings
billing.body: Your bank details, support numbers, the reminder schedule and a note for shops. Shops see them on the fee reminder and on their Software fees screen. Wallets (Easypaisa, JazzCash) go under Payment accounts.
billing.example: Fill your Meezan Bank details and WhatsApp 0300 1234567 once → every shop's reminder shows where to pay and whom to message.

bankName.title: Bank name
bankName.body: The bank where shops can send your fee by transfer.

accountTitle.title: Account title
accountTitle.body: The name on your bank account exactly as the bank shows it, so the shop owner sees he is paying the right person.

accountNumber.title: Account number
accountNumber.body: Your bank account number, for a transfer from the same bank or a bank app.

iban.title: IBAN
iban.body: Your 24-character bank number that starts with PK. Any bank app can send money to it.

branch.title: Branch
branch.body: Your bank branch name or code. Some shop owners pay at the bank counter and need it.

supportPhone.title: Support phone
supportPhone.body: The number shop owners call for help with the software or the fee. It shows on the reminder.

supportWa.title: Support WhatsApp
supportWa.body: The WhatsApp number shops message for help or to send the payment screenshot. The Help on WhatsApp button opens a chat with it.
supportWa.example: 0300 1234567 → the shop owner taps Help on WhatsApp and the chat opens with you.

schedule.title: Reminder schedule
schedule.body: How many days before the plan ends each reminder starts: first a yellow bar, then orange with a popup, then red. After the end date the grace days run; after them the shop is locked.
schedule.example: Yellow 7, orange 3, red 1, grace 7; plan ends 30 November → yellow from 23 Nov, orange from 27 Nov, red on 29 Nov, locked from 8 December.

infoDays.title: Yellow bar from
infoDays.body: Days before the end date when a small yellow bar starts showing on the shop's screens. No popup yet.
infoDays.example: 7 → plan ends 30 November, the yellow bar shows from 23 November.

warnDays.title: Orange bar + popup from
warnDays.body: Days before the end date when the bar turns orange and a reminder popup shows once a day.
warnDays.example: 3 → from 27 November the owner sees the popup once each day.

urgentDays.title: Red bar + popup from
urgentDays.body: Days before the end date when the bar turns red; the popup comes back after the snooze hours.
urgentDays.example: 1 → on 29 November the bar is red and the popup returns every 4 hours.

graceDays.title: Grace days after expiry
graceDays.body: Days after the end date when the shop still works fully, with a red bar and the popup. After them the shop is locked: it can only view, pay and back up its data.
graceDays.example: 7 → plan ends 30 November, the shop works till 7 December and is locked from 8 December.

snoozeHours.title: Snooze hours
snoozeHours.body: When the owner taps Remind me later on the red popup, it stays away this many hours.
snoozeHours.example: 4 → snoozed at 11 am, the popup comes back at 3 pm.

note.title: Note for shops
note.body: A short message shown to shop owners with your payment details. Write the same message in English, Urdu and Roman Urdu.
note.example: Please write your shop name in the transfer remarks.

accounts.title: Payment accounts
accounts.body: Your wallets and accounts where shop owners send the fee: Easypaisa, JazzCash, SadaPay or a bank. Every shop sees this list on its Software fees screen.
accounts.example: Easypaisa · Ahmed Raza · 0345 1234567 → the shop owner copies the number and sends Rs. 2,000.

label.title: Account name
label.body: The name of the wallet or bank as the shop owner knows it.

name.title: Account holder
name.body: The name registered on that account, so the shop owner can check it before sending.

number.title: Number / IBAN
number.body: The wallet's mobile number or the bank IBAN the money goes to.

note.title: Account note
note.body: An optional line shown under the account for the shop owner.
note.example: Send the screenshot on WhatsApp after paying.

shopRequests.title: Shop requests from the website
shopRequests.body: People who filled the form on the website to get the app. Open a new shop fills the form with their details; the tick marks the request done.
shopRequests.example: Bilal from Saddar, Karachi asks for the basic package → tap Open a new shop; his name and number are already filled.

pwRequests.title: Password requests
pwRequests.body: Shop owners who tapped Forgot password on the login screen. Set a new password for the shop and send it on WhatsApp, then tap the tick.
pwRequests.example: Usman forgot his password → Set password, type ms4821, Save, Send on WhatsApp, tick.

filter.title: All · Fees due · Locked
filter.body: Narrows the shop list. Fees due: plans ending in 7 days or less, or already ended but still in grace days. Locked: the grace days are over, so the shop can only view and pay.
filter.example: 2 shops end this week and 1 ended 3 days ago → Fees due 3.

shops.title: Customer shops
shops.body: Every shop using your software, with its owner, package, days left and monthly fee. Tap a shop to change its package, record a payment, make a renewal code or set a password.
shops.example: Star Mobiles · basic · 12 days left · Rs. 2,000/month.

planStatus.title: Package and days left
planStatus.body: The shop's package and how long its plan runs. Green: running. Amber: 7 days or less left. Red: ended (grace days) or locked. Expires is the last paid day.
planStatus.example: basic · 5 days left · Expires 30 Nov → remind him to pay Rs. 2,000.

openShop.title: Open this shop
openShop.body: Opens the shop's app as if you were inside it, to check or fix something for the owner. Your visit is written in that shop's activity log.
openShop.example: The owner says a sale is missing → open his shop and look at today's sales yourself.

ownerPassword.title: Owner's password
ownerPassword.body: When the shop owner forgets his password, set a new one here and send it to him. The old password stops working.
ownerPassword.example: Type ms5521 → Save → Send on WhatsApp → he logs in with 0321 5550002 and ms5521.

newPassword.title: New password
newPassword.body: The new login password for the shop owner, at least 6 characters. Keep it easy to type on a phone.

modules.title: Modules for this shop
modules.body: Which extra parts of the app this shop can use. The basics (stock, sale, purchase, khata, payments) are always on. Follow the plan ticked: the package decides; untick it to choose by hand.
modules.example: A basic shop also needs repairs → untick Follow the plan, tick Repairs, Save modules.

followPlan.title: Follow the plan
followPlan.body: Ticked: the shop gets its package's modules, and they change when the package changes. Unticked: only the modules you tick below.
followPlan.example: basic gives accessories, expenses, hold a sale and tax; moving the shop to pro adds repairs and reports by itself.

plans.title: Package
plans.body: trial: everything, for trying the app. basic: the basics plus accessories, expenses, hold a sale and tax. pro: also repairs, exchange, reports, downloads, WhatsApp, qist, hazri and the assistant. chain: everything, for owners with several shops.
plans.example: A new shop starts on trial; after the trial he chooses basic at Rs. 2,000 a month.

monthlyFee.title: Monthly fee
monthlyFee.body: What this shop pays you each month, in rupees. It feeds the MRR and the coming / overdue fees of the business console. Empty or 0 = no fee.

expiresOn.title: Paid until
expiresOn.body: The last day the shop's plan is paid for. Reminders count down to it; after it the grace days start. Leave it empty and Save plan = no end date.
expiresOn.example: 30 November 2026 → from 1 December the shop is in its grace days.

feeNote.title: Note (only you)
feeNote.body: Your own remark about this shop's fee or deal. The shop owner never sees it.
feeNote.example: Pays every 3 months; first month free (friend of Bilal).

extend.title: +1 / +3 / +12 months
extend.body: Adds months to the plan at once and saves it. Counted from Paid until if it is still ahead, otherwise from today, so paying early never loses days. It records no payment.
extend.example: Paid until 20 November, today 10 November, tap +3 months → paid until 20 February.

unlimited.title: Unlimited
unlimited.body: Removes the end date: the shop gets no reminders and is never locked. For your own shop, a friend or a lifetime deal.
unlimited.example: Your demo shop: tap Unlimited and it shows No end date.

shopGrace.title: This shop's grace days
shopGrace.body: Days after the end date this one shop may keep working before it is locked. Empty = the grace days set in Billing settings.
shopGrace.example: Default 7; a trusted dealer gets 15 → he is locked only 15 days after his end date.

recordPayment.title: Record a payment
recordPayment.body: For money you received yourself (cash, or a transfer you saw in your bank app). It is saved as received, the plan is extended by the months at once, and a receipt number is made.
recordPayment.example: Bilal gives Rs. 6,000 cash: amount 6000, months 3, paid through cash → receipt SUB-0007 and his plan runs 3 more months.

payAmount.title: Amount (Rs)
payAmount.body: The rupees received in this payment. It starts as the shop's monthly fee; change it if he paid for more months.

payMonths.title: Months
payMonths.body: How many months this payment buys. The plan is extended by this many months.
payMonths.example: 3 → paid until moves from 30 November to 28 February.

payMethod.title: Paid through
payMethod.body: How the money came: cash, Easypaisa, JazzCash, bank and so on. The business console groups money by this word; capitals and spaces do not matter.
payMethod.example: Easypaisa and easypaisa count as one channel.

paidOn.title: Paid on
paidOn.body: The day the money was actually sent or handed over. The business console counts it in that day's month.
paidOn.example: Sent on 31 October, recorded on 2 November → it counts in October.

renewalCode.title: Renewal code
renewalCode.body: A signed key that adds months to this shop's plan when the owner pastes it in More → Software fees. It works without internet, only once. Every code is kept under Business → Keys.
renewalCode.example: A one-PC shop with no internet pays Rs. 2,000 → make a 1-month code, send it on WhatsApp, he pastes it → plan +1 month.

codeMonths.title: Months in the code
codeMonths.body: How many months the code adds when it is used. Making a code records no payment.
codeMonths.example: 12 → a one-year key for a shop that paid Rs. 20,000 for the year.

addBranch.title: Add a branch
addBranch.body: Opens another shop for the same owner. He switches shops with the same login; each shop keeps its own stock, khata and bills, while the package and fee stay one.
addBranch.example: Star Mobiles opens a second shop in Hafeez Centre → add the branch Star Mobiles 2, Lahore.

branchName.title: Branch name
branchName.body: The new shop's name, as it will show on its bills and screens.

city.title: City
city.body: The city of the shop. It shows in your shop list and helps you find the shop.

shopName.title: Shop name
shopName.body: The shop's name as it will show at the top of its bills and screens.

ownerName.title: Owner's name
ownerName.body: The name of the shop owner. It shows in your shop list.

ownerPhone.title: Owner's mobile (login)
ownerPhone.body: The owner logs in with this number, and the login details are sent to it on WhatsApp.

password.title: Password for the owner
password.body: The shop owner's first password, at least 6 characters. Give it to him with the login number.
password.example: ms4821 → he logs in with 0321 5550002 and ms4821.

language.title: Shop language
language.body: The language the shop's app, bills and WhatsApp messages start in. Each user can still switch the app language.
language.example: Urdu for a shop in Anarkali whose staff read only Urdu.

giveDetails.title: Login details
giveDetails.body: The mobile number and password the new shop owner logs in with. Send them on WhatsApp; the message also has the website and Android app links.

page.title: Business
page.body: Your business as the software owner: income, payments by channel, fees coming and overdue, each shop's package and time left, who uses the app online or offline, and the license keys.
page.example: 3 shops pay Rs. 2,000 a month → MRR Rs. 6,000; one of them ends in 5 days → Coming in 7 days Rs. 2,000.

tabs.title: Overview · Shops · Payments · Keys
tabs.body: Overview: the totals. Shops: one line per customer with package, days left and use. Payments: every fee payment with channel and status. Keys: renewal keys made, sent, used or cancelled.
tabs.example: Bilal says he paid → Payments, search Bilal → Rs. 2,000 · easypaisa · Pending.

mrr.title: Monthly income (MRR)
mrr.body: MRR means monthly recurring revenue: the monthly fees of all shops on a paid package (basic, pro, chain) whose plan has not ended. Trial, ended and locked shops are not counted.
mrr.example: 3 shops pay Rs. 2,000 a month and a 4th is locked → MRR Rs. 6,000.

arpu.title: Average per paying shop
arpu.body: MRR divided by the number of shops on a paid package (the Shops figure beside it). Ended and locked shops are in that number but add no fee, so they pull the average down.
arpu.example: MRR Rs. 6,000 and 3 shops → Rs. 2,000; with a 4th, locked shop → Rs. 1,500.

collectedMonth.title: Received this month
collectedMonth.body: Fees you approved, counted by the day they were paid, from the 1st of this month. Below it: the same for last month.
collectedMonth.example: Rs. 2,000 paid on 3 Nov and Rs. 6,000 on 10 Nov → Rs. 8,000; Last month Rs. 4,000.

collectedTotal.title: Received in total
collectedTotal.body: All approved fees since you started. Shops: how many different shops have paid at least once.

pending.title: Pending (to check)
pending.body: Payments shops reported that you have not approved or rejected yet; the number below counts the payments. Tap the tile to open Payments.
pending.example: 2 screenshots of Rs. 2,000 each → Rs. 4,000, Shops: 2.

coming7.title: Coming in 7 days
coming7.body: Monthly fees of the shops whose plan ends within the next 7 days, today included. These are the shops to remind now.
coming7.example: 2 shops of Rs. 2,000 end this week → Rs. 4,000, Shops: 2.

coming30.title: Coming in 30 days
coming30.body: Monthly fees of the shops whose plan ends within the next 30 days. It includes the 7-day ones.
coming30.example: 5 shops of Rs. 2,000 end this month → Rs. 10,000, Shops: 5.

overdue.title: Overdue
overdue.body: Monthly fees of the shops whose end date has passed (in grace days or locked): money you should have received already.
overdue.example: Ali Mobiles ended 5 days ago, fee Rs. 2,000 → Overdue Rs. 2,000, Shops: 1.

onlineNow.title: Using it now
onlineNow.body: Shops using the app right now: an online shop used in the last 10 minutes, a one-PC install that checked in within the last hour. Below it: shops used today and in the last 7 days.
onlineNow.example: 14 shops: 5 now, 11 today, 13 this week → 1 shop has not opened the app for a week.

keysTile.title: License keys
keysTile.body: The big number is the keys made but not used yet. Below it: keys used and keys cancelled. Tap the tile to open Keys.
keysTile.example: 10 keys made, 6 used, 1 cancelled → 3 not used yet.

byMonth.title: Received by month
byMonth.body: Approved fees of the last 12 months, one bar per month, by the day paid.
byMonth.example: October Rs. 18,000, November Rs. 24,000 → the bar for November is taller.

byChannel.title: By channel
byChannel.body: All approved fees grouped by how they were paid (the Paid through word): number of payments and total.

byPlan.title: By package
byPlan.body: How many shops are on each package and the monthly income (MRR) from them. Trial and ended plans add no income.

usage.title: Who is using it
usage.body: How many shops use the online app (website / Android) and how many the one-PC Windows install, and how many shops are in each plan status.
usage.example: Online 11, Offline 3; Running 9, Ending soon 2, Locked 1.

cloud.title: Online (website / app)
cloud.body: Shops using the app over the internet, on the website or the Android app. Their data is on your server.
cloud.example: 11 shops use the website or the app.

local.title: Offline (one-PC install)
local.body: Shops running the app on one shop computer, without your server. Their use shows only when that PC has internet and checks in.

statuses.title: Plan status
statuses.body: Running: more than 7 days left. Ending soon: 7 days or less. Expired (grace): ended but still working. Locked: grace over, view and pay only. No end date: unlimited. Trial: on the trial package.
statuses.example: Ending soon 2 → those 2 shops should get a reminder this week.

shopList.title: Shops list
shopList.body: One line per customer: monthly fee, package, status, days left, online or offline (green dot = in use now), total paid, last payment and channel, pending money and last use. Locked and ending shops come first. Tap a shop for details.
shopList.example: Star Mobiles · Rs. 2,000 / month · basic · Ending soon · 3 days left · Paid in total Rs. 12,000.

deployment.title: Online or offline
deployment.body: Whether the shop uses the online app (website / Android) or the one-PC install. In a shop's details you set it yourself, e.g. after installing the PC version.
deployment.example: You installed the Windows version at Ali Mobiles → set Offline (one-PC install).

version.title: Version
version.body: The app version on the shop's one-PC install, as the PC last reported it. It tells you if the PC needs an update.
version.example: 1.4.2 while the newest is 1.5.0 → update that PC.

fee.title: Fee
fee.body: This shop's monthly fee, with its package below it.

status.title: Plan status
status.body: Days left on the paid plan (or days past the end), with its status. ∞ means no end date.

paidTotal.title: Paid in total
paidTotal.body: All fees from this shop that you approved; the × figure is how many payments.

lastUsed.title: Last used
lastUsed.body: When someone in this shop last used the app (for a one-PC install: when it last checked in). Green dot = in use now.
lastUsed.example: never → he got the login but has not opened the app yet.

shopPayments.title: This shop's payments
shopPayments.body: Every fee this shop reported or you recorded, with channel, date, months, receipt and status.

payList.title: Payments list
payList.body: Every fee payment, newest first: shop, channel, date paid, months, reference, receipt and status. Search by shop name, transaction ID or receipt number.
payList.example: Search SUB-0007 to find the receipt Bilal asks about.

channels.title: Channel
channels.body: Shows only the payments made through one channel (the Paid through word).
channels.example: Tap jazzcash → only JazzCash payments are listed.

payStatus.title: Payment status
payStatus.body: Pending: waiting for you to check. Received: approved, the plan was extended. Rejected: not accepted; the shop saw your reason.
payStatus.example: Tap Pending to see the screenshots still to check.

approvedTotal.title: Received (shown)
approvedTotal.body: Total of the received payments in the list below, after the channel, status and search filters. Pending and rejected ones are not added.

what.title: License key
what.body: A signed code that adds months to one shop's plan. The shop owner pastes it in More → Software fees → Renewal code; it works on the website, the app or the one-PC install, without internet, once. The magic link shows the key to the shop owner for 7 days.
what.example: Ali Mobiles pays Rs. 6,000 → make a 3-month key, send it on WhatsApp; he pastes it and his plan runs 3 more months.

status.title: Not used · Used · Cancelled
status.body: Not used: made, waiting for the shop. Used: the shop renewed with it (on the website / app or the one-PC install). Cancelled: you revoked it and it no longer works.
status.example: A key sent to the wrong number → cancel it and make a new one.

forShop.title: For which shop
forShop.body: The shop the key is made for. A key works only for that shop.
forShop.example: Pick Star Mobiles; the same key will not work at Ali Mobiles.

months.title: Months in the key
months.body: How many months the key adds to the plan when it is used. Making a key records no payment; record the money separately.
months.example: 3 months → paid until 30 November becomes 28 February.

note.title: Key note
note.body: Your own remark on the key, such as why you made it. Only you see it.

card.title: Key card
card.body: The key, when it was made, how often it was sent and its link opened. WhatsApp / SMS: send it with the magic link. Copy key / Copy link: for any other app. Renew: a new key with the same months; the old unused one is cancelled. New magic link: a fresh 7-day link. Cancel key: it stops working.
card.example: Bilal lost the message → tap WhatsApp again: same key, Sent 2×.

pageWhat.title: Renewal key
pageWhat.body: Your software provider sent you this key to extend your shop's plan by the months shown. It is for your shop only and works once.
pageWhat.example: 3 months → after you paste it, your plan runs 3 more months.

pageSteps.title: How to use the key
pageSteps.body: Tap Copy key, open the shop app, go to More → Software fees → Renewal code, paste it and tap Renew. It works even without internet.
pageSteps.example: Paid until 30 November; after a 1-month key → paid until 30 December.

page.title: Chargers, covers etc.
page.body: Every counted item of the shop: chargers, cables, covers, glass, parts. Each item keeps how many pieces are here, its price and its whole history.
page.example: You have 25 Type-C cables and 8 iPhone 13 covers: both are items here, each with its own count and price.

stock.title: In stock
stock.body: All your items with how many pieces are in the shop now and the sale price. Tap one to see its page.
stock.example: Samsung 25W charger · 12 · Rs. 1,800 means 12 pieces are in the shop, sold at Rs. 1,800 each.

low.title: Low stock
low.body: Items whose count has come down to the "Reorder at" number or below. Time to buy more.
low.example: Reorder at is 5 and only 4 glass protectors are left → the glass protector shows here.

pending.title: Pending accessories
pending.body: The box, charger or other thing that belongs with a phone but is not handed over yet: the dealer still has to give it to you, or you promised it to a customer. Press Delivered when it is done.
pending.example: You sold an iPhone 13 and promised the box tomorrow → it shows "To customer" with tomorrow's date until you press Delivered.

filters.title: Filters
filters.body: Show only some items: one brand, one quality, or only the ones with no pieces left.
filters.example: Filters → brand Anker → the list shows only Anker chargers and cables.

reportsLink.title: Item reports
reportsLink.body: Opens the reports for items: what to order, stock value, fast and slow sellers, profit, dead stock and suppliers. Only the owner and manager see it.
reportsLink.example: Item reports → Low stock shows that Samsung chargers are short and the order would cost about Rs. 18,000.

brand.title: Brand
brand.body: The company that made the item. Type it once; next time it is offered in the list.

grade.title: Quality
grade.body: What kind of item it is: original, company (OEM), A-grade, copy / China or used. It helps you and the customer know what they are getting.
grade.example: Two iPhone chargers: original at Rs. 6,500 and copy at Rs. 1,200 — set the quality so they are never mixed up.

outOfStock.title: Out of stock
outOfStock.body: Shows only the items with no pieces left (0 or less).
outOfStock.example: Out of stock → "Infinix Hot 40 cover · 0" shows: none left, buy more.

name.title: Item name
name.body: What you call this item at the counter. It shows on bills, labels and in search.

similar.title: Similar items
similar.body: While you type a new name, the app shows items already in stock with a similar name, so you do not make the same item twice.
similar.example: You type "Type C cable" and the app shows "Type-C cable 1m · 18 pieces": use that one instead of making a new item.

category.title: Category
category.body: The kind of item: charger, cable, cover, glass, battery, repair part and so on. Reports and filters group items by it.
category.example: A 20,000 mAh power bank goes in "Power bank"; a screen for repairs goes in "Repair part".

price.title: Sale price
price.body: The price of one piece for a normal customer. The sale screen fills it in; you can still change it at the counter.
price.example: Sale price Rs. 1,800 → a customer buying 2 chargers is billed Rs. 3,600.

qty.title: In stock
qty.body: How many pieces are in the shop now: everything bought and added, minus everything sold, used in repairs or removed.
qty.example: Bought 20 cables, sold 7, 1 used in a repair → 12 in stock.

reorder.title: Reorder at
reorder.body: When the count comes down to this number or below, the item shows as low stock and goes on the order list.
reorder.example: Reorder at 5: with 5 or fewer Samsung chargers left, they show in Low stock.

openingQty.title: Opening qty
openingQty.body: Pieces of this item already in the shop before you started the app. Add them once; no money is paid now.
openingQty.example: 30 old covers on the shelf → Opening qty 30.

openingCost.title: Cost each
openingCost.body: What one of those old pieces cost you. Profit and stock value are worked out from it.
openingCost.example: 30 old covers bought at Rs. 250 each → Cost each 250; stock value Rs. 7,500.

color.title: Colour
color.body: The colour of this item, if you keep colours apart.
color.example: iPhone 13 silicone cover: Black and Blue as two items.

compatible.title: Fits (phone / model)
compatible.body: Which phones this item is for. It helps you find the right cover, glass or battery for a customer's phone.
compatible.example: Glass protector · Fits: Samsung A15, A25.

size.title: Size / variant
size.body: Size and details that tell two versions apart: size, capacity, connector, watts and colour, shown together.

capacity.title: Capacity
capacity.body: How much it holds: mAh for batteries and power banks, GB for memory cards and USBs.
capacity.example: Power bank 10,000 mAh; memory card 64 GB.

connector.title: Connector
connector.body: The plug type of a cable, charger or handsfree.

wattage.title: Watts
wattage.body: How fast a charger charges, written on it in W.
wattage.example: Samsung super fast charger 25W; normal charger 10W.

warrantyBy.title: Warranty by
warrantyBy.body: Who fixes or replaces it if it goes bad: your shop, or the supplier you bought it from.
warrantyBy.example: Anker power bank, warranty by Supplier: if it stops working you send it back to the dealer on Hall Road.

warrantyTerms.title: Warranty terms
warrantyTerms.body: Short conditions of the warranty, in your own words.
warrantyTerms.example: Replace only, not for water or broken pin.

piecesInBox.title: Pieces in one box
piecesInBox.body: How many pieces come in one box of this item. When you buy by the box, the app counts the pieces for you. Empty = the shop's usual box size.
piecesInBox.example: One box of glass protectors has 25 pieces → buying 2 boxes adds 50 pieces.

piecesInCarton.title: Pieces in one carton
piecesInCarton.body: How many pieces come in one carton of this item. Buying by the carton is counted in pieces. Empty = the shop's usual carton size.
piecesInCarton.example: One carton of cables has 200 pieces → 1 carton adds 200 pieces to stock.

pricing.title: Pricing
pricing.body: Fixed price: you type the sale price yourself. Markup on cost: the app sets the sale price from the buying price plus your %, again after every purchase.
pricing.example: Markup 40% and the charger costs Rs. 500 → sale price Rs. 700. Next stock costs Rs. 550 → Rs. 770.

markupPct.title: Markup %
markupPct.body: How much % to add on the average buying price to get the sale price. The app rounds it to the nearest Rs. 10.
markupPct.example: Cost Rs. 340, markup 50% → 510 → sale price Rs. 510.

wholesale.title: Wholesale price
wholesale.body: A lower price for dealers and wholesale customers. When the customer on the sale is marked "Dealer / wholesale", this price fills in by itself.
wholesale.example: Retail Rs. 1,800, wholesale Rs. 1,450: a shopkeeper from Hafeez Centre marked wholesale gets Rs. 1,450.

minPrice.title: Minimum sale price
minPrice.body: The lowest price staff may sell at. Below it, the owner or manager must allow the sale. Below the buying price only the owner or manager can sell.
minPrice.example: Minimum Rs. 1,500: a salesman typing Rs. 1,400 needs the manager's OK.

promo.title: Promo price
promo.body: A special offer price. Between the promo dates it fills in on the sale screen for everyone, before the normal or wholesale price.
promo.example: Eid offer: cover Rs. 999 instead of Rs. 1,299 from 5 to 12 April.

promoDates.title: Promo from / till
promoDates.body: The first and last day of the promo price. Empty "from" = starts now; empty "till" = no end.
promoDates.example: From 5 April till 12 April: on 13 April the price goes back to Rs. 1,299.

taxRate.title: GST %
taxRate.body: Optional. When a sale is taxed, this item is taxed at its own GST % instead of the bill's rate; phones and items without a rate take the bill's rate. A sale without tax stays without tax.
taxRate.example: Bill taxed at 18%: phone Rs. 10,000 → Rs. 1,800; two cables at Rs. 1,000 with GST 5% → Rs. 100. Bill tax Rs. 1,900.

taxIncl.title: Price includes tax
taxIncl.body: On: the sale price already has the tax inside it. Off: the tax is on top of the sale price.
taxIncl.example: Price Rs. 1,180 with 18% included → Rs. 1,000 price + Rs. 180 tax.

maxStock.title: Maximum stock
maxStock.body: The most pieces you want to keep. The order list suggests buying up to this number. Empty = three times "Reorder at".
maxStock.example: Maximum 30, 6 left → the order list suggests 24 pieces.

location.title: Shelf / rack
location.body: Where this item is kept in the shop, so anyone can find it fast.

showInSale.title: Show on the sale screen
showInSale.body: Off: the item stays in stock but is not offered on the sale screen. Use it for parts you only use in repairs.
showInSale.example: Infinix Hot 40 screen kept for repairs → turn it off so it does not show in sales.

supplierSkus.title: Supplier codes
supplierSkus.body: The code each dealer uses for this item on his bill. When you type or scan that code, the app finds this item.
supplierSkus.example: The Hall Road dealer calls it "SC-25W": save it here and his bill lines match this charger.

supplierSku.title: Supplier's code
supplierSku.body: The code written for this item on that dealer's bill or box.

detail.title: Item's page
detail.body: Everything about one item: how many are here, prices, what it cost, its purchase batches and every movement in and out.
detail.example: Samsung 25W charger: 12 in stock, sells for Rs. 1,800, cost Rs. 1,200 each, last bought from Ali Traders.

adjust.title: Adjust stock
adjust.body: Correct the count by hand when it does not match the shelf: add found pieces or remove damaged / lost ones. A reason is required and the change stays in the history.
adjust.example: App says 12, shelf has 10 because 2 broke → adjust −2, reason "damaged".

delta.title: Change (+/−)
delta.body: How many pieces to add (+) or remove (−).
delta.example: −2 for two broken covers; +3 for three cables found in the store room.

adjustCost.title: Cost each
adjustCost.body: Only when adding pieces: what one added piece cost. Empty = the current average cost.
adjustCost.example: +3 cables, cost each Rs. 150 → the stock value goes up by Rs. 450.

reason.title: Reason
reason.body: Why the count is changed. It is kept with the change so the owner can see it later.
reason.example: Damaged in rain; count correction after stock check.

labels.title: Print sticker
labels.body: Prints barcode stickers for this item, to stick on the pieces or the shelf. Scanning a sticker finds the item at once.
labels.example: Print 20 stickers for the new cables; at the sale, scan one and the cable is added.

makeUnit.title: Track one by serial
makeUnit.body: For counted watches and tablets: takes one piece out of the count and makes it a separate unit with its own serial, history, barcode and price.
makeUnit.example: 5 smart watches counted together; one is sold with a warranty card → make it a unit so its serial is on record.

avgCost.title: Average cost
avgCost.body: The average buying price of one piece, worked out from every purchase at its own price. Only the owner and manager see it.
avgCost.example: 10 bought at Rs. 400 and 10 at Rs. 500 → average cost Rs. 450.

profitEach.title: Profit each
profitEach.body: Sale price minus average cost, for one piece; the % is that profit compared with the cost.
profitEach.example: Sells for Rs. 1,800, average cost Rs. 1,200 → profit Rs. 600 each, 50%.

stockValue.title: Stock value
stockValue.body: What the pieces in the shop cost you: pieces in stock × average cost.

batches.title: Purchase batches
batches.body: Every purchase of this item with its own buying price, and how many of it are still left. Sales take the oldest batch first.
batches.example: Batch 1: 20 at Rs. 400, 0 left; batch 2: 20 at Rs. 450, 12 left → the next sale comes from batch 2.

timeline.title: History
timeline.body: Every movement of this item: bought, sold, returned, used in a repair, adjusted, and price changes, with the date and the count after it.
timeline.example: 3 May sold 2 to Bilal (= 10 left); 5 May price changed 1,800 → 1,700.

page.title: Item reports
page.body: Reports for chargers, covers and other counted items: what to order, what the stock is worth, what sells, what profit it made, what is lying unsold, and whom you buy from.
page.example: Check "Dead stock" every month to find covers that have not sold for 60 days.

low.title: Low stock (order list)
low.body: Items at or below "Reorder at", grouped by the supplier you last bought each from, with how many to order.
low.example: Ali Traders: Samsung charger 3 left / 5, order 12; Type-C cable 2 left / 5, order 13.

suggest.title: Order quantity
suggest.body: How many to order: up to the item's maximum stock (or three times "Reorder at" if no maximum is set), minus what is left.
suggest.example: Reorder at 5, no maximum, 3 left → order 15 − 3 = 12.

estimate.title: Estimated cost
estimate.body: About how much this supplier's order will cost: order quantity × the item's average cost, added up.

value.title: Stock value
value.body: What all items in the shop are worth now: at cost (what you paid) and at sale price, and the profit you expect if all of it sells.
value.example: At cost Rs. 2,40,000, at sale price Rs. 3,50,000 → expected profit Rs. 1,10,000.

atCost.title: At cost
atCost.body: Pieces in stock × average cost, for every item, added up.

atRetail.title: At sale price
atRetail.body: Pieces in stock × sale price, for every item, added up.

expected.title: Expected profit
expected.body: At sale price minus at cost: the profit if every piece sells at its full price.

byCategory.title: By category
byCategory.body: The same stock value split by category: how many items and pieces, at cost (big number) and at sale price (small number).
byCategory.example: Covers: 12 items · 100 pieces · Rs. 25,000 at cost · Rs. 50,000 at sale price.

movers.title: Fast / slow
movers.body: Which items sold the most pieces in the chosen days, and which items in stock sold the least.
movers.example: Last 30 days: Type-C cable sold 60 (fast); Nokia 105 cover sold 0 with 15 in stock (slow).

fast.title: Fast movers
fast.body: The 20 items that sold the most pieces in these days (returns not counted), with what is left, the profit, and how many days the stock will last at this speed.
fast.example: Sold 60 cables in 30 days = 2 a day; 20 left → about 10 days of stock.

slow.title: Slow movers
slow.body: Items that are in stock but sold the fewest pieces in these days. Think about a discount or stop buying them.
slow.example: Nokia 105 cover: 15 in stock, sold 0 in 30 days.

profit.title: Profit
profit.body: Profit on items sold in the chosen days: what they sold for minus what they cost, by category or by brand. Returned pieces and cancelled bills are left out.
profit.example: Chargers: 40 sold for Rs. 72,000, cost Rs. 48,000 → profit Rs. 24,000.

group.title: By category / by brand
group.body: Choose how the profit is grouped: by kind of item, or by the company that made it.
group.example: By brand: Anker Rs. 9,000, Samsung Rs. 15,000.

dead.title: Dead stock
dead.body: Items in stock that have not sold for the number of days you choose (or never sold), the costliest first, with the money stuck in them at cost.
dead.example: Not sold for 60 days: 20 old Infinix covers × Rs. 200 = Rs. 4,000 stuck.

notSoldFor.title: Not sold for (days)
notSoldFor.body: How many days without a sale counts as dead stock.
notSoldFor.example: 60 → items whose last sale was more than 60 days ago, or that never sold.

suppliers.title: Suppliers
suppliers.body: How much of these items you bought from each supplier in the chosen days: bills, pieces and amount. Returned lines are left out.

field.title: Which price
field.body: Choose which price to change on many items at once: sale price, wholesale price or minimum price.
field.example: Dollar went up: raise the sale price of all chargers by 10%.

pct.title: Change by %
pct.body: Raise (+) or lower (−) the chosen price by this %.

amount.title: Or by amount
amount.body: Add (+) or take off (−) a fixed number of rupees from the chosen price. If you fill both, the % is applied first, then the amount.

scope.title: Which items
scope.body: All items, or only one category. Every change is kept in each item's history.
scope.example: Category "Glass protector" → only glass prices change.

page.title: Repairs
page.body: Every phone left with you for repair, and where each job is: taken in, being fixed, ready or given back. Ready ones come first so you can call the customer.
page.example: Samsung A54 screen change · ready → call Usman to collect it.

view.title: Open / All
view.body: Open: jobs not given back yet. All: also the ones already given back or returned without repair.
view.example: Open shows 6 phones still in the shop; All also shows last month's finished jobs.

new.title: Take a phone in
new.body: Write whose phone it is, which phone, what is wrong, the likely cost and when it will be ready. Saving prints a slip for the customer.
new.example: Ahmed's Infinix Hot 40, charging problem, likely Rs. 1,500, ready tomorrow → slip printed with job no. R-0042.

device.title: Phone name
device.body: Brand, model and colour of the phone left for repair, so it is never mixed up with another.

faults.title: What is the problem?
faults.body: Tap every fault the customer tells you. They are printed on the slip.

faultText.title: Other problem
faultText.body: A fault that is not in the list, in your own words.

estimate.title: Likely cost
estimate.body: The price you tell the customer before the repair. It is printed on the slip; the real bill is made when it is fixed.
estimate.example: Likely Rs. 4,500 for an A54 screen; the final bill came to Rs. 4,800.

advance.title: Advance taken
advance.body: Money the customer pays now, before the repair. It goes into the galla and is taken off the bill when the phone is given back.
advance.example: Bill Rs. 4,800, advance Rs. 2,000 → Rs. 2,800 left to take.

promised.title: Ready by
promised.body: The day you promise the phone will be ready. After this day the job shows as late.
promised.example: Promised Friday, still not fixed on Saturday → the job turns red as late.

received.title: Received with the phone
received.body: Things the customer left with the phone. They are printed on the slip so you give all of them back.
received.example: SIM + memory card + cover kept with the phone.

job.title: Repair job
job.body: One repair: the customer, the faults, where the job is, the bill and every step with who did it.
job.example: R-0042 · Ahmed · Infinix Hot 40 · being fixed · bill Rs. 1,500, advance Rs. 500.

stages.title: Repair stages
stages.body: The four steps of every repair: taken in → being fixed → ready → given back. The dark bars show how far this job has come.
stages.example: Three bars dark = ready; call the customer.

steps.title: Moving the job on
steps.body: "It is fixed" opens the bill (parts and work charge) and marks the phone ready. "Start fixing" and "Waiting for parts" only change the stage; "Can't fix" closes it without a repair.
steps.example: Screen ordered from Hall Road → Waiting for parts; screen fitted → It is fixed, bill Rs. 4,800.

bill.title: Repair bill
bill.body: Parts used plus the work charge make the total; the advance is taken off and the rest is what to take from the customer. Before the bill is made, the likely cost is shown.
bill.example: Screen Rs. 3,800 + work Rs. 1,000 = Rs. 4,800; advance Rs. 2,000 → left Rs. 2,800.

labour.title: Work charge
labour.body: What you charge for your work, on top of the parts. It is repair income.
labour.example: Battery Rs. 2,500 + work charge Rs. 500 → bill Rs. 3,000.

total.title: Total
total.body: Parts plus work charge: the full bill for this repair.

left.title: Left to take
left.body: What the customer still has to pay: the total minus the advance.

paid.title: Paid
paid.body: Everything the customer paid for this repair: the advance plus what was taken when the phone was given back. Anything not paid is on his khata.
paid.example: Advance Rs. 2,000 + Rs. 2,000 at hand-over = Rs. 4,000 paid; Rs. 800 on khata.

history.title: History
history.body: Every step of this job with the date and who did it.
history.example: 2 May taken in (Ali) · 3 May waiting for parts · 4 May ready (Bilal).

part.title: Part
part.body: A part put in the phone. Pick it from your stock below, or type its name.

partPrice.title: Part price
partPrice.body: What you charge the customer for one of this part.

fromStock.title: Parts from stock
fromStock.body: Tap an item from your stock to add it as a part (the number is how many you have). When the phone is given back, that piece leaves your stock at its cost.
fromStock.example: + Hot 40 battery (4) → added at Rs. 2,500; on hand-over the stock goes to 3.

outsideCost.title: Paid to outside technician
outsideCost.body: For the shop's own phone: what you paid another technician to fix it. It is added to that phone's cost.
outsideCost.example: Your iPhone 11 cost Rs. 70,000; outside repair Rs. 3,000 → its cost becomes Rs. 73,000.

page.title: Installments (qist)
page.body: Every sale on monthly installments: who pays how much and when. Choose a view to see what is due today, what is late, what is running or finished.
page.example: Kamran bought a Samsung A15 on 6 qist of Rs. 6,000; he shows here until the last one is paid.

today.title: Due today
today.body: Running plans whose next installment is due today or is already past due.
today.example: Kamran's qist was due on the 10th; today is the 10th → he shows here.

overdue.title: Late
overdue.body: Running plans with at least one installment whose date has passed without full payment.
overdue.example: Due on the 5th, today is the 12th and nothing paid → late by 7 days.

active.title: Running
active.body: All plans that still have money left to pay.

closed.title: Finished
closed.example: All 6 installments of Rs. 6,000 received → finished.

plan.title: Installment plan
plan.body: One customer's qist plan: the bill, what is paid and left, each month's date and amount, and the guarantor.
plan.example: Samsung A15 for Rs. 46,000: advance Rs. 10,000, then 6 × Rs. 6,000 on the 10th of each month.

total.title: Total
total.body: The full amount of the bill sold on installments.
total.example: Samsung A15 on qist for Rs. 46,000.

paid.title: Paid
paid.body: Everything received on this bill so far: the advance plus the installments.

remaining.title: Left
remaining.body: What is still to be received: total minus paid.

planLine.title: The plan
planLine.body: The advance paid at the sale, how many monthly installments of how much, and on which day of the month they are due.
planLine.example: Advance Rs. 10,000 · 6 × Rs. 6,000 · day 10 of each month.

collect.title: Take installment
collect.body: Receive this month's money. It is a normal payment on the bill: the galla or account goes up and what is left goes down.
collect.example: Kamran pays Rs. 6,000 by Easypaisa → left goes from Rs. 24,000 to Rs. 18,000.

remind.title: Remind on WhatsApp
remind.body: Sends the customer a WhatsApp message with the installment due. If WhatsApp sending is not set up, WhatsApp opens with the message ready and you tap send.
remind.example: A day before the 10th, remind Kamran: "Rs. 6,000 qist due on 10 June".

schedule.title: Schedule
schedule.body: Every installment with its date and amount and whether it is paid, part paid, due today, late or still to come.
schedule.example: 10 May Rs. 6,000 Paid · 10 June Rs. 6,000 Part (Rs. 2,000 received) · 10 July Due.

guarantor.title: Customer and guarantor
guarantor.body: Who pays the installments, and the zamin who promised to pay if the customer does not. Call or WhatsApp them from here.

nextDue.title: Next due
nextDue.body: The date of the next installment not yet fully paid.

amount.title: Amount
amount.body: How much the customer pays now. It starts at the next installment; you can take less or more, up to what is left.
amount.example: Installment Rs. 6,000, he brings Rs. 4,000 → write 4,000; that month shows as part paid.

page.title: Expenses
page.body: Money the shop spends that is not stock: rent, bills, salaries, tea, transport. Each expense comes out of the galla; profit after expenses takes it away. Close the day here too.
page.example: Electricity bill Rs. 8,000 and tea Rs. 300 today → Rs. 8,300 of expenses.

dayClose.title: Close the day
dayClose.body: At night, count the cash in the galla and write it. The app compares it with what should be there and saves the difference. A day can be closed once.
dayClose.example: App expects Rs. 52,000, you count Rs. 51,500 → Rs. 500 short is saved for the day.

opening.title: Opening cash
opening.body: Cash in the galla when the day started: the galla balance at the end of yesterday.
opening.example: Last night Rs. 20,000 was left in the galla → today's opening is Rs. 20,000.

in.title: Cash in
in.body: All cash that came into the galla today: sales, money received from people, advances and so on.
in.example: Sales Rs. 35,000 + udhaar received Rs. 5,000 = Rs. 40,000 in.

out.title: Cash out
out.body: All cash that left the galla today: expenses, stock paid in cash, payments to dealers, refunds.
out.example: Expenses Rs. 3,000 + paid a dealer Rs. 5,000 = Rs. 8,000 out.

expected.title: Expected in drawer
expected.body: What should be in the galla now: opening cash + cash in − cash out.

counted.title: Counted cash
counted.body: The cash you actually count in the galla now, notes and coins.

difference.title: Difference
difference.body: Counted minus expected. Minus means cash is short; plus means there is extra.

category.title: Category
category.body: What the money was spent on. Reports add expenses up by category.

categories.title: Categories
categories.body: The list of expense kinds. Built-in ones stay; your own ones can be renamed or removed.
categories.example: Add "Generator fuel" as your own category.

categoryName.title: Category name
categoryName.body: The name of your own expense category.

description.title: Details
description.body: A few words on what exactly it was, so you remember later.
description.example: June electricity bill; Eid bonus for Ali.

all.title: All
all.body: Everyone in your khata book: customers, dealers, other shops and technicians.

customer.title: Customers
customer.body: People who buy from you, or sell you their own used phone.

supplier.title: Dealers
supplier.body: Wholesalers and distributors you buy stock from.

shop.title: Other shops
shop.body: Other mobile shops you buy from, sell to or lend phones to.
shop.example: Madina Mobiles next door took 2 phones on loan → other shop.

balance.title: With balance
balance.body: Only people whose khata is not clear: they owe you, or you owe them.
balance.example: Bilal owes Rs. 12,000 and you owe Ali Traders Rs. 50,000 → both show here.

detail.title: Person's khata
detail.body: One person's page: the balance, money in and out, len-den, phones bought from or sold to them, and the full khata history.
detail.example: Bilal: will get Rs. 12,000; sold him 2 phones; khata history shows every bill and payment.

balance.title: Balance
balance.body: The whole khata in one number: every bill, payment, len-den and opening balance with this person. "I will get" means he owes you; "I have to give" means you owe him.
balance.example: Sold him a phone for Rs. 40,000, he paid Rs. 28,000 → I will get Rs. 12,000.

unitsReceivable.title: They owe (phones)
unitsReceivable.body: Of the balance, what is still unpaid on phones you sold to this person, added up phone by phone.
unitsReceivable.example: Sold him an A15 (Rs. 8,000 left) and a Redmi (Rs. 4,000 left) → Rs. 12,000.

unitsPayable.title: We owe (phones)
unitsPayable.body: Of the balance, what you still have to pay on phones you bought from this person.
unitsPayable.example: Bought an iPhone 12 from him for Rs. 85,000, paid Rs. 60,000 → Rs. 25,000.

other.title: Other / opening
other.body: The part of the balance that is not on phones: the opening balance from your old diary, items like chargers and covers, len-den and adjustments.
other.example: Balance Rs. 15,000, phones Rs. 12,000 → other Rs. 3,000 (old diary udhaar).

kinds.title: Type
kinds.body: What this person is to the shop: customer, dealer, other shop or technician. One person can be more than one.
kinds.example: Madina Mobiles: other shop and dealer, because you buy from them and sell to them.

gotMoney.title: Money received
gotMoney.body: Money this person gives you to pay what he owes on his bills. His khata goes down. For a loan with no bill, use Len-den below.
gotMoney.example: Bilal owes Rs. 12,000 and pays Rs. 5,000 → he now owes Rs. 7,000.

gaveMoney.title: Money paid
gaveMoney.body: Money you pay this person for what you owe on your purchases from him. What you owe goes down. For a loan with no bill, use Len-den below.
gaveMoney.example: You owe Ali Traders Rs. 50,000 and pay Rs. 20,000 → you now owe Rs. 30,000.

whatsapp.title: WhatsApp
whatsapp.body: A separate WhatsApp number, if the person has one different from his mobile number.

city.title: City
city.body: The city the person or shop is in. Useful for dealers from other cities.

statement.title: Khata history
statement.body: Every entry in this person's khata, newest first, with the balance after it. Cancelled entries are struck through. Download it to send to him.

wholesale.title: Dealer / wholesale customer
wholesale.body: On: when you sell items to this person, the item's wholesale price fills in instead of the normal price.
wholesale.example: Charger retail Rs. 1,800, wholesale Rs. 1,450 → this dealer is billed Rs. 1,450.

journey.title: Journey
journey.body: This person's whole story with the shop: phones sold and bought, money both ways, returns, profit and balance. Choose a day to see it as it was then. Owner and manager only.
journey.example: Since Jan 2025: sold him 4 phones, bought 2, received Rs. 1,60,000, balance Rs. 12,000.

firstLast.title: First / last dealing
firstLast.body: The first and the latest day of any bill, payment or return with this person.

soldTo.title: Sold to them
soldTo.body: Phones sold to this person (returned ones not counted), with the number of bills and their value after returns.

boughtFrom.title: Bought from them
boughtFrom.body: Phones you bought from this person (returned ones not counted), with the number of bills and their value.

received.title: Money received
received.body: All money this person gave you: at the counter when the bill was made, plus payments he brought later.
received.example: At counter Rs. 1,20,000 · later Rs. 40,000 → Rs. 1,60,000.

paid.title: Money paid
paid.body: All money you gave this person: at the counter when you bought, plus payments made later.
paid.example: At counter Rs. 70,000 · later Rs. 25,000 → Rs. 95,000.

profitOnSales.title: Profit on sales
profitOnSales.body: On phones sold to this person (not returned): sale price minus the phone's cost, added up.
profitOnSales.example: Sold an A15 for Rs. 46,000 that cost Rs. 41,000 → Rs. 5,000 profit.

profitOnSourced.title: Profit on phones from them
profitOnSourced.body: Phones you bought from this person and later sold to anyone: how many are sold and the profit they made.
profitOnSourced.example: Bought 2 iPhones from him; 1 sold for Rs. 8,000 more than its cost → 1 sold, Rs. 8,000.

returns.title: Returns
returns.body: How many times this person returned a phone to you, or you returned one to him, the amount, and how much was refunded to him.
returns.example: 1 return of Rs. 40,000; refunded Rs. 38,000 (shop kept Rs. 2,000).

balance.title: Balance
balance.body: The khata balance on the chosen day (today if none): he owes you, you owe him, or settled.
balance.example: As of 30 June: he owes Rs. 20,000; today he owes Rs. 12,000.

timeline.title: Timeline
timeline.body: Every bill, payment and return with this person, in order. Tap one to open it.
timeline.example: 3 Jan sale S-0102 Rs. 46,000 · 10 Jan received Rs. 10,000.

units.title: Phones
units.body: Every phone bought from or sold to this person: the agreed price, what is paid and what is still to pay or to get. Tap a phone to open it; the button takes a payment for that one phone.
units.example: iPhone 12 bought for Rs. 85,000 · paid Rs. 60,000 · still to pay Rs. 25,000.

title.title: Len-den
title.body: Money given to or taken from this person with no bill, like a loan. It is part of the same khata, and the number shows how much of it is still open.
title.example: Lent Bilal Rs. 10,000, he returned Rs. 4,000 → len-den open Rs. 6,000 (he owes).

due.title: Return date
due.body: The earliest promised return date among the open len-den entries: when it is due, how many days late, and when he was last reminded.
due.example: Promised back on 1 June, today 4 June → 3 days late.

remind.title: Send reminder
remind.body: Sends this person a WhatsApp message about the money he owes. If automatic sending is not set up, WhatsApp opens with the message ready. The night job also reminds when it is due, at most every 3 days, if udhaar reminders are on.
remind.example: Bilal is 3 days late → Send reminder: "Rs. 6,000 was due back on 1 June".

lent.title: Given
lent.body: All len-den money the shop has given this person (cancelled entries left out).
lent.example: Gave Rs. 10,000 in March and Rs. 5,000 in May → Rs. 15,000.

borrowed.title: Taken
borrowed.body: All len-den money the shop has taken from this person, including loans he paid back (cancelled entries left out).
borrowed.example: He returned Rs. 4,000 of the loan → Rs. 4,000 taken.

fromBills.title: From bills
fromBills.body: The rest of the khata balance that comes from bills and payments, not from len-den: balance minus open len-den.
fromBills.example: Balance Rs. 18,000, len-den open Rs. 6,000 → from bills Rs. 12,000.

give.title: Gave money (len-den)
give.body: Write money the shop gives this person with no bill, like a loan. It goes on his khata; you can add a return date.
give.example: Lent Bilal Rs. 10,000 from the galla, to be returned on 1 June.

take.title: Took money (len-den)
take.body: Write money the shop takes from this person with no bill: a loan he gives you, or his loan coming back.
take.example: Madina Mobiles lent you Rs. 50,000 for a week → took money Rs. 50,000.

settle.title: Adjust against bills
settle.body: Money already given in advance or as len-den can pay open bills: his money goes on his unpaid sale bills, the shop's money on its unpaid purchase bills to him, oldest first. The khata total does not change; only the bills show as paid.
settle.example: He gave Rs. 10,000 len-den and has an unpaid bill of Rs. 8,000 → adjust: the bill becomes paid, Rs. 2,000 stays as len-den.

entries.title: Len-den entries
entries.body: The latest len-den entries with this person: given (−) or taken (+), the date and note. Cancelled ones are struck through. Tap the date line to set or change a return date.

dueDate.title: Return date
dueDate.body: The day the money should come back. Leave empty for no date. After this day the entry shows as late and reminders can go out.
dueDate.example: Set 15 June; on 16 June it shows "1 day late".

category.title: Type of device
category.body: Mobile, tablet or smart watch. Each type asks only its own things: a watch has no storage, a Wi-Fi tablet has no IMEI.
category.example: Buying an iPad: tap Tablet, then choose Wi-Fi only or Wi-Fi + SIM.

connection.title: Does it take a SIM?
connection.body: A tablet or watch with a SIM slot is checked like a phone: it needs its IMEI and PTA status. Without a SIM it is found by its serial number.
connection.example: Galaxy Tab A9 Wi-Fi only → no IMEI, write the serial. Galaxy Tab A9 LTE → Wi-Fi + SIM, write the IMEI.

serial.title: Serial number
serial.body: The maker's own number for this one unit, on the box or in Settings → About. For a device with no SIM it is its identity: the app checks it against your old stock the same way as an IMEI.
serial.example: Apple Watch SE GPS: Settings → General → About → Serial "F4KXJ2Q1HQ".

imei2.title: IMEI 2
imei2.body: A dual-SIM phone has a second IMEI, one for each SIM slot. Dial *#06# to see both. Scanning the box fills IMEI 1 first, then IMEI 2.
imei2.example: Infinix Hot 40: *#06# shows 35xxxxxxxxxxxx1 and 35xxxxxxxxxxxx9 → the second one goes here.

brand.title: Brand
brand.body: The company that made it. Tap one; if it is not in the list, "New brand" adds it for next time too.
brand.example: Samsung, Infinix, Apple. A new brand like "Itel" is added once and stays in the list.

model.title: Model
model.body: The exact model of that brand. Type a few letters to find it. Choosing a model also fills the spec sheet if the app already knows it.
model.example: Brand Samsung, type "A15" → tap Galaxy A15.

watchSize.title: Case size
watchSize.body: The width of the watch body in millimetres, written on the box or the back. The same model comes in more than one size and price.
watchSize.example: Apple Watch Series 9: 41mm or 45mm — the 45mm usually sells for Rs. 8,000–10,000 more.

storage.title: Storage
storage.body: How much the phone can hold (ROM), in GB. It changes the price a lot, so the rate suggestion matches it too. "New size" adds a missing one.
storage.example: iPhone 13 128GB vs 256GB: same phone, about Rs. 15,000 apart.

colour.title: Colour
colour.body: The colour of this unit. It helps to find the right phone on the shelf and is printed on the sticker. Typing a colour that already exists simply picks it.
colour.example: Two Galaxy A15 in stock: one Blue Black, one Light Blue — the customer wants light blue.

condition.title: Condition
condition.body: Box pack: new and sealed. Open box: new but the seal is opened. Used: someone has used it. Patched (phones only): a part or the board has been changed — write what was done.
condition.example: Customer sells his 1-year-old Galaxy A54 → Used. Dealer's sealed Infinix Hot 40 → Box pack.

patch.title: Patch details
patch.body: What was changed inside a patched phone. It stays in the phone's history so you can tell the next buyer honestly.
patch.example: "Board changed, original IMEI on box does not match" or "China screen fitted".

battery.title: Battery health %
battery.body: How strong the battery still is compared with new (100%). Find it in Settings → Battery. Leave empty if the device does not show it.
battery.example: Used iPad 9th gen showing 86% → write 86. Below 80% buyers usually ask for less.

pta.title: PTA status
pta.body: PTA approved: registered in Pakistan, any SIM works for ever. Non-PTA: not registered — a Pakistani SIM works only for a limited time, then the phone is blocked unless PTA tax is paid. JV: made to work through a "jugaad" (patched or registered on another IMEI) — it also has limited SIM time and is the riskiest to buy.
pta.example: iPhone 13 from Dubai, no tax paid, SIM works 2 more months → Non-PTA, SIM time 2. JV iPhone 12 → JV, and tell the buyer.

simTime.title: SIM time (months)
simTime.body: For a Non-PTA or JV phone: how many more months a Pakistani SIM will keep working in it. It must be filled, and the sale screen warns the buyer.
simTime.example: Non-PTA Pixel 7 with about 2 months left → write 2. After that the SIM stops until PTA tax is paid.

warrantyMonths.title: Warranty (months)
warrantyMonths.body: How many months of warranty this unit has. From a dealer it starts at 12, from a customer at 0. It is printed on the sale receipt.
warrantyMonths.example: Box-pack Galaxy A15 with 12 months company warranty → 12. Used phone from a customer → 0.

lock.title: Lock check
lock.body: Before buying a used device, make sure no account lock is left (iCloud, Google / FRP, Samsung, paired watch). A device with a lock "Still on" cannot be bought or sold. Tablets and watches always need it; phones when the shop has turned it on.
lock.example: Used iPad: Find My is still on → mark iCloud "Still on" — the app will not let you buy it until the seller removes it.

activation.title: iCloud / activation lock
activation.body: On Apple devices: the owner's Apple ID is still on it (Find My). After a reset it asks for that ID, so nobody else can use it.
activation.example: iPhone 11 asks "Apple ID of the owner" after reset → Still on. Seller signs out of iCloud in front of you → Cleared.

frp.title: Google / FRP lock
frp.body: On Android: after a factory reset the phone asks for the last Google account. If the seller has not removed it, the next buyer is stuck.
frp.example: Galaxy A32 shows "Verify your account" after reset → Still on. Seller removes the Google account first → Cleared.

account.title: Samsung / account lock
account.body: A maker's own account lock (Samsung account, Xiaomi Mi account and so on) that also asks for the old owner after a reset.
account.example: Redmi Note 12 asks for the Mi account password → Still on.

paired.title: Paired-device lock
paired.body: A smart watch still joined to the old owner's phone. Until it is unpaired, it cannot be set up with a new phone.
paired.example: Apple Watch still paired to the seller's iPhone → Still on. He unpairs it in the Watch app → Cleared.

carrier.title: Carrier lock
carrier.body: Some phones from the USA or UK work only with one company's SIM (for example AT&T). "Factory unlocked" phones take any SIM.
carrier.example: iPhone 12 from the US shows "SIM not supported" with a Jazz SIM → carrier lock Still on.

modelNumber.title: Model number
modelNumber.body: The maker's code for the exact version, in Settings → About or on the box. It tells you which country / variant it is.
modelNumber.example: Galaxy A15 "SM-A155F/DS" — DS means dual SIM.

ram.title: RAM (GB)
ram.body: The working memory, which makes the phone fast. It is different from storage. Shown on the box as "8GB + 256GB" (the first is RAM).

grade.title: Grade
grade.body: How clean a used unit is, so the price fits. Used A: almost like new. Used B: marks or small faults. Refurbished: repaired / reconditioned. Copy / China: not the original brand. The owner can change the list.
grade.example: Galaxy S21 with no scratch → Used A, Rs. 85,000. Same phone with a cracked back → Used B, Rs. 72,000.

warrantyBy.title: Warranty by
warrantyBy.body: Who honours the warranty: the shop itself, the dealer you bought from, or the company (official service centre).
warrantyBy.example: Box-pack Galaxy A15 → Company (Samsung service centre). Used iPhone with your 1-month check warranty → Shop.

specs.title: Spec sheet
specs.body: The phone's features: screen, battery, camera and so on. Optional. Once filled for a model, the next unit of the same model is filled by itself.
specs.example: Fill Galaxy A15 once (6.5", 5000 mAh, 50 MP) → the next A15 you buy already has it.

accessoriesBuy.title: What came with it
accessoriesBuy.body: For each thing (box, charger, cable…): No, Yes now (you got it), or Yes later (the seller still has to give it — set the day). Later items show as pending on the phone.
accessoriesBuy.example: Customer sells iPhone 13 with box, charger to bring tomorrow → Box: Yes now; Charger: Yes later, tomorrow.

accessoriesSell.title: What goes with it
accessoriesSell.body: For each thing: No, Yes now (given at the counter), or Yes later (the shop gives it later — set the day). It is printed on the receipt so nobody argues later.
accessoriesSell.example: Galaxy A15 sold, cover given now, original charger next week → Charger: Yes later.

status.title: Where it is now
status.body: In stock, On loan (at another shop), With customer (for approval), Sold, In repair, Faulty, or Returned to supplier. It changes by itself with every sale, loan or repair.
status.example: You gave the phone to Ali Mobiles on amanat → status "On loan" until it comes back or they keep it.

verification.title: ID check status
verification.body: No check needed: a box-pack phone from a dealer. ID check pending: a phone bought from a person whose papers are not complete. ID checked: complete, it can be sold. Stolen? Do not sell: eGadget flagged it — it cannot be sold.
verification.example: Bought a used Galaxy A54 from a walk-in, no CNIC photo yet → "ID check pending".

badges.title: Labels on this phone
badges.body: Quick facts in one row: condition, grade, PTA, lock check, ID check, and "Cycle N" when the shop has bought this same phone N times.
badges.example: iPhone 13 · Used · Used A · Non-PTA · Locks cleared · Cycle 2 = you bought it, sold it, and bought it back.

retype.title: Change type
retype.body: Moves a unit saved under the wrong type (phone / tablet / watch). Press Check first: it lists anything that does not fit. History, IMEI / serial, barcode and money stay the same.
retype.example: A Galaxy Tab was saved as a Mobile → Change to Tablet → Check → Apply.

os.title: OS / version
os.body: The software the device runs and its version, in Settings → About.

chipset.title: Processor / chipset
chipset.body: The phone's "engine". A better chipset means faster games and apps.
chipset.example: Helio G99, Snapdragon 8 Gen 2, Apple A15.

display_in.title: Display size
display_in.body: Screen size in inches, measured corner to corner.

display_type.title: Display type
display_type.body: The kind of screen. AMOLED / OLED have deeper colours and cost more to replace than LCD / IPS.
display_type.example: Galaxy A15: Super AMOLED; Redmi A3: IPS LCD.

resolution.title: Resolution
resolution.body: How sharp the screen is, in dots across × down. More dots = sharper picture.

refresh_hz.title: Refresh rate (Hz)
refresh_hz.body: How many times a second the screen redraws. 90 or 120 Hz feels smoother than 60 Hz.

battery_mah.title: Battery (mAh)
battery_mah.body: The battery size from the box. A bigger number usually lasts longer.
battery_mah.example: 5000 mAh lasts about a full day of normal use.

expandable.title: microSD slot
expandable.body: Yes if a memory card can be added for more space.
expandable.example: Galaxy A15: Yes (up to 1TB). iPhone: No.

sim_type.title: SIM type
sim_type.body: Nano is the normal small card. eSIM is built in, with no card; a Pakistani eSIM must be issued by the network.
sim_type.example: iPhone 14 (US): eSIM only — no slot for a Jazz card.

camera_rear_mp.title: Rear camera (MP)
camera_rear_mp.body: Main back camera megapixels (the biggest one).

stylus_support.title: Stylus / pencil support
stylus_support.body: Yes if the tablet works with a pen.

unlock.title: Unlock
unlock.body: How the screen opens: fingerprint, face, both, or only a PIN.

port.title: Charging port
port.body: The socket for the charger cable, so the right cable is given.

fast_charge_w.title: Fast charge (W)
fast_charge_w.body: The highest charging power in watts. More watts = charges quicker.
fast_charge_w.example: Galaxy A15: 25 W; Infinix Note 40: 45 W.

case_material.title: Case material
case_material.body: What the watch body is made of. Steel and titanium cost more than aluminium.
case_material.example: Apple Watch Series 9: aluminium or steel.

band_material.title: Band material
band_material.body: What the strap is made of.

band_color.title: Band colour
band_color.body: The strap's colour, if different from the watch.
band_color.example: Black watch with a Midnight Blue band.

band_size.title: Band size
band_size.body: Strap size for the wrist: S, M, L or one size.
band_size.example: Apple Watch sport band S/M fits a thin wrist.

compatible_with.title: Works with
compatible_with.body: Which phones the watch connects to. An Apple Watch works only with an iPhone.
compatible_with.example: Galaxy Watch 6 → Android; Apple Watch → iOS.

sensors.title: Sensors
sensors.body: Health readings the watch can take: heart rate, SpO2 (oxygen in blood), sleep, ECG (heart rhythm).
sensors.example: Galaxy Watch 6: heart rate, SpO2, sleep, ECG.

water.title: Water resistance
water.body: How much water it can take. IP68 / 5ATM survive rain and washing hands; "none" should be kept dry.
water.example: Galaxy S23: IP68. Most cheap phones: none.

aod.title: Always-on display
aod.body: Yes if the watch can show the time all the time without lifting the wrist.
aod.example: Apple Watch Series 9: Yes; SE: No.

calling.title: Bluetooth calling
calling.body: Yes if calls can be answered on the watch (through the phone).
calling.example: Many Rs. 8,000 smart watches have Bluetooth calling.

battery_days.title: Battery life (days)
battery_days.body: How many days the watch runs on one charge, as the company says.
battery_days.example: Apple Watch: 1 day; Huawei Watch Fit: 10 days.

bluetooth.title: Bluetooth
bluetooth.body: Bluetooth version, for earbuds and watches. Newer is more stable.

wifi.title: Wi-Fi
wifi.body: Wi-Fi type it supports. Wi-Fi 6 is faster on new routers.

nfc.title: NFC
nfc.body: Yes if the phone can tap to pay or tap to connect.
nfc.example: Galaxy A55: Yes — works with tap-to-pay bank cards in apps.

gps.title: GPS
gps.body: Yes if it has its own location (maps, running) without the phone.

year.title: Release year
year.body: The year the model came out. Older models sell for less.

page.title: Add stock
page.body: Buying phones, tablets, watches or accessories for the shop, in 3 steps: from whom, what and at what cost, then done. Each phone gets its own history and sticker.
page.example: Bought 3 Galaxy A15 from a Hall Road dealer for Rs. 1,05,000 → they are in stock, and Rs. 1,05,000 is on his khata if not paid.

source.title: Where it comes from
source.body: From a dealer (wholesaler, new / box-pack stock) or from a customer selling his own phone. A customer's phone needs an ID check before it can be sold.
source.example: Infinix box from the distributor → From a dealer. A student sells his used iPhone 11 → Buy a customer's phone.

fromDealer.title: From a dealer
fromDealer.body: Stock from a wholesaler or distributor. Phones start as Box pack with 12 months warranty, and no ID check is needed for box-pack phones.
fromDealer.example: 10 Redmi A3 from a Hall Road wholesaler at Rs. 22,500 each.

fromCustomer.title: Buy a customer's phone
fromCustomer.body: A person sells you his own used phone. Phones start as Used with 0 warranty. Keep his CNIC and photo (ID check) so you can show who sold it if it turns out stolen.
fromCustomer.example: A customer sells his Galaxy A54 for Rs. 70,000 cash → take CNIC photos on the ID check screen.

dealer.title: Which dealer
dealer.body: The dealer's khata. What you do not pay now is added there as money you have to give him. Tap + if he is new.
dealer.example: Choose "Rehman Traders, Hall Road" → his khata shows Rs. 2,40,000 to give after this bill.

seller.title: Who is selling
seller.body: The person selling the phone. Save his name and mobile number (and later his CNIC) so the phone's history shows who it came from.
seller.example: Ahmed Raza, 0300 1234567, sells an iPhone 12 → new person, tap + and save him.

lines.title: Phones on this bill
lines.body: Add each phone, tablet or watch one by one, with its IMEI and cost. Tap a line to correct it before saving.
lines.example: 2 Galaxy A15 at Rs. 35,000 + 1 iPhone 13 at Rs. 1,40,000 → 3 lines, total Rs. 2,10,000.

items.title: Accessories / counted items
items.body: Chargers, covers, ordinary watches and other things you keep by count, not by IMEI. Buying raises their count in stock.
items.example: 20 Type-C cables at Rs. 150 → the cable count goes up by 20.

packUnit.title: Bought by piece / dozen / box
packUnit.body: Choose how the dealer sold it. Quantity and cost are per that unit; stock is always kept in pieces.
packUnit.example: 2 dozen covers at Rs. 1,800 a dozen → 24 pieces, Rs. 150 each.

miscItem.title: Other item
miscItem.body: Something else on the dealer's bill that is not kept in stock. It is added to the bill total only.
miscItem.example: "Display stand" Rs. 1,500 on the same bill.

unitCost.title: Unit cost
unitCost.body: What you pay for one unit (one piece, or one dozen / box if you chose that). Quantity × unit cost = this line.

paidHow.title: How you paid
paidHow.body: Cash from the galla, bank, wallet (Easypaisa / JazzCash), or Udhaar — pay later. With udhaar the amount goes on the seller's khata as money you have to give.
paidHow.example: Bill Rs. 80,000 sent by Easypaisa → choose Easypaisa. Not paid yet → Udhaar.

idCheck.title: ID card check
idCheck.body: Check now / later: the phone waits as "ID check pending" until his CNIC, photos, eGadget and signed paper are done. Skip, I know this person: the phone is marked checked now and the skip is written in its history.
idCheck.example: Your regular customer Bilal sells his old phone → Skip. A stranger → Check now.

paidNow.title: Paid now
paidNow.body: With udhaar: how much you gave the seller today. The rest stays on his khata as money you have to give.
paidNow.example: Bill Rs. 1,50,000, paid Rs. 50,000 now → Rs. 1,00,000 to give.

dueDate.title: We pay by
dueDate.body: The day you promised to pay the rest. Optional. After that day the audit shows this udhaar as overdue; without a date it only shows how old it is.
dueDate.example: Promised the dealer to pay on the 10th → after the 10th it shows as overdue.

when.title: When was it bought
when.body: Just now, or Earlier with the date and time. An earlier date puts the purchase in that day's hisaab and reports.
when.example: Forgot to enter Saturday's purchase → Earlier, Saturday 5 pm.

discount.title: Discount from the seller
discount.body: Money the seller took off the whole bill. It is shared over the lines by their price, so each item's cost goes down.
discount.example: 2 phones of Rs. 50,000, discount Rs. 2,000 → each phone's cost becomes Rs. 49,000.

reference.title: Reference
reference.body: Any number or word that helps you find this purchase later, such as the dealer's slip or lot number. Only kept for searching.

supplierBill.title: Supplier bill no.
supplierBill.body: The number printed on the dealer's own bill, so you can match it with his paper if there is a question.
