extraCosts.title: Freight / loading
extraCosts.body: Money spent to bring this stock (courier, rickshaw, loading). It is shared over the lines by price and added to each item's cost, so profit is true.
extraCosts.example: 2 phones of Rs. 50,000 each, courier Rs. 1,000 → each phone costs Rs. 50,500.

extraNote.title: Freight note
extraNote.body: What the extra cost was for, to remember later.

total.title: Total
total.body: All lines added, minus the discount, plus freight. This is what the shop owes for this purchase.
total.example: Lines Rs. 1,00,000 − discount Rs. 2,000 + freight Rs. 500 = Rs. 98,500.

stillToGive.title: Still to give
stillToGive.body: Total minus what you paid now. It goes on the seller's khata.
stillToGive.example: Total Rs. 98,500, paid Rs. 40,000 → Rs. 58,500 still to give.

openingTotal.title: Total of old stock
openingTotal.body: The buying prices of the phones you are adding, added up. No money leaves the galla — this only makes the stock value complete.
openingTotal.example: 3 old phones at Rs. 30,000, 45,000 and 60,000 → total Rs. 1,35,000.

cnicScan.title: Scan CNIC
cnicScan.body: Take a photo of the front of the ID card: the app reads the number and name for you and keeps the photo as the CNIC front. Always check what it filled.
cnicScan.example: Photo of the card → "35202-1234567-1, Ahmed Raza" filled in; fix a digit if it misread.

sheet.title: Price stickers
sheet.body: Prints small stickers to put on the phone or its box: model, price, barcode and what else you choose. Scanning the sticker later opens the phone straight away.
sheet.example: Print 5 stickers for the new Galaxy A15s → stick them on the boxes; at the counter one scan finds the right phone.

size.title: Sticker size
size.body: Pick the size of your label roll (width × height in mm), an A4 sheet of 65, or your own size.

customSize.title: Own size (mm)
customSize.body: Width 20–110 mm and height 10–110 mm, measured on one label of your roll.

fields.title: What goes on it
fields.body: Tap to add or remove each thing on the sticker: shop name, model, storage · colour, price, barcode, IMEI, condition, PTA, date, cost code.
fields.example: For a small 38 × 25 sticker keep only model, price and barcode.

costCode.title: Cost code
costCode.body: The buying price written in letters of a secret 10-letter word, so you can read your cost but the customer cannot. Letter 1 = 0, letter 2 = 1, and so on. Only the owner and manager see this choice.
costCode.example: Word BLACKHORSE (B=0 L=1 A=2 C=3 K=4 H=5 O=6 R=7 S=8 E=9): cost Rs. 45,000 → "KHBBB".

copies.title: Copies of each
copies.body: How many stickers to print for each phone or item.
copies.example: 2 copies: one for the phone, one for its box.

remember.title: Remember these choices
remember.body: Keeps this size and these fields for next time. The owner saves them for the whole shop; others save them on this device only.
remember.example: Set 50 × 30 with model, price, barcode once → it opens like that every time.

barcode.title: Barcode
barcode.body: The shop's own code for this phone, given when it was bought and never changed. It is printed on the sticker; scanning it opens this phone.
barcode.example: Sticker "MS000123" on the box → scan at the counter → this iPhone 13 opens for sale.

manufacturer.title: Maker's barcode
manufacturer.body: The barcode already printed on the box by the company. Saving it lets you scan the box later to find this phone. Optional.
manufacturer.example: Scan the Samsung box barcode "8806095..." → it is saved here.

ownBarcode.title: Own barcode
ownBarcode.body: Leave empty and the app makes a barcode for the sticker. Type one only if you already use your own codes. Once saved it never changes.
ownBarcode.example: Empty → the app gives "MS000124". Your old system code "HR-77" → type HR-77.

hint.title: Your rate for this phone
hint.body: What your own shop sold the same model for in the last 6 months — same storage and condition first — and the same model in stock now. "Use" puts the middle price, rounded to Rs. 100, into the box.
hint.example: Last 4 Galaxy A15 128GB used sold for Rs. 33,000–36,000 → "Use 34,500".

reason.title: Reason
reason.body: Why the price is changing. It is saved in the phone's history with who changed it.

ownerPin.title: Owner PIN
ownerPin.body: If the owner has set price changes to need approval, a staff member types the owner's PIN here to allow it.
ownerPin.example: Salesman lowers an iPhone 13 from Rs. 1,45,000 to Rs. 1,40,000 → owner types his 4-digit PIN.

page.title: Stock
page.body: Every phone, tablet and smart watch the shop has had, one card each. Counted items like chargers and covers are under Accessories.
page.example: 12 cards under "In stock" = 12 devices on your shelf right now.

search.title: Search stock
search.body: Type part of the model, the IMEI or the barcode. A scanner works too: scanning a sticker opens that phone straight away.
search.example: Type "A15" → all Galaxy A15. Type the last digits "4512" → the phone whose IMEI ends in 4512.

brands.title: Brands
brands.body: Tap a brand to see only its devices. The number is how many of that brand are in the list now.

statusFilter.title: Which phones to show
statusFilter.body: In stock: on your shelf. On loan: with another shop on amanat. Sold: already sold. Faulty: marked as having a fault. All: everything.
statusFilter.example: Customer asks about a phone you sold last week → tap Sold and search its IMEI.

sort.title: Order of the list
sort.body: Newest / Oldest: by the last thing that happened to the phone (bought, price change, loan…). Price low / high: by the selling price.
sort.example: Oldest first shows phones nobody has touched for weeks — time to lower their price.

filters.title: More filters
filters.body: Narrow the list by grade, RAM, a price range, or devices whose lock check was never done.
filters.example: Customer wants an 8GB RAM phone under Rs. 40,000 → RAM 8, price to 40000.

priceRange.title: Price from / to
priceRange.body: Shows only devices whose selling price is between these two amounts. Leave one empty for no limit on that side.
priceRange.example: From 25000 to 35000 → every phone priced Rs. 25,000–35,000.

lockUnchecked.title: Lock not checked
lockUnchecked.body: Shows used devices where no lock check (iCloud, Google / FRP…) has been saved yet, so you can check them before a customer asks.
lockUnchecked.example: 3 used iPads show up → open each, press Lock check, mark Cleared.

card.title: What a card shows
card.body: Each card: model, colour and price; then storage (or watch size), PTA (or Wi-Fi / GPS), condition, and Days = days since the last thing happened to it. Tap the card for its full page.
card.example: Days 45 on a Galaxy A15 = nothing has happened to it for 45 days — it is slow stock.

seenBefore.title: Seen before
seenBefore.body: This IMEI is already in your shop's records: it shows how many times you bought it and where it is now. If it is still in stock it cannot be bought again.
seenBefore.example: A customer brings an iPhone 12 you sold him in March → "Seen before · bought 1 time", status Sold — you can buy it back.

notSeen.title: New to this shop
notSeen.body: This IMEI has never been in your shop. You can buy it — for a used phone, still do the ID check.
notSeen.example: A walk-in brings a Galaxy A54 → "Not seen before" → Add stock.

newKind.title: New kind of item
newKind.body: If the item is not one of the kinds in the list, write its kind once; it is then offered for next items too.

itemKinds.title: Kinds of items
itemKinds.body: Tap a kind to see only those items, or All for everything.

itemSearch.title: Find an item
itemSearch.body: Type part of the name or a code: the shop's barcode, the maker's code or the supplier's SKU. A scan fills it.

countPage.title: Stock count
countPage.body: Check the shelf against the app: scan every phone and item you can see, then press Check. The app tells you what is missing and what should not be there.
countPage.example: App says 40 phones in stock; you scan 39 → 1 shows as Missing with its IMEI.

countScanned.title: Scanned
countScanned.body: How many codes you have scanned or typed so far. The list stays on this device until you clear it, even if the app closes.
countScanned.example: Scanned 25 boxes, lunch break, come back → still 25.

countType.title: Type a code
countType.body: If a sticker will not scan, type the IMEI or barcode and press Enter.

countFound.title: Found
countFound.body: Phones you scanned that the app also says are in stock. All good.
countFound.example: 38 found = 38 phones are where they should be.

countMissing.title: Missing
countMissing.body: Phones the app says are in stock but you did not scan. Find them, or check whether one was sold or loaned without being entered.
countMissing.example: Missing: Infinix Hot 40 → it was given to the shop next door without an amanat entry.

countUnexpected.title: Should not be here
countUnexpected.body: Codes you scanned that are not in stock in the app: already sold, on loan, or not known at all. A sale may be missing or a phone was never entered.
countUnexpected.example: Scanned an iPhone 11 that shows "Sold" → its return was never entered.

countItems.title: Items
countItems.body: Counted items you scanned, with how many pieces you scanned against how many the app has.
countItems.example: Type-C cable: scanned 18 of 20 → 2 cables are short.

countInStock.title: Should be in stock
countInStock.body: How many phones the app has as "In stock" right now. Found + Missing equals this number.
countInStock.example: 40 should be in stock = 38 found + 2 missing.

detail.title: One phone's page
detail.body: Everything about this one device: where it is, its prices, details, accessories, the money paid and still owed on it, and its full history from the first day.
detail.example: Open the iPhone 13 → bought from Ahmed for Rs. 1,30,000, sold to Sana for Rs. 1,45,000, Rs. 5,000 still to get.

withParty.title: With
withParty.body: The shop or person who has the phone right now (on amanat, for approval or for repair).
withParty.example: "With: Ali Mobiles" → it is at Ali Mobiles on amanat.

actions.title: Actions
actions.body: Things you can do with this phone now. Only what fits its status shows: an in-stock phone can be loaned or sent for repair, a faulty one can be cleared. Every action is saved in its history.
actions.example: Screen stopped working → Mark faulty. Back from the technician → Repair returned.

deviceInfo.title: Device details
deviceInfo.body: The fixed facts saved for this unit: second IMEI, serial, SIM time, warranty, RAM, specs, lock check, patch details and notes. "Edit details" corrects them.
deviceInfo.example: Warranty 12 months · Company — shown here and on the receipt.

accessories.title: Accessories
accessories.body: What came with this phone and what is still pending: green = came with it, yellow = the seller still has to give it, red = the shop still has to give it to the buyer.
accessories.example: Charger · seller gives later → remind the dealer before you sell the phone.

history.title: History
history.body: Every step of this phone from the first day: bought, price changed, ID checked, loaned, repaired, sold, returned, and every payment for it. Nothing is ever removed. Tap a row to open the bill behind it.
history.example: Bought 1 Oct → price changed 15 Oct → sold 20 Oct → payment Rs. 5,000 received 25 Oct.

title.title: Money on this phone
title.body: The money story of this one phone: what it cost, what was paid and is still owed to the seller, what it sold for, what the buyer has paid and still owes, and the margin.
title.example: Cost Rs. 60,000, still to pay Rs. 10,000; sold Rs. 68,000, still to get Rs. 3,000; margin Rs. 8,000.

stillToPay.title: Still to pay
stillToPay.body: What the shop still owes the seller for this phone: its price on the purchase bill minus what was paid towards it.
stillToPay.example: Bought for Rs. 60,000, paid Rs. 50,000 → Rs. 10,000 still to pay.

askingNow.title: Asking now
askingNow.body: The selling price set on this phone today.

askingFirst.title: First asking
askingFirst.body: The selling price it had when it was first added, before any change. Shown only when the price was changed later.
askingFirst.example: First Rs. 72,000, now Rs. 68,000 → lowered by Rs. 4,000.

soldFor.title: Sold for
soldFor.body: This phone's price on the sale bill, after its share of any discount.
soldFor.example: Bill of Rs. 70,000 with Rs. 2,000 discount, only this phone on it → sold for Rs. 68,000.

stillToGet.title: Still to get
stillToGet.body: What the buyer still owes for this phone: sold for minus what he paid towards it.
stillToGet.example: Sold for Rs. 68,000, received Rs. 65,000 → Rs. 3,000 still to get.

margin.title: Margin
margin.body: Sold for minus cost, for this phone only. Shop expenses are not taken out here.
margin.example: Sold Rs. 68,000 − cost Rs. 60,000 = Rs. 8,000 margin.

bought.title: Bought from
bought.body: Who sold you this phone and on which bill. Tap the name to open his khata. When the bill had other things on it, the figures below are this phone's share.
bought.example: Bought from Rehman Traders, bill P-0042 of Rs. 1,80,000 with other items.

sold.title: Sold to
sold.body: Who bought this phone and on which bill. Tap the name to open his khata.
sold.example: Sold to Sana Khan, bill S-0310.

agreed.title: Agreed
agreed.body: This phone's price on that bill.

paidOut.title: Paid
paidOut.body: All the shop has paid for this phone: at the time of the bill plus later payments put against it.
paidOut.example: Rs. 30,000 on the day + Rs. 20,000 a week later = Rs. 50,000 paid.

receivedIn.title: Received
receivedIn.body: All the buyer has paid for this phone: at the counter plus later payments put against its bill.
receivedIn.example: Rs. 60,000 at the counter + Rs. 5,000 later = Rs. 65,000 received.

upfront.title: At the time
upfront.body: Money paid on the day the bill was made. Below it, each later payment with its own receipt.
upfront.example: Paid at the time Rs. 30,000 · then RV-0012 Rs. 20,000.

seller.title: Seller
seller.body: The person who sold you this phone, his CNIC number and photos: the front and back of his CNIC, his face, and the phone. All four CNIC / face items are needed for the check to be complete.
seller.example: Ahmed Raza, 35202-1234567-1, with CNIC front, back and his photo taken at the counter.

photos.title: Photos
photos.body: Tap a box to take a photo: CNIC front, CNIC back, the seller's face, and the phone. A green tick means it is saved. The phone photo is extra proof; the other three are required.
photos.example: CNIC front ✓, back ✓, seller ✓ → only eGadget and the signed paper are left.

egadget.title: eGadget check
egadget.body: Punjab Police's website for reported stolen phones. Open it, enter the IMEI, and mark the result here. Clear is needed to finish the check; Flagged blocks the phone from sale.
egadget.example: egadget.punjab.gov.pk says "No record found" for the IMEI → mark Clear.

egadgetRef.title: Reference no.
egadgetRef.body: Any number the eGadget site shows for your search, so you can prove you checked. Optional.

pta.title: PTA check
pta.body: Send the IMEI by SMS to 8484; PTA replies whether it is approved. Tick it and choose what PTA said. It is saved with the check (not required to complete it).

declaration.title: Signed declaration
declaration.body: A printed paper where the seller says the phone is his and not stolen, and signs it. Print, get it signed, keep it, then tick here. Needed to complete the check.
declaration.example: Print → Ahmed signs → keep it in the file → tick.

notes.title: Physical condition notes
notes.body: How the phone looked when you bought it, so there is no argument later.
notes.example: "Back glass cracked, Face ID works, battery 84%".

result.title: Result
result.body: Clear: everything is done and eGadget is clear — the phone can be sold. Not checked: something is still missing. Flagged: eGadget shows it as stolen — it cannot be sold.
result.example: All papers and eGadget clear → Clear.

missing.title: Still missing
missing.body: What is left before the check is complete: CNIC number, CNIC front, CNIC back, seller photo, eGadget clear, signed declaration.
missing.example: Still missing: CNIC back, declaration → take the back photo and get the paper signed.

override.title: Owner override
override.body: The owner or manager can clear the phone for sale even with papers missing, with a written reason. The reason and who did it stay in the phone's history.
override.example: Phone bought from your cousin, no CNIC copy → override, reason "Known family member".

overrideReason.title: Reason for override
overrideReason.body: Why you are clearing it without the full check — at least 5 letters. Write something you can explain later.

signature.title: Seller's signature
signature.body: The person selling you the phone signs on the screen that it is his and not stolen. It is saved with the ID check and printed on the declaration.
signature.example: Usman sells you a used Redmi: he signs with his finger, you tap Save — the declaration now shows his signature above the line.

page.title: Amanat (loans)
page.body: Phones given to another shop to show or sell. The phone stays yours until it comes back or they keep it — then it becomes a sale to that shop on their khata.
page.example: Gave an iPhone 13 to Ali Mobiles on Monday; they sold it, so you "sell" it to them for Rs. 1,40,000.

outCount.title: Phones out now
outCount.body: How many of your phones are at other shops right now on amanat.
outCount.example: 4 → four phones are sitting at other shops.

overdue.title: Overdue
overdue.body: Amanat phones whose "back by" date has passed and that have not come back. Call that shop.
overdue.example: Given for 7 days on the 1st, not back on the 9th → overdue.

views.title: Out / Returned / Sold
views.body: Out: still at the other shop. Returned: came back into your stock. Sold to them: they kept it and it became a sale on their khata.
views.example: Tap Sold to them to see every amanat phone that became a sale this month.

price.title: Agreed price
price.body: The price you agreed with that shop for the phone they kept. It becomes a sale bill to them.
price.example: Ali Mobiles kept the Galaxy S23 at Rs. 1,95,000 → bill of Rs. 1,95,000.

paidNow.title: Paid now
paidNow.body: What that shop paid you today for the phone. The rest goes on their khata.
paidNow.example: Price Rs. 1,95,000, they paid Rs. 1,50,000 → Rs. 45,000 on their khata.

onKhata.title: On their khata
onKhata.body: Agreed price minus paid now: what that shop will owe you after this.

pickPhone.title: Which phone
pickPhone.body: Search and pick a phone from your stock. Only in-stock phones can be given on amanat.

toShop.title: Which shop
toShop.body: The other shop taking the phone. It is saved as a party, so if they keep the phone the bill goes on their khata.

expectedBack.title: Back by
expectedBack.body: When the phone should come back. After this day it shows as overdue. "No date" if you agreed none.
expectedBack.example: Back in 7 days from 1 Nov → overdue from 9 Nov.

page.title: Brands & models
page.body: The lists you pick from when adding stock: brands, models, storage sizes and colours. Built-in ones are shared and fixed; the shop's own can be renamed or deleted.
page.example: Add model "Hot 50 Pro" under Infinix once → it shows every time you buy one.

brands.title: Brands
brands.body: Phone, tablet and watch companies. The number beside each is how many models it has.

models.title: Models
models.body: The models of one brand. Choose the brand first, then add or rename its models.

storages.title: Storage sizes
storages.body: Memory sizes to pick from. Write them like 128GB or 1TB.

colours.title: Colours
colours.body: Colour names to pick from when adding a phone.

pickBrand.title: Choose a brand
pickBrand.body: Models belong to a brand, so tap the brand whose models you want to see or add.

builtin.title: Built-in
builtin.body: Comes with the app for every shop, so it cannot be renamed or deleted. Rows without this mark were added by your shop and can be changed.
builtin.example: "Samsung" is built-in; your own "Itel" can be renamed.

quickAdd.title: Add a new one
quickAdd.body: Type the missing name and press Save: it is added to the list for your shop; in the add-stock form it is also chosen right away.
quickAdd.example: Model "Spark 30C" not in the list → type it → Save → it is selected.

home.title: Home (shop counter)
home.body: Your first screen: find a phone, sell, add stock, and the main numbers of your shop. Tap any card to open its details.
home.example: In the morning Sales shows Rs. 0. You sell a Samsung A15 for Rs. 32,000 cash → Sales shows Rs. 32,000.

search.title: Search stock
search.body: Type a model or IMEI, or scan the box barcode. The stock list opens with only the phones that match.
search.example: Type "A15" → the list shows your 3 Samsung A15 phones with their prices.

sell.title: Sell
sell.body: Starts a new sale: pick the phone or item, write the price and how it was paid (cash, online, udhaar). The bill is made and stock goes down by itself.
sell.example: iPhone 13 sold for Rs. 1,45,000: Rs. 1,00,000 cash, Rs. 45,000 udhaar → bill made, the phone leaves stock, Rs. 45,000 goes on the customer's khata.

addStock.title: Add stock
addStock.body: Enter a phone or item you bought: new from a dealer or used from a customer. It goes into stock at its buying price; what you still owe goes on the dealer's khata.
addStock.example: Bought 2 Infinix Hot 40 from a Hall Road dealer at Rs. 38,000 each and paid Rs. 50,000 → 2 phones in stock, Rs. 26,000 on the dealer's khata.

otherJobs.title: Other jobs
otherJobs.body: Quick buttons for the other daily work: udhaar khata, stock, repair, return, invoices and expense. Each one opens its own screen.
otherJobs.example: A customer brings a phone back → tap Return. You paid the electricity bill of Rs. 6,500 → tap Expense.

glanceAll.title: At a glance
glanceAll.body: The main numbers of your shop. Sales, profit, in hand and expenses are for the days you pick below; cash & bank, udhaar and stock are as of right now.
glanceAll.example: Pick "This month": Sales Rs. 8,50,000 and Expenses Rs. 60,000 are this month's; "I will get" Rs. 1,20,000 is everything owed to you today.

sales.title: Sales
sales.body: Total of the bills made in these days, after discount and minus anything that came back (tax included if added). Cancelled bills are not counted. The small line counts phones sold.
sales.example: Sold 3 phones for Rs. 1,20,000; one of Rs. 40,000 came back → Sales Rs. 80,000, phones sold 2.

profit.title: Profit
profit.body: Real profit for these days: sales minus the buying price of what was sold, minus expenses, plus repair and other income. Only the owner and manager see it.
profit.example: Sales Rs. 3,00,000, their buying price Rs. 2,60,000, expenses Rs. 15,000, repair income Rs. 5,000 → profit Rs. 30,000.

cashBank.title: Cash & bank
cashBank.body: All the money the shop has right now: the galla (cash drawer) plus bank, Easypaisa, JazzCash and other accounts together. It is today's balance, not for the chosen days.
cashBank.example: Galla Rs. 40,000 + Meezan Bank Rs. 1,50,000 + Easypaisa Rs. 10,000 → Rs. 2,00,000.

toGet.title: I will get
toGet.body: All the udhaar people owe the shop right now: every khata with a balance in your favour, added up.
toGet.example: Ali owes Rs. 25,000 and Bilal Rs. 15,000 → I will get Rs. 40,000.

toGive.title: I have to give
toGive.body: All the shop owes others right now: dealers not paid in full, money taken with no bill, customers with money left with you. Every khata in their favour, added up.
toGive.example: Hall Road dealer Rs. 60,000 + Usman Rs. 10,000 → I have to give Rs. 70,000.

inStock.title: Phones in stock
inStock.body: How many phones, tablets and watches are in the shop right now (sold ones and ones out on amanat are not counted). Worth is at buying price for the owner and manager, at selling price for other staff.
inStock.example: 12 phones in the shop, bought for Rs. 4,80,000 → In stock 12, Worth 4,80,000.

expenses.title: Expenses
expenses.body: Shop expenses written for these days: rent, bills, salaries, tea and so on. Cancelled expenses are not counted.
expenses.example: Rent Rs. 30,000 + electricity Rs. 8,000 + tea Rs. 2,000 → Expenses Rs. 40,000.

week.title: Last 7 days
week.body: One bar for each of the last 7 days: that day's sales after returns. Tap a bar to open that day's hisaab.
week.example: Tuesday's bar is the tallest at Rs. 2,10,000 → tap it to see what was sold that day.

moneySplit.title: Where the money sits
moneySplit.body: Your business in four parts: cash & bank, udhaar people owe you, what you owe others, and the stock's worth. Tap a part to open it.
moneySplit.example: Cash Rs. 2,00,000, to get Rs. 1,00,000, to give Rs. 50,000, stock Rs. 5,00,000 → most of your money is in stock.

hazri.title: Hazri (attendance)
hazri.body: Tap Check in when you reach the shop and Check out when you leave. The owner sees everyone's times and hours under Staff.
hazri.example: In at 10:00 am, out at 8:00 pm → 10 hours for today.

ai.title: Assistant
ai.body: Ask about your shop in plain words; it answers from your own records.
ai.example: Ask "Who owes the most?" → it answers, for example, "Ali, Rs. 45,000".

reports.title: Profit & reports
reports.body: Opens the owner's reports: real profit after expenses, tax, best sellers, old stock and an estimate for next week.
reports.example: See that Infinix Hot 40 sold 9 pieces this month, and which phones have sat unsold for 60 days.

attention.title: Needs attention
attention.body: Things waiting for you. Each line shows how many; tap it to open the list.
attention.example: "2 repair jobs open" → tap it to see which phones are still in repair.

pendingCheck.title: ID check pending
pendingCheck.body: Phones in stock whose seller's ID card check is not finished, or that are marked as suspected. Finish the check before selling.
pendingCheck.example: You bought a used Vivo Y20 and skipped the CNIC photo → it shows here until you add it.

openRepairs.title: Repairs open
openRepairs.body: Repair jobs taken in and not yet given back to the customer.
openRepairs.example: 3 phones in for screen and battery work → 3 repair jobs open.

instOverdue.title: Installments late
instOverdue.body: Installment (qist) plans where at least one monthly installment has passed its date without being paid.
instOverdue.example: Kashif's qist of Rs. 8,000 was due on the 10th; today is the 15th → his plan shows as late.

instToday.title: Installments due today
instToday.body: Plans whose next installment falls due today (and none is late).
instToday.example: Three customers pay on the 10th and today is the 10th → 3 due today.

lendLate.title: Len-den late
lendLate.body: People who took money from the shop with no bill (len-den) and whose return date has passed.
lendLate.example: You gave Usman Rs. 20,000 to return on the 1st; today is the 5th → he shows here.

lendWeOwe.title: Len-den to give back
lendWeOwe.body: Money the shop took from someone with no bill, whose return date is within 3 days or has already passed.
lendWeOwe.example: You took Rs. 50,000 from Imran to return on Friday; today is Wednesday → it shows here.

lowStock.title: Items low on stock
lowStock.body: Counted items (chargers, covers, watches and so on) whose quantity is at or below the reorder level you set.
lowStock.example: Reorder level 5 for the Samsung 25W charger and 4 are left → it shows here.

dayReport.title: Day's hisaab
dayReport.body: The business of one day or a period: what was sold, how the money came, udhaar given and received back, expenses, money left in hand and the list of what was sold.
dayReport.example: Pick Yesterday: Sold Rs. 1,50,000, cash Rs. 1,00,000, udhaar given Rs. 50,000, expenses Rs. 5,000.

cameIn.title: Came in
cameIn.body: All the money that came into the galla, bank and wallets in these days, with the reason: sales, udhaar received, repairs, len-den, moves from your own account, other.
cameIn.example: Sales Rs. 80,000 + udhaar received Rs. 20,000 → came in Rs. 1,00,000.

wentOut.title: Went out
wentOut.body: All the money that left the galla, bank and wallets in these days, with the reason: stock bought, returns, expenses, paid to people, len-den, moves to your own account, other.
wentOut.example: Stock bought Rs. 75,000 + expenses Rs. 5,000 → went out Rs. 80,000.

cashIn.title: Cash received
cashIn.body: Cash paid at the counter on the bills of these days. Udhaar paid back later is counted in Udhaar received.
cashIn.example: Two sales: Rs. 30,000 in cash and Rs. 20,000 on udhaar → cash received Rs. 30,000.

digital.title: Bank / Easypaisa
digital.body: Money paid at the counter on these bills into the bank, Easypaisa or JazzCash.
digital.example: A customer paid Rs. 45,000 by Easypaisa for a Redmi 13 → Rs. 45,000 here.

udhaarGiven.title: Given on udhaar
udhaarGiven.body: The part of these bills not paid at the counter; it went on the customers' khata.
udhaarGiven.example: Bill Rs. 1,45,000, paid Rs. 1,00,000 → Rs. 45,000 given on udhaar.

udhaarBack.title: Udhaar received
udhaarBack.body: Payments people made in these days against their khata or old bills, of any date. Len-den money is not counted here.
udhaarBack.example: Bilal paid Rs. 15,000 against last month's bill today → Rs. 15,000 here.

refunded.title: Given back on returns
refunded.body: Money handed back to customers on returns in these days. What the shop kept is shown in Cut on returns.
refunded.example: A Rs. 1,00,000 phone came back and you handed back Rs. 90,000 → Rs. 90,000 here, cut Rs. 10,000.

items.title: What was sold
items.body: Every item on the bills of these days, with the buyer, who sold it and how it was paid. A crossed-out line came back later. Tap a line to open its bill.
items.example: "Samsung A15 · Ali · Part udhaar · 32,000" → tap it to open Ali's bill.

sales.title: Sales
sales.body: Money paid at the counter when a bill was made (cash, online, cheque...). Udhaar paid later is not here.
sales.example: iPhone 13 sold for Rs. 1,45,000, Rs. 1,00,000 paid now → Rs. 1,00,000 here.

udhaarBack.title: Udhaar received
udhaarBack.body: Money people paid later against their khata or old bills, installments included.
udhaarBack.example: Ali paid Rs. 10,000 of his old udhaar → Rs. 10,000 here.

repairs.title: Repairs
repairs.body: Advance and final payments taken for repair jobs.
repairs.example: Screen change of Rs. 6,000, Rs. 2,000 advance today → Rs. 2,000 here.

lendingIn.title: Len-den taken
lendingIn.body: Money that came in with no bill: someone lent the shop money, or paid back money the shop had lent him.
lendingIn.example: Usman returned the Rs. 20,000 you had given him → Rs. 20,000 here.

lendingOut.title: Len-den given
lendingOut.body: Money that went out with no bill: the shop lent money to someone, or paid back money it had taken.
lendingOut.example: You lent a neighbour shop Rs. 30,000 cash → Rs. 30,000 here.

transfer.title: Moved between your accounts
transfer.body: Money moved from one of your own accounts to another, e.g. galla to bank. It shows once as came in and once as went out, so the total does not change.
transfer.example: Deposited Rs. 1,00,000 from the galla into Meezan Bank → Rs. 1,00,000 in both came in and went out.

other.title: Other
other.body: Money moves that fit none of the other reasons, e.g. a dealer paying back for a returned phone, a cancelled bill, the opening cash, or pay to an outside technician.
other.example: A dealer gave back Rs. 30,000 for a faulty phone you returned → Rs. 30,000 under other (came in).

stock.title: Stock bought
stock.body: Money paid when buying stock (phones, items). It is not lost: it is now goods in your shop.
stock.example: Bought 2 Infinix Hot 40 for Rs. 76,000 cash → Rs. 76,000 here, and 2 more phones in stock.

returns.title: Returns
returns.body: Money handed back to customers for returned items, and the difference given back on exchanges.
returns.example: A customer returned a Redmi 13 and you gave back Rs. 40,000 → Rs. 40,000 here.

expenses.title: Expenses
expenses.body: Money paid for shop expenses: rent, bills, salaries, tea and so on.
expenses.example: Paid the shop rent of Rs. 30,000 from the galla → Rs. 30,000 here.

paidOut.title: Paid to people
paidOut.body: Payments against a khata: paying a dealer's old bill, or giving a customer back money he had left with you.
paidOut.example: Paid the Hall Road dealer Rs. 50,000 of the old balance → Rs. 50,000 here.

reminders.title: Udhaar reminders
reminders.body: Everyone who owes the shop, with how long since their last khata entry. Send a WhatsApp reminder to one person or to all.
reminders.example: Ali owes Rs. 25,000 and his last entry was 40 days ago → tap the green button and WhatsApp opens with the message ready.

remindFilter.title: Older than
remindFilter.body: Shows only people whose last khata entry (bill or payment) is at least this many days old. Everyone shows all who owe.
remindFilter.example: Pick "Older than 30 days": Bilal (45 days) shows, Ali (10 days) is hidden.

stockPage.title: Stock worth
stockPage.body: How many phones are in the shop and what they are worth, by brand and then by model.
stockPage.example: Samsung 8 phones worth Rs. 3,20,000, Infinix 5 phones worth Rs. 1,90,000 → total 13 phones, Rs. 5,10,000.

stockValue.title: Stock in shop
stockValue.body: Total value of the phones, tablets and watches in stock now. The owner and manager see it at buying price, other staff at selling price. Counted items (chargers, covers) are not included.
stockValue.example: 10 phones bought for Rs. 4,00,000 with asking prices of Rs. 4,50,000 → the owner sees Rs. 4,00,000, a salesman sees Rs. 4,50,000.

stockBrands.title: By brand
stockBrands.body: Each brand with how many phones and their value, the biggest first. Tap a brand to see its models; tap a model to see those phones.
stockBrands.example: Tap Samsung → A15 (4 phones), A35 (2), S23 (2); tap A15 to see the 4 phones.

page.title: Sell
page.body: A sale in steps: pick the phone or item, write the price and how it was paid, then print or share the bill. Stock and khata update by themselves.
page.example: Pick an Infinix Hot 40, price Rs. 39,000, Cash → Complete → the receipt prints and the phone leaves stock.

search.title: Find a phone
search.body: Type the model or IMEI to find the phone in stock, or scan its barcode: a scanned phone goes straight on the bill.
search.example: Scan the box of a Samsung A15 → that phone is added to the bill with its asking price.

devCat.title: Type of device
devCat.body: Show only mobiles, tablets or smart watches in the list below. All shows everything in stock.
devCat.example: Tap Tablet → only your Galaxy Tab and iPad units are listed.

pickPhone.title: Phones in stock
pickPhone.body: Only phones in stock are listed. Tap one to put it on the bill with its asking price filled in. A yellow or red mark means its ID check is pending or it is suspected.
pickPhone.example: Tap "Redmi 13 · 128GB" → it goes on the bill at its asking price of Rs. 42,000.

items.title: Items on the bill
items.body: "+ Another phone" adds a phone from stock. "Accessory / watch" is a counted item from stock: selling it lowers its quantity. "+ Charger, cover or other item" is anything you type yourself, with no stock change. "Discount & customer" opens those boxes.
items.example: An A15 plus a Rs. 1,500 cover from stock → the cover count goes from 10 to 9.

reviseAsking.title: Update asking price
reviseAsking.body: Tick it to change this phone's asking (selling) price now. The change is written in the phone's history with your name; by the shop's rule it may need the owner or manager, or the owner's PIN.
reviseAsking.example: The market dropped: tick it and set the A35 from Rs. 62,000 to Rs. 58,000.

newAsking.title: New asking price
newAsking.body: The selling price this phone should carry from now on. Your sold price is compared with it.
newAsking.example: Asking was Rs. 60,000, new asking Rs. 55,000, sold at Rs. 55,000 → not under asking.

askingReason.title: Reason
askingReason.body: Why the asking price changed. The owner reads it in the phone's history.
askingReason.example: "New model launched, rate dropped by Rs. 4,000."

soldFor.title: Sold for
soldFor.body: The price the customer pays for this phone. It starts at the asking price; selling under it may need the owner or manager, or the owner's PIN, by the shop's rule.
soldFor.example: Asking Rs. 42,000, customer bargains → type Rs. 40,000.

belowCost.title: Below buying price
belowCost.body: The price you typed is less than what the shop paid for this phone, so it is a loss. Only the owner or manager can allow it, with the button below.
belowCost.example: Bought for Rs. 50,000, typed Rs. 47,000 → a loss of Rs. 3,000; only the owner or manager can confirm.

tier.title: Price type
tier.body: Which price was filled in for this item: the dealer price for a customer marked as a dealer, the promo price while a promotion runs, otherwise the retail price.
tier.example: Charger retail Rs. 1,200, dealer price Rs. 1,000 → when you pick a dealer as the customer, Rs. 1,000 is filled in.

belowMin.title: Below minimum price
belowMin.body: This item has a lowest selling price set and your price is under it. The shop's price rule decides whether the owner or manager must approve.
belowMin.example: Minimum for an AirPods copy is Rs. 2,500 and you typed Rs. 2,200 → it is marked here.

itemName.title: Item
itemName.body: The name of a thing that is not in your counted stock, as it should appear on the bill. It does not change any stock.

unitPrice.title: Price of one
unitPrice.body: The price of one piece. The line comes to quantity × this price.
unitPrice.example: 3 covers at Rs. 500 → Rs. 1,500 on the bill.

taxRate.title: Tax %
taxRate.body: The sales tax percent added on top of the bill after discount. It starts at your shop's rate from settings.

on.title: Sell on installments (qist)
on.body: The customer pays an advance now and the rest monthly. A plan with due dates is made with a guarantor, and late installments show on Home.
on.example: Phone Rs. 1,20,000, advance Rs. 30,000, 6 months → Rs. 15,000 a month.

advance.title: Advance
advance.body: What the customer pays today, by the method chosen above. The rest is split into monthly installments.
advance.example: Bill Rs. 80,000, advance Rs. 20,000 → Rs. 60,000 left for the installments.

months.title: Months
months.body: How many monthly installments the rest is split into.
months.example: Rs. 60,000 left over 6 months → 6 installments of Rs. 10,000.

monthly.title: Monthly
monthly.body: The amount of one installment. It is worked out as what is left ÷ months, but you can change it; the last month takes whatever is left.
monthly.example: Rs. 90,000 over 6 months → Rs. 15,000. Type Rs. 16,000 → 5 × Rs. 16,000 and the last month Rs. 10,000.

dueDay.title: Day of month
dueDay.body: The date of each month on which the installment is due (1 to 28).
dueDay.example: Day 10 → installments fall on 10 March, 10 April, 10 May...

firstDue.title: First installment
firstDue.body: The date of the first installment. Left empty, it is next month on the day above.
firstDue.example: Sold on 5 March with day 10 and this left empty → first installment on 10 April.

guarantor.title: Guarantor (zamin)
guarantor.body: A person who stands behind the customer. If the customer stops paying, you contact him. His name, mobile and CNIC are kept with the plan.
guarantor.example: Kashif buys on qist; his brother Asif, with his mobile and CNIC, is the guarantor.

gName.title: Guarantor's name
gName.body: The guarantor's full name as on his ID card. It is printed with the plan.

gCnic.title: Guarantor's CNIC
gCnic.body: The 13 digits of the guarantor's ID card; the dashes come by themselves.

promiseDate.title: Promised date
promiseDate.body: The day the customer promises to pay the udhaar. After it, the audit shows this udhaar as overdue; without a date it only shows how old it is.
promiseDate.example: Udhaar Rs. 20,000, promised for the 30th → from the 31st it shows as overdue.

flagged.title: Suspected stolen
flagged.body: This phone was marked as possibly stolen during its ID check. Only the owner can sell it, and must write a reason.
flagged.example: A used iPhone 12 was flagged at purchase → a salesman cannot sell it; the owner can, with a reason.

override.title: Reason to sell anyway
override.body: Write why you are selling it without a cleared check (at least 3 letters). It is saved on the sale and in the phone's history.
override.example: "Seller came back with his original CNIC and box bill."

pendingCheck.title: ID check pending
pendingCheck.body: The seller's CNIC check for this used phone is not done. Check now, or tap Skip if you know the person; skipping is written in the phone's history.
pendingCheck.example: You bought it from a regular customer you know → tap Skip and sell.

total.title: Total
total.body: What the customer pays for the whole bill: all lines, minus discount, plus tax if added.
total.example: Phone Rs. 50,000 + cover Rs. 1,000 − discount Rs. 1,000 → total Rs. 50,000.

held.title: Held sales
held.body: Park a bill when a customer steps away, serve the next one, and resume it later from any counter phone. Nothing is sold and no stock moves until you complete it.
held.example: A customer goes to the ATM → hold his A15 bill as "Ali ATM", sell to the next person, then resume Ali's bill.

confirm.title: Check before you sell
confirm.body: A last look before the bill is made: each phone's sold price against its asking price, and for the owner and manager its cost and profit.
confirm.example: Asking Rs. 42,000, sold Rs. 40,000 → it shows "Rs. 2,000 under the asking price" before you confirm.

lineProfit.title: Profit on this phone
lineProfit.body: Sold price minus the buying price of this phone. Expenses are not taken out here.
lineProfit.example: Bought Rs. 52,000, sold Rs. 58,000 → profit Rs. 6,000.

underAsking.title: Under the asking price
underAsking.body: You are selling this much below the asking price. By the shop's rule it may need the owner or manager, or the owner's PIN, and it is written in the phone's history.
underAsking.example: Asking Rs. 65,000, sold Rs. 62,000 → Rs. 3,000 under asking, saved with your name.

ownerPin.title: Owner PIN
ownerPin.body: The shop's rule asks for the owner's PIN for this price. The owner types it on this phone, and the sale records that he approved it.
ownerPin.example: The salesman sells Rs. 2,000 under asking → the owner types his 4-digit PIN and the sale goes through.

list.title: Sales
list.body: Every sale bill, newest first, with what is still to be received on it. Tap one to open, print, take items back or cancel it.
list.example: Ali's bill INV-0042: total Rs. 45,000, Rs. 15,000 still due → tap it to take the payment or print it.

statusFilter.title: Paid / unpaid
statusFilter.body: Unpaid: nothing paid yet. Partly paid: some udhaar is left. Paid: fully paid. All shows every bill.
statusFilter.example: Tap Partly paid → only bills with some udhaar left, e.g. Rs. 45,000 bill with Rs. 15,000 due.

detail.title: Sale bill
detail.body: One bill: customer, items, totals, what is paid and what is still due. Print it, share it, take items back or cancel it from here.
detail.example: Open INV-0042 → see the A15 sold to Ali, Rs. 30,000 paid, Rs. 15,000 due, and print it again.

customer.title: Customer
customer.body: Who the bill is for. Cash customer means no khata is kept. Tap the name to open his khata.
customer.example: Bill for "Ali Mobile Zone" → tap the name to see his whole khata.

soldBy.title: Sold by
soldBy.body: The staff login that made this bill.
soldBy.example: Sold by Hamza → Hamza's login made it, even if the owner's PIN approved the price.

subtotal.title: Items total
subtotal.body: The sum of all lines before discount and tax.
subtotal.example: Phone Rs. 50,000 + cover Rs. 1,000 → Rs. 51,000 before the discount.

paidSoFar.title: Paid
paidSoFar.body: Everything received on this bill: at the counter plus later payments put against it.
paidSoFar.example: Rs. 30,000 at the counter + Rs. 10,000 next week → paid Rs. 40,000.

returnedTotal.title: Returned items
returnedTotal.body: The value of the items on this bill that came back. It is taken off what the customer owes.
returnedTotal.example: Bill Rs. 51,000, the Rs. 1,000 cover came back → Rs. 1,000 here.

billProfit.title: Profit on this bill
billProfit.body: Bill total minus tax minus the buying price of everything on it. Returns and expenses are not taken out here.
billProfit.example: Total Rs. 58,000, no tax, buying price Rs. 52,000 → profit Rs. 6,000.

settlement.title: Settlement
settlement.body: What happens to the money the customer paid for the returned items. Refund now: you hand it back. Keep as credit: it stays on his khata to use later. Keep as income: the shop keeps it.
settlement.example: Returned a Rs. 5,000 earbud: Refund now → you give Rs. 5,000 back; Keep as credit → his khata shows Rs. 5,000 in his favour.

returnPage.title: Return
returnPage.body: A customer brings back what he bought: pick it, decide how much to hand back, and the phone goes back into stock. The bill and the khata are corrected by themselves.
returnPage.example: Ali returns an A15 bought for Rs. 32,000 → you give back Rs. 30,000, the shop keeps Rs. 2,000, the A15 is back in stock.

returnSearch.title: Find the sold phone
returnSearch.body: Type the IMEI, the buyer's name or mobile, or scan, to find the phone that was sold. A scanned phone opens its bill straight away.
returnSearch.example: Scan the A15's IMEI → Ali's bill opens with that phone ticked.

recentSales.title: Recent sales
recentSales.body: The latest bills. Tap one to take items back from it.
recentSales.example: The charger sold an hour ago is faulty → tap that bill at the top.

returnLines.title: What came back
returnLines.body: Tick the items on this bill that came back. Items returned before are greyed out.
returnLines.example: Bill has an A15 and a cover; only the cover came back → tick only the cover.

onUdhaarOnly.title: Only off the udhaar
onUdhaarOnly.body: Nothing was paid for these items, so no money is handed back; their price just comes off the customer's udhaar.
onUdhaarOnly.example: A Rs. 20,000 phone given fully on udhaar comes back → his udhaar drops by Rs. 20,000, no cash moves.

paidForIt.title: Customer had paid
paidForIt.body: What the customer actually paid for the items coming back: their price minus any udhaar still open on this bill.
paidForIt.example: Bill Rs. 1,00,000 with Rs. 20,000 still on udhaar, the whole bill comes back → he had paid Rs. 80,000.

giveFrom.title: Give back from
giveFrom.body: Which account the money goes back from: galla (cash), bank or wallet. Keep in khata: nothing is handed over now; the amount stays on his khata in his favour.
giveFrom.example: Give back from Cash → the galla goes down by the refund. Keep in khata → he can use it on his next purchase.

giveBack.title: Give back
giveBack.body: How much you hand back to the customer. It starts at the full amount; type less and the rest is the shop's cut.
giveBack.example: He had paid Rs. 32,000, you type Rs. 30,000 → the shop's cut is Rs. 2,000.

returnReason.title: Reason
returnReason.body: Why it came back. It is saved with the return and in the phone's history.

page.title: Exchange / upgrade
page.body: The customer gives his old phone and takes a new one. The old one goes into your stock at the agreed value, the new one is sold, and only the difference is paid.
page.example: New iPhone 13 Rs. 1,50,000, old iPhone 11 taken at Rs. 80,000 → the customer pays Rs. 70,000.

oldPhone.title: Old phone
oldPhone.body: Enter the customer's phone like a purchase: model, IMEI, condition and the value you give for it.
oldPhone.example: iPhone 11, 64GB, PTA, minor scratches, value Rs. 80,000.

tradeValue.title: Trade-in value
tradeValue.body: What you give the customer for his old phone. It is taken off the new phone's price and becomes the old phone's buying price in your stock.
tradeValue.example: Old Redmi Note 12 taken at Rs. 35,000 → Rs. 35,000 off the bill, and it sits in stock at a cost of Rs. 35,000.

newPrice.title: New phone price
newPrice.body: The price of the phone the customer takes. It starts at its asking price.
newPrice.example: Samsung A35 asking Rs. 75,000 → you agree Rs. 73,000 and type that.

previous.title: Previous balance
previous.body: What was already on the customer's khata before this exchange (plus means he owes you).
previous.example: He already owed Rs. 5,000 → it is added to what is left after the exchange.

difference.title: Difference
difference.body: New phone price minus trade-in value. If it is more, the customer pays it; if it is less, you hand the difference back from the galla.
difference.example: New Rs. 60,000, old Rs. 70,000 → you give the customer Rs. 10,000.

newBalance.title: New balance
newBalance.body: The customer's khata after this exchange: previous balance + difference − paid now.
newBalance.example: Previous Rs. 0, difference Rs. 70,000, paid Rs. 50,000 → new balance Rs. 20,000 on his khata.

page.title: Invoices
page.body: Every bill of the shop in one place: sales, purchases, returns and repairs. Find any bill, see what is still due, open and print it.
page.example: A customer asks for last month's bill → search his mobile number, open it and print it again.

search.title: Find a bill
search.body: Type the bill number, a name, a mobile number or an IMEI, or scan. A search looks through all dates, not only the chosen period.
search.example: Scan the IMEI of a returned phone → its sale bill and its purchase bill both show.

kind.title: Type of bill
kind.body: Show only sales, purchases (owner and manager only), returns or repairs. All shows every type.
kind.example: Tap Repairs → only repair bills for this month.

state.title: Money
state.body: Udhaar left: money still to receive (or to pay, on a purchase). Paid: fully settled. In repair: the repair job is not finished. Returned and Cancelled are closed bills.
state.example: Tap Udhaar left → every bill someone still owes on, e.g. Ali's Rs. 15,000.

toGet.title: Still to get
toGet.body: What is still due on the sale and repair bills in this list (this period and filter). The khata total may differ: it also counts payments and len-den not tied to a bill.
toGet.example: Two bills listed with Rs. 15,000 and Rs. 5,000 due → still to get Rs. 20,000.

toGive.title: Still to pay
toGive.body: What the shop still owes on the purchase bills in this list.
toGive.example: A Hall Road purchase of Rs. 1,00,000 with Rs. 60,000 paid → still to pay Rs. 40,000.

balance.title: Khata balance
balance.body: This person's khata right now. A plus amount means he owes the shop; a minus amount means the shop owes him.
balance.example: Balance Rs. 25,000 → Ali owes you Rs. 25,000. Balance −Rs. 10,000 → you owe him Rs. 10,000.

forBill.title: For this bill
forBill.body: This payment goes against this one bill only, up to what is left on it.
forBill.example: Bill INV-0042 has Rs. 15,000 left; he pays Rs. 15,000 → this bill is cleared.

amount.title: Amount
amount.body: How much money is received or paid. It is put on the person's oldest unpaid bills first; anything more is kept on his khata.
amount.example: Ali has two bills of Rs. 10,000 and Rs. 15,000 and pays Rs. 20,000 → the first is cleared and Rs. 10,000 goes on the second.

lending.title: Len-den
lending.body: Money given or taken with no bill, e.g. a neighbour shop borrows cash. It stays in the person's khata, is kept apart from sales in the reports, and can later be adjusted against a bill.
lending.example: You lend Usman Rs. 20,000 → his khata shows Rs. 20,000 len-den, not a sale.

lendAmount.title: Len-den amount
lendAmount.body: How much money was given or taken. It is not put on any bill now.
lendAmount.example: Imran gives the shop Rs. 50,000 for a week → type 50000.

lendDue.title: Return date
lendDue.body: When the money should come back, or when the shop must return it. After this date it shows as late on Home, and a WhatsApp reminder can be sent.
lendDue.example: Lent Rs. 20,000 to return on the 1st → from the 2nd he shows under "Len-den late".

allocated.title: Applied to
allocated.body: The bills this payment was put against, and how much went on each.

advance.title: Advance kept
advance.body: The part of the payment that was more than his open bills. It stays on his khata in his favour and lowers what he owes next time.
advance.example: He owed Rs. 15,000 and paid Rs. 20,000 → Rs. 5,000 kept as advance.

cash.title: Cash
cash.body: Money in notes, into or out of the galla (cash drawer). The galla balance changes by this amount.
cash.example: Customer pays Rs. 32,000 in notes → the galla goes up by Rs. 32,000.

online.title: Online
online.body: A bank transfer or Easypaisa, JazzCash or another app. Pick the bank or app; the money is counted in that account, not in the galla.
online.example: Customer sends Rs. 45,000 by Easypaisa → it goes into your Easypaisa account, the galla does not change.

bank.title: Which bank or app
bank.body: The bank or wallet the money went through. The common ones are buttons; any other is in the list below them.
bank.example: Paid through Meezan Bank → tap Meezan. Paid through Bank Alfalah → pick it from the list.

chequeDate.title: Cheque date
chequeDate.body: The date written on the cheque; it can be cashed only from that day.
chequeDate.example: Cheque dated 15 March → write 15 March, and do not deposit it before then.

foreign.title: Amount in foreign money
foreign.body: How much was sent, in the other country's currency.
foreign.example: His brother in Riyadh sent 500 SAR → type 500.

rate.title: Rate
rate.body: How many rupees one unit of that currency is worth for this payment.

inRupees.title: In rupees
inRupees.body: Amount × rate. This is the rupee amount booked on the bill or khata.

sender.title: Sender's name
sender.body: Who sent the money from abroad, so you can find it later.

service.title: Sent through
service.body: The service the money came through, e.g. Western Union or a bank. Optional.
service.example: Sent through Western Union → tap Western Union.

mtcn.title: Reference / MTCN
mtcn.body: The tracking number of the transfer (MTCN for Western Union). Optional, but it helps if there is a question later.

fee.title: Service fee
fee.body: What the money service kept. Only the international report uses it (net = amount − fee); the bill still shows the full rupee amount.
fee.example: Rs. 37,100 came in and the service kept Rs. 600 → net Rs. 36,500 in the report.

status.title: Money status
status.body: Pending: not collected yet. Received: collected. Settled: fully done. It is for your own tracking in the international report.
status.example: MTCN given but not yet collected from the bank → Pending.

party.title: Choose the person
party.body: Search your customers and dealers by name or mobile and tap one, or tap + to add a new person. The amount beside a name is his khata balance.
party.example: Type "0300" → Ali (0300 1234567) shows with Rs. 25,000 due; tap him.

walkIn.title: Cash customer
walkIn.body: A walk-in who pays in full now: no name and no khata is kept.
walkIn.example: Someone buys a Rs. 800 charger and pays cash → leave it as cash customer.

docLang.title: Document language
docLang.body: The language of the printed or shared bill: English or Urdu. It does not change the app's own language.
docLang.example: The app is in English but the customer reads Urdu → tap اردو, then print the receipt.

shop.title: Shop
shop.body: Your shop name, city and phone. They are printed at the top of every bill and used in WhatsApp messages.
shop.example: Name "Star Mobiles", city Lahore, phone 0321 5550002 → the bill header reads "Star Mobiles · Lahore · 0321 5550002".

name.title: Shop name
name.body: The name customers know your shop by. It shows on bills, slips and messages.
name.example: "Star Mobiles Hall Road" → every bill starts with this name.

city.title: City
city.body: The city of the shop. Printed under the name on bills.

phone.title: Shop phone
phone.body: The number customers call. It is printed on bills so a customer can reach you about warranty or a balance.
phone.example: Phone 0300 1234567 on the bill → a customer with a fault calls this number.

language.title: Language for prints
language.body: The language of bills, declarations and WhatsApp messages the shop sends. Each person can still choose their own language on their screen.
language.example: Set to Urdu → the bill and the udhaar reminder go out in Urdu, even if the salesman uses the app in English.

staffLogin.title: Staff login
staffLogin.body: How your staff open the app on their phones. You decide whether they may use a fingerprint.
staffLogin.example: Ali (salesman) logs in with his mobile number and password, or with his finger if you allow it.

fingerprint.title: Staff fingerprint login
fingerprint.body: On: staff may switch on fingerprint login on their own phone. Off: they must type the password or PIN every time. The fingerprint never leaves their phone.
fingerprint.example: On → Ali taps "Log in with fingerprint" and is in within a second. Off → Ali types his password.

tax.title: Sales tax
tax.body: Only for shops registered for sales tax with FBR. When it is on, tax is added on bills at the rate you set.
tax.example: Not registered → keep it off; bills have no tax line. Registered at 18% → turn it on.

taxEnabled.title: Charge sales tax
taxEnabled.body: On: every new bill works out sales tax at the rate below and shows it on the bill. Off: no tax on bills. Tax collected is the government's money, not your income.
taxEnabled.example: On at 18%: phone Rs. 10,000 → bill shows tax Rs. 1,800. Off → bill is just Rs. 10,000.

taxRate.title: Tax rate %
taxRate.body: The sales tax percentage used on bills. Type only the number.
taxRate.example: Type 18 → a Rs. 10,000 sale carries Rs. 1,800 tax.

taxInclusive.title: Prices include tax
taxInclusive.body: On: the price you type already has the tax inside it, so the customer pays the same price. Off: tax is added on top of the price.
taxInclusive.example: Price Rs. 11,800 at 18%. On → customer pays Rs. 11,800 (Rs. 1,800 of it is tax). Off on a Rs. 10,000 price → customer pays Rs. 11,800.

receipt.title: Receipt
receipt.body: How your bill numbers start and the line printed at the bottom of every bill.
receipt.example: Prefix "SM" and footer "Thank you, come again" → bill SM-000123 ending with that line.

invoicePrefix.title: Invoice prefix
invoicePrefix.body: The letters in front of every sale bill number. Numbers keep counting on their own; only new bills use a new prefix.

footer.title: Receipt footer
footer.body: A short line printed at the bottom of every English bill — a thank-you or a return rule.
footer.example: "No return after 7 days. Thank you!" appears under the total.

footerUr.title: Receipt footer (Urdu)
footerUr.body: The same bottom line for bills printed in Urdu. If it is empty the English line is used.
footerUr.example: "7 دن بعد واپسی نہیں۔ شکریہ!" under the total of an Urdu bill.

codeWord.title: Sticker cost code
codeWord.body: A secret 10-letter word that turns the buying price into letters on stickers. You can read your cost at a glance; the customer cannot.
codeWord.example: Word BLACKHORSE: 0=B, 1=L, 2=A, 3=C, 4=K, 5=H … Cost Rs. 45,000 → sticker shows KHBBB.

codeWordInput.title: Code word (10 letters)
codeWordInput.body: Type exactly 10 different letters. The 1st letter stands for 0, the 2nd for 1, and so on up to 9. Leave it empty to print no cost code.
codeWordInput.example: MOBILESHOP is not allowed (O is twice). BLACKHORSE works: 3,200 → CABB.

rules.title: Price rules
rules.body: Who may sell a phone under its asking price, and who may change the asking price. Owner and manager always may. Every such sale is listed in Reports → Prices.
rules.example: Rule "Owner / manager": salesman Ali cannot sell a Rs. 52,000 phone for Rs. 50,000 on his own.

rulesBelow.title: Selling under the asking price
rulesBelow.body: Who may finish a sale for less than the asking price on the phone. Anyone: no check. Owner / manager: only they may. With owner PIN: staff may if the owner types the PIN on the spot.
rulesBelow.example: Asking Rs. 45,000, customer wants Rs. 44,000. "With owner PIN" → the owner types his PIN and the sale goes through, recorded with his name.

rulesAsking.title: Changing the asking price
rulesAsking.body: Who may change the asking (selling) price written on a phone in stock. Each change is recorded with who did it.
rulesAsking.example: Rule "Owner / manager": a salesman cannot lower an iPhone 13 from Rs. 1,45,000 to Rs. 1,35,000 by himself.

rulesPin.title: With owner PIN
rulesPin.body: The owner types his own quick PIN on the salesman's screen to approve, without logging the salesman out. The approval is saved with the owner's name.
rulesPin.example: Salesman asks to sell under asking; owner standing at the counter types 4321 → approved and recorded.

auditPrefs.title: Stock audit thresholds
auditPrefs.body: The limits the Shop Audit uses to sort your stock: how many days is fresh, slow or dead, what is a costly phone, what is a thin margin, and when skipped ID checks look odd. Change them to suit your shop.
auditPrefs.example: Bands 15 / 30 / 60 / 90: a phone 40 days in the shop shows as "slow"; after 90 days it is "dead stock".

ageFresh.title: Fresh up to (days)
ageFresh.body: A phone in stock this many days or fewer counts as fresh in the audit.
ageFresh.example: 15 → a Samsung A15 bought 10 days ago is fresh.

ageNormal.title: Normal up to (days)
ageNormal.body: After the fresh days and up to this day the phone is normal. After this a costly phone starts to show an alert.
ageNormal.example: 30 → a phone 25 days in the shop is normal; at 31 days a high-value one is flagged.

ageSlow.title: Slow up to (days)
ageSlow.body: Between the normal days and this day the phone is slow-moving: think about a lower price.
ageSlow.example: 60 → an Infinix Hot 40 unsold for 45 days is slow.

ageAttention.title: Attention up to (days)
ageAttention.body: Up to this day the phone needs attention. After it, the phone is dead stock and is listed as an alert.
ageAttention.example: 90 → a phone 100 days in the shop is dead stock: money stuck in it.

highValue.title: High value from (Rs.)
highValue.body: A phone whose buying price is this much or more is "high value". If it sits past the normal days, the audit warns you.
highValue.example: Rs. 50,000 → an iPhone 13 bought for Rs. 1,20,000 and 35 days unsold shows a warning.

lowMargin.title: Thin margin under (%)
lowMargin.body: If the asking price is less than this % above the buying price, the audit marks the phone "low margin".
lowMargin.example: 5% → bought Rs. 40,000, asking Rs. 41,000 (2.5% more) → low margin.

bypassMin.title: Unusual from (skips)
bypassMin.body: How many times one person may skip the ID / CNIC check when buying a used phone before the audit calls it unusual (together with the share below).
bypassMin.example: 3 → Ali skipped the ID check on 4 used phones this month → he is listed.

bypassShare.title: … and share of own intakes (%)
bypassShare.body: The skips must also be at least this % of the phones that person bought. Both limits together decide.
bypassShare.example: 50% → Ali bought 6 used phones and skipped 4 (67%) → unusual. Bought 20, skipped 4 (20%) → not.

items.title: Item settings
items.body: How accessories and other counted items are valued, whether their count may go below zero, and how many pieces are in a dozen, box or carton.
items.example: Chargers: weighted average cost, no selling past zero, 1 box = 10 pieces.

valuation.title: Stock valuation
valuation.body: How the buying price of an accessory that is sold is worked out. Weighted average: the average of everything bought. FIFO: the oldest batch is sold first, at its own price. It changes profit, not the selling price.
valuation.example: Bought 10 cables at Rs. 100, later 10 at Rs. 140; sell 1. Average → cost Rs. 120. FIFO → cost Rs. 100 (oldest batch).

negative.title: Allow selling past zero stock
negative.body: Off: the app stops a sale when the item count would go below zero. On: it lets the sale through and the count shows minus until you enter the purchase.
negative.example: App shows 0 handsfree but 5 are on the shelf (purchase not entered yet). On → you can sell 2 and the count shows -2.

units.title: Pieces in a pack
units.body: How many pieces one dozen, box or carton holds in your shop. When you buy by the box the app counts pieces from this.
units.example: Box = 10: buying 3 boxes of chargers adds 30 pieces to stock.

unitDozen.title: Pieces in a dozen
unitDozen.body: Usually 12. Used when you buy or sell by the dozen.

unitBox.title: Pieces in a box
unitBox.body: How many pieces come in one box from your supplier.

unitCarton.title: Pieces in a carton
unitCarton.body: How many pieces come in one carton.

devices.title: Device settings
devices.body: Rules for phones, tablets and watches: whether a used mobile must have its lock check, and the grades you give used units.
devices.example: Lock check on and grades "a, b, refurbished" → every used phone you buy is checked and graded.

lockCheck.title: Lock check for used mobiles
lockCheck.body: On: a used mobile can be bought only after you mark its locks (iCloud / Google account / FRP) as cleared or not. A unit with a lock still on can never be sold. Tablets and watches always need it.
lockCheck.example: On → buying a used iPhone 11, the app asks "iCloud cleared?" before saving. Off → you may skip it for phones.

grades.title: Grades of used units
grades.body: The condition grades you pick from when you buy a used phone, tablet or watch, separated by commas. They show on stock and stickers.
grades.example: "a, b, refurbished, copy" → a clean used Samsung A15 is graded "a", a scratched one "b".

card.title: Logo & business details
card.body: Your logo and business details. They make the printed bill look like your shop's own and are shown in the app.
card.example: Upload the logo and address once → every sale bill and repair slip carries them.

logo.title: Logo
logo.body: Your shop's picture or sign. It is printed at the top of bills when "Logo" is on under Printed bill. A large picture is made smaller on its own.
logo.example: Upload a photo of your signboard → it appears above the shop name on every bill.

legalName.title: Registered business name
legalName.body: The name on your tax or company papers, if it is different from the shop name.
legalName.example: Shop "Star Mobiles", registered as "Star Traders (SMC-Pvt) Ltd".

tagline.title: Tagline (English)
tagline.body: A short line under your name on English bills.

taglineUr.title: Tagline (Urdu)
taglineUr.body: The same short line for bills printed in Urdu.

whatsapp.title: WhatsApp number
whatsapp.body: The shop's WhatsApp number, printed on bills so customers can message you.
whatsapp.example: 0321 5550002 → customer sends a photo of a fault to this number.

email.title: Email
email.body: The shop's email address, for bills and dealers. Optional.

website.title: Website / page
website.body: Your website or online page, if you have one.

type.title: Business type
type.body: How the business is owned: one owner, partners, a company and so on. Tap again to clear it.
type.example: Two brothers run the shop together → Partnership.

registration.title: Registration no.
registration.body: A registration number from SECP or the chamber of commerce, if you have one.
registration.example: SECP 0123456 printed for dealers who ask for it.

since.title: In business since
since.body: The year the shop started. Customers trust an old shop.

province.title: Province
province.body: The province of the shop. Useful for the tax registration. Tap again to clear.

hours.title: Opening hours
hours.body: When the shop is open, in your own words.

social.title: Social pages
social.body: Your Facebook, Instagram or TikTok name. Printed on bills only if "Facebook / Instagram / TikTok" is on under Printed bill.
social.example: Instagram "starmobiles.pk" → customers find your new stock videos.

owner.title: Owner details
owner.body: The owner's name and CNIC. Printed on the bill only if "Owner's name" is on; also needed for tax papers.

ownerName.title: Owner / proprietor name
ownerName.body: The full name of the shop owner.

ownerCnic.title: Owner CNIC
ownerCnic.body: The owner's 13-digit ID card number. The dashes come on their own.

taxCard.title: Tax registration (FBR)
taxCard.body: Your FBR numbers. They are printed on bills when filled and "NTN / STRN" is on. Charging tax itself is set in the Sales tax card.
taxCard.example: NTN 1234567-8 on every bill for a corporate customer who needs it.

ntn.title: NTN
ntn.body: National Tax Number from FBR, for income tax.

strn.title: STRN
strn.body: Sales Tax Registration Number, only if you are registered for sales tax.

fbrPos.title: FBR POS ID
fbrPos.body: Only for shops in FBR's point-of-sale scheme: the ID FBR gave your counter. Leave empty otherwise.
fbrPos.example: POS ID 123456 printed on the bill.

currency.title: Currency
currency.body: Money is always Pakistani rupees. Here you choose only how amounts are written on screen and on bills.

symbol.title: Sign
symbol.body: The sign written with every amount.

paisa.title: Paisa
paisa.body: Rupees only hides the paisa; "always show paisa" adds .00 to every amount. The amount itself does not change.
paisa.example: Rupees only → Rs. 45,000. Always paisa → Rs. 45,000.00.

preview.title: Looks like
preview.body: A sample of how amounts will look with your choices, before you save.
preview.example: Choosing "after" and PKR → the sample shows 45,000 PKR.

printCard.title: Printed bill
printCard.body: Switch on or off what appears on sale bills and repair slips, and write your terms and bank details.
printCard.example: Logo on, owner's name off, terms on → the bill shows the logo and your return rule but not your name.

logo.title: Logo on the bill
logo.body: On: your uploaded logo is printed at the top. Off: only the name.
logo.example: On → Star Mobiles logo above the bill.

tagline.title: Tagline on the bill
tagline.body: On: your tagline is printed under the name.
tagline.example: On → "All brands · New & used" under the shop name.

ntn.title: Tax numbers on the bill
ntn.body: On: NTN, STRN and FBR POS ID (the ones filled in) are printed on the bill.

owner.title: Owner's name on the bill
owner.body: On: the owner's name is printed on the bill.
owner.example: On → "Prop: Abdur Rehman" on every bill.

bank.title: Bank details on the bill
bank.body: On: your bank and wallet details are printed, so a customer with a balance can pay online.
bank.example: On → "HBL 1234… / Easypaisa 0300 1234567" at the bottom of an udhaar bill.

terms.title: Terms on the bill
terms.body: On: your terms (returns / warranty) are printed at the bottom.
terms.example: On → "No return after 7 days" on every bill.

social.title: Social pages on the bill
social.body: On: your Facebook / Instagram / TikTok names are printed.

terms.title: Terms (English)
terms.body: Your return and warranty rules, printed on English bills when Terms is on.
terms.example: "No return after 7 days. Warranty by the company. Box and bill needed."

termsUr.title: Terms (Urdu)
termsUr.body: The same rules for bills printed in Urdu.
termsUr.example: "7 دن بعد واپسی نہیں۔ وارنٹی کمپنی کی۔ ڈبہ اور بل ساتھ لائیں۔"

bank.title: Bank details on the bill
bank.body: The account a customer can pay a balance into. Printed only when "Bank / wallet details" is on.
bank.example: Customer owes Rs. 12,000 → he sends it to the HBL account printed on his bill.

bankTitle.title: Account title
bankTitle.body: The name the account is in, exactly as the bank shows it.
bankTitle.example: Star Mobiles or Abdur Rehman Afzal.

iban.title: IBAN
iban.body: The 24-character account code starting with PK. Transfers from other banks need it.

wallet.title: Easypaisa / JazzCash
wallet.body: A mobile wallet number customers can pay into.
wallet.example: Easypaisa 0300 1234567 → customer pays Rs. 5,000 from his phone.

card.title: Barcode settings
card.body: Every phone and item gets its own barcode the moment it is bought. A barcode never changes. Here you choose how new barcodes are made.
card.example: Buy a Samsung A15 → it gets MS000124; scan that sticker at the counter to sell it.

type.title: Barcode type
type.body: The kind of barcode printed on new labels. Code 128 reads on every scanner; EAN-13 is digits only; QR needs a 2-D scanner or a phone camera. Old labels keep working.
type.example: A cheap laser scanner → keep Code 128. Scanning with phone cameras → QR.

prefix.title: Shop prefix
prefix.body: Up to 6 letters or digits in front of every new barcode number, so your labels are easy to tell apart.

start.title: Start numbering from
start.body: The number the next barcode starts at. It can only move forward, so two labels never get the same code.
start.example: Old system ended at 5,000 → start from 5001; the next label is MS005001.

mode.title: Barcode value
mode.body: What the barcode of a new phone holds: prefix + number, or the phone's own IMEI. Accessories always get prefix + number.
mode.example: IMEI chosen → the sticker on a new Infinix Hot 40 scans as its IMEI 356789012345678.

next.title: Next barcode
next.body: The code the next phone or item you buy will get, and its type.
next.example: Next: MS000125 · code128 → the next purchase gets MS000125.

testPrint.title: Test print
testPrint.body: Prints one sample label of the chosen type, to check your printer and that your scanner reads it.
testPrint.example: Print, then scan the label in "Test scan" below → it should beep.

backfill.title: Barcodes for old stock
backfill.body: Gives a barcode to every phone and item that was entered before barcodes existed. Nothing else changes; existing barcodes stay.
backfill.example: 40 old phones without a code → tap once → all 40 get one; print their labels.

testScan.title: Test scan
testScan.body: Scan any label here (or type the code and press Enter) to see what the app finds. It sells nothing.
testScan.example: Scan the sticker of an iPhone 13 → it shows "iPhone 13 · 3567…". "Item not found" means the code is not in your stock.

daily.title: Daily work
daily.body: The jobs you do every day at the counter: sell, buy, returns, khata, repairs and the day's hisaab.
daily.example: A customer buys a phone → "Sell". A man sells you his old phone → "Add stock".

stock.title: Stock
stock.body: Everything about what is in the shop: phones, accessories, their value, counting and the list of brands and models.
stock.example: Want to know how many Samsung A15 are left → "Stock list".

records.title: Records
records.body: Lists of everything done before: bills, sales, purchases, money in and out, returns and the people you deal with.
records.example: A customer asks for last month's bill → "Invoices" and search his name.

accounts.title: Money & reports
accounts.body: Expenses, closing the day, cash and bank accounts, reports and the shop audit. Owner and manager only.
accounts.example: End of month: "Reports" shows the real profit after rent and salaries.

admin.title: Shop & staff
admin.body: Owner tools: shop settings, staff, notifications, software fees and your quick PIN.

sell.title: Sell
sell.body: Make a sale bill: scan or pick the phone or item, set the price, take cash, online or udhaar. Stock, khata and the galla update on their own.
sell.example: Sell a Samsung A15 for Rs. 38,000, customer pays Rs. 30,000 → Rs. 8,000 goes on his khata.

addStock.title: Add stock
addStock.body: Enter a purchase: new phones from a dealer, a used phone from a walk-in customer, or accessories. Each phone gets its barcode and history.
addStock.example: Bought 5 Infinix Hot 40 from a Hall Road dealer at Rs. 33,000 each on udhaar → stock +5, dealer khata +Rs. 1,65,000.

returnJob.title: Return
returnJob.body: A customer brings back what he bought, or you send something back to a supplier. Money is refunded or adjusted on the khata, and the phone comes back into stock.
returnJob.example: Customer returns a handsfree bought for Rs. 1,500 → refund Rs. 1,500 from the galla, stock +1.

installments.title: Installments (qist)
installments.body: Sell on monthly installments: set the advance, number of months and due dates, and see who has a qist due or late.
installments.example: iPhone 13 for Rs. 1,50,000: advance Rs. 50,000, then 10 months of Rs. 10,000.

assistant.title: Assistant
assistant.body: Ask a question about your shop in your own words and get the answer from your own records.
assistant.example: "How many phones did I sell this week?" → "14 phones, Rs. 5,20,000".

repairs.title: Repairs
repairs.body: Take in a phone for repair, track its work and parts, and hand it back with the bill.
repairs.example: Screen change on a Redmi Note 12: job card today, ready tomorrow, customer pays Rs. 6,500.

exchange.title: Exchange (old for new)
exchange.body: The customer gives his old phone and takes another one, paying the difference. One bill does both the purchase and the sale.
exchange.example: Old Samsung A12 taken for Rs. 18,000, new A15 sold for Rs. 38,000 → customer pays Rs. 20,000.

loans.title: Loans (amanat)
loans.body: A phone handed to another shop without money changing hands yet. It stays yours until it comes back, or the other shop keeps it and it becomes a sale to that shop.
loans.example: You give an iPhone 12 to a shop on Hall Road to show a customer → it shows "on loan" until it comes back or is billed.

hisaab.title: Day's hisaab
hisaab.body: Today's summary: sales, purchases, money in and out of the galla and bank, udhaar given and received.
hisaab.example: Tonight: sales Rs. 1,20,000, expenses Rs. 3,000, galla should have Rs. 62,000.

stock.title: Stock list
stock.body: Every phone, tablet and watch in the shop with its IMEI, condition, cost and asking price. Search, filter and open its history.
stock.example: Filter "Used · Non-PTA" → 6 phones; tap one to see who sold it to you and when.

stockWorth.title: Stock in shop
stockWorth.body: How many phones you have, by brand and model, and what they are worth at cost and at asking price.
stockWorth.example: Samsung 12 phones, cost Rs. 4,80,000, asking Rs. 5,40,000.

accessories.title: Accessories
accessories.body: Chargers, cables, covers, handsfree and other counted items: quantity in hand, cost, price and every movement.
accessories.example: Type-C cable: 38 pieces, cost Rs. 120, price Rs. 250.

imeiSearch.title: IMEI search
imeiSearch.body: Find a phone by its IMEI (type or scan it). It opens the stock list with the search box ready.
imeiSearch.example: Type the last digits 4512 → the phone with IMEI ending 4512 appears.

openingStock.title: Old stock
openingStock.body: Add phones that were already on your shelf before you started the app. No money is paid, so the day's hisaab does not change.
openingStock.example: First day: add the 25 phones already in the shop with their buying prices.

count.title: Stock count
count.body: Count the phones and items on the shelf by scanning them; the app shows what is missing or extra compared with its records.
count.example: Scan 48 phones; app expected 50 → 2 missing, listed by IMEI.
