catalogue.title: Brands & models
catalogue.body: The list of brands, models, storage sizes and colours you pick from when buying. Fix spellings or add your own.
catalogue.example: Add "Tecno Spark 20 Pro" once → it appears in the list on the next purchase.

invoices.title: Invoices
invoices.body: Every sale bill with its number, customer, amount and what is still due. Open one to print it again or send it on WhatsApp.
invoices.example: Find bill INV-000231 → print a copy for the customer.

sales.title: Sales list
sales.body: Every phone and item sold, newest first, with price and customer.
sales.example: See that 3 iPhones were sold yesterday and to whom.

purchases.title: Purchases list
purchases.body: Every purchase bill: from whom, when, the total and what you still owe. Tap one to see its phones, return them or cancel the bill.
purchases.example: Purchase P-000045 from Ali Traders: Rs. 1,65,000, paid Rs. 1,00,000 → still owe Rs. 65,000.

payments.title: Money received / paid
payments.body: Every payment on a khata: money a customer paid you, or money you paid a dealer. Green is in, red is out.
payments.example: Bilal paid Rs. 10,000 on Easypaisa → shows +10,000; you paid Ali Traders Rs. 50,000 → shows -50,000.

returns.title: Returns list
returns.body: Every return: sales a customer brought back and purchases you sent back, with the amount and whether money was refunded or adjusted on the khata.
returns.example: Return R-000012: customer returned a cover, Rs. 800 refunded.

parties.title: People & khata
parties.body: Everyone you deal with — customers, dealers, other shops — with their khata balance: who owes you and whom you owe.
parties.example: Bilal owes Rs. 12,000; you owe Ali Traders Rs. 65,000.

expenses.title: Expenses
expenses.body: Shop costs that are not stock: rent, electricity, salaries, tea. They are taken away from profit.
expenses.example: Rent Rs. 40,000 paid from the bank → profit this month is Rs. 40,000 lower.

dayClose.title: Close the day
dayClose.body: At night count the cash in the galla and type it. The app compares it with what should be there and keeps the difference on record.
dayClose.example: App expects Rs. 62,000, you count Rs. 61,500 → short by Rs. 500, saved with your name.

cash.title: Cash & bank
cash.body: Every place the shop keeps money — the galla, bank accounts, Easypaisa, JazzCash — with its balance worked out from every sale, payment and expense. Open one to see its cash book; move money between them.
cash.example: Galla Rs. 40,000 + HBL Rs. 2,00,000 + Easypaisa Rs. 15,000.

reports.title: Reports
reports.body: Profit and loss for any days, best sellers, a 7-day estimate, old stock, stock by type and price changes. Download any of them for your accountant.
reports.example: This month: sales Rs. 12,50,000, profit after expenses Rs. 1,40,000.

settings.title: Shop settings
settings.body: Everything about how your shop works in the app: name and bill, tax, language, price rules, barcodes, item and device rules, audit limits. Owner only.
settings.example: Turn on "Lock check for used mobiles" → no used phone is bought without its iCloud / Google check.

staff.title: Staff
staff.body: Add the people who work in your shop, give each a role, mark their hazri and see what each one did. Owner only.
staff.example: Add Ali as salesman → he can sell and buy but cannot see your buying prices or profit.

notifications.title: Notifications
notifications.body: Choose which WhatsApp or email messages the app sends: to you on each sale, a night report, udhaar reminders, and bills to customers. Owner only.
notifications.example: Night report on at 9:30 pm → every night you get the day's hisaab on WhatsApp.

fees.title: Software fees
fees.body: Your plan for this software, until when it is paid, where to pay, and how to report a payment or use a renewal code. Owner only.
fees.example: Paid until 30 November; send Rs. 2,000 on JazzCash and report it with the transaction ID.

pin.title: Quick PIN
pin.body: A 4–6 digit PIN to open the app fast on your phone instead of the full password. The owner's PIN also approves a salesman's under-price sale.
pin.example: Set PIN 4321 → next time type 4321 to log in.

pinPassword.title: Your password
pinPassword.body: Your full login password, to prove it is you before the PIN is set.
pinPassword.example: Type the password you log in with, then the new PIN.

pinNew.title: New PIN
pinNew.body: 4 to 6 digits that only you know. Avoid 1234 or your phone number.

shops.title: My shops
shops.body: If you run more than one shop, pick which one you are working in. Each shop's stock, khata and cash are kept apart.
shops.example: Tap "Star Mobiles Saddar" → everything you see is now that branch's.

app.title: App
app.body: How the app looks on this phone only: language, colours and light or dark. It does not change bills or other people's screens.
app.example: You pick Urdu here; your salesman can still use English on his phone.

language.title: Language
language.body: The language of the screens on this phone: Urdu, Roman Urdu or English. Bills follow the shop's print language in Settings.

look.title: Look
look.body: The colour style of the app on this phone. Only the look changes; nothing in your data.
look.example: Pick "Navy" → dark blue headers and cards.

theme.title: Appearance
theme.body: Light, dark, or follow the phone's own setting. Dark is easier on the eyes at night.
theme.example: Pick "System" → the app turns dark when your phone does.

fingerprint.title: Fingerprint login
fingerprint.body: Log in on this phone with one touch instead of the password. Your fingerprint stays on the phone; the app never sees it. Staff can use it only if the owner allows it in Settings.
fingerprint.example: Turn on → next time tap "Log in with fingerprint" and touch the sensor.

purchaseDoc.title: Purchase bill
purchaseDoc.body: One purchase: who you bought from, the phones and items on it, the total, what you paid and what you still owe. You can return lines or cancel it from here.
purchaseDoc.example: P-000045 from Ali Traders: 5 phones, Rs. 1,65,000, paid Rs. 1,00,000 → due Rs. 65,000.

purchaseFrom.title: Bought from
purchaseFrom.body: The dealer or person you bought from. Tap the name to open his khata.
purchaseFrom.example: Ali Traders → his khata shows this bill and what you owe him.

addedBy.title: Added by
addedBy.body: The staff member who entered this bill in the app.
addedBy.example: Added by Ali → he entered it from his phone.

purchaseTotal.title: Total
purchaseTotal.body: The full amount of this purchase: all phones and items on it, after any discount.

purchasePaid.title: Paid
purchasePaid.body: What you have paid the seller for this bill so far, at the time of buying and later.
purchasePaid.example: Paid Rs. 1,00,000 cash on the day.

purchaseReturned.title: Returned
purchaseReturned.body: The value of phones or items from this bill that you sent back to the seller.
purchaseReturned.example: One phone of Rs. 33,000 returned → shows -33,000.

purchaseDue.title: Due
purchaseDue.body: What you still owe the seller on this bill: total minus paid minus returned. It is on his khata.

purchaseRefund.title: Refund amount
purchaseRefund.body: Cash the seller hands back to you now for the returned items. Leave 0 if he does not pay back: the amount then comes off what you owe him on his khata.
purchaseRefund.example: Return a Rs. 33,000 phone: dealer gives Rs. 33,000 cash → type 33000. He keeps it against your balance → leave 0.

returnReason.title: Reason
returnReason.body: Why it is going back, in a few words. It stays on the return record.

kindStock.title: Phones (stock)
kindStock.body: Many phones in one sheet, one row each with IMEI, brand, model, condition, PTA, cost and asking price. With a supplier the rows become a purchase bill; without one they are old stock.
kindStock.example: 50 old phones on the shelf → one sheet, one upload.

kindPeople.title: People
kindPeople.body: Customers and dealers with their phone, type and an opening balance if there is one.
kindPeople.example: Copy your old register: Bilal, 0321 5550002, owes Rs. 12,000.

kindItems.title: Accessories
kindItems.body: Accessories with the quantity in hand, unit cost and sale price.
kindItems.example: Type-C cable, 40 pieces, cost Rs. 120, price Rs. 250.

kindSales.title: Sales
kindSales.body: Sales of phones that are already in stock in the app: IMEI, price, paid and customer. What is not paid goes on the customer's khata.
kindSales.example: Last week's 12 sales from the notebook → one upload.

kindExpenses.title: Expenses
kindExpenses.body: Expenses with date, category, amount and the account paid from.
kindExpenses.example: October rent Rs. 40,000, electricity Rs. 9,500, tea Rs. 3,000.

step1.title: Download the sheet
step1.body: An Excel file in the right layout, with yellow sample rows, a Help sheet and drop-down lists. The sample rows are skipped on their own.
step1.example: Download, open in Excel, write your phones under the samples.

step2.title: Fill it in Excel
step2.body: Write one row per phone, person, item, sale or expense. Keep the column names as they are.

step3.title: Upload and check
step3.body: Choose the filled file (Excel or CSV, up to 2,000 rows) and press Check. The app reads every row and tells you what is wrong. Nothing is saved yet.
step3.example: Upload 50 rows → 47 ok, 2 notes, 1 error (IMEI has 14 digits).

optCatalogue.title: Create new brands and models
optCatalogue.body: On: a brand or model in the sheet that is not in your list is added on its own. Off: such rows show an error so you can fix the spelling.
optCatalogue.example: Sheet says "Tecno Spark 20". On → the model is created. Off → "model not found".

optBelowCost.title: Allow selling under cost
optBelowCost.body: On: sales in the sheet priced below the phone's buying price are accepted (you confirm the loss). Off: those rows show an error.
optBelowCost.example: Phone cost Rs. 40,000, sheet says sold for Rs. 38,000. Off → error. On → saved with a Rs. 2,000 loss.

optSkip.title: Skip rows with errors
optSkip.body: Off: if any row has an error, nothing is imported (all or nothing). On: the good rows are imported and the rows with errors are left out for you to fix.
optSkip.example: 50 rows, 1 error. Off → fix it first. On → 49 saved, 1 left out.

preview.title: Check result
preview.body: What the app found in your file, row by row, before anything is saved. Tap a row to see every message and value.
preview.example: Row 12: "IMEI already in stock" → remove it from the sheet.

counts.title: Row counts
counts.body: ok: will be saved. note: will be saved but read the note. error: cannot be saved until fixed. skipped: sample or empty rows, ignored.
counts.example: 45 ok · 3 note · 2 error · 3 skipped → fix 2 rows or tick "skip rows with errors".

done.title: Imported
done.body: What was saved by the import: how many phones, bills, people and so on, and how many rows were left out.
done.example: 48 phones and 1 purchase bill saved · 2 rows left out.

export.title: Download my data
export.body: Your current data in the same layout as the sheet, as Excel or CSV. Fix it in Excel and upload it back if needed, or keep it as a backup.
export.example: Download stock → change 20 asking prices in Excel → keep a copy for the accountant.

history.title: Earlier imports
history.body: Every import done before: what kind, the file, who did it, when and what it created. If the same file is uploaded again the app warns you.

staff.title: Staff list
staff.body: Everyone who can log in to your shop, with their role. Tap a person to change the role, reset the password or disable them.
staff.example: Ali · Salesman, Usman · Technician, Kashif · Manager.

hazri.title: Hazri (attendance)
hazri.body: Each person's attendance for the chosen days: present, half day, leave, absent, and "no record" for days nobody marked. Tap a person to mark a day.
hazri.example: This month Ali: 20 present, 2 half, 1 leave, 0 absent, 1 no record.

activity.title: Activity
activity.body: What each person did in the chosen days: sales (how many · Rs), money received, purchases, expenses, repairs and the number of actions in the app. Tap a person to see the full list.
activity.example: Today Ali: 4 sales · Rs. 1,52,000, received Rs. 90,000, 1 purchase, 23 actions.

name.title: Name
name.body: The staff member's name as it will show on bills he makes and in reports.

phone.title: Mobile number
phone.body: His own mobile number. He logs in with this number.
phone.example: 0300 1112233 → Ali types this number to log in.

password.title: Password
password.body: At least 6 characters. Tell it to him privately; he logs in with his number and this password.

pin.title: Quick PIN
pin.body: Optional 4–6 digits for fast login on the shop phone instead of the password.
pin.example: PIN 2580 → Ali opens the app in two seconds.

role.title: Role
role.body: What the person may do. Salesman: sell, buy, take payments; cannot see buying prices or profit. Technician: repair work only. Manager: everything except staff and shop settings, and sees cost and profit.
role.example: Ali as Salesman sees a phone's asking price Rs. 45,000 but not that it cost Rs. 40,000.

resetPassword.title: New password
resetPassword.body: Type a new password if he forgot his. The old one stops working.
resetPassword.example: Ali forgot it → type ali@1122 and Save; tell him the new one.

disable.title: Disable / enable
disable.body: Disable stops the person from logging in, at once. Nothing he did is deleted; his bills and history stay. Enable lets him back in.
disable.example: Ali left the job → Disable; his past sales still show his name.

hazriMark.title: Mark hazri
hazriMark.body: Set or correct this person's attendance for one day. Marking the same day again replaces it.
hazriMark.example: Ali forgot to check in yesterday → day = yesterday, Present, Save.

hazriStatus.title: Status for the day
hazriStatus.body: Present, half day, leave (allowed off) or absent (did not come without leave).
hazriStatus.example: Usman came at 3 pm → Half day.

toOwner.title: To the owner
toOwner.body: Messages that come to you: on each sale or purchase, by WhatsApp or email. Put your own number and email here.
toOwner.example: Sale on: Ali sells a phone at 4 pm → you get "Sale INV-000231 Rs. 38,000" on WhatsApp.

ownerWhatsapp.title: Owner WhatsApp number
ownerWhatsapp.body: Your own WhatsApp number. Sale alerts and the night report go here.

ownerEmail.title: Owner email
ownerEmail.body: Your email, for the messages you choose to get by email.

ownerOnSale.title: On every sale
ownerOnSale.body: On: you get a message each time anyone in the shop makes a sale, with the bill number and amount.
ownerOnSale.example: On → while you are away you see every sale as it happens.

ownerOnPurchase.title: On stock added
ownerOnPurchase.body: On: you get a message each time a purchase (stock in) is entered.
ownerOnPurchase.example: Salesman buys a used iPhone 11 for Rs. 70,000 → you are told at once.

sending.title: How WhatsApp is sent
sending.body: If the WhatsApp Business API is set on the server, messages go out by themselves. If not, each message opens in WhatsApp and you tap Send.
sending.example: No API → a sale alert waits in "Messages" below; tap Share → WhatsApp opens with the text ready.

emailSending.title: How email is sent
emailSending.body: Email goes out only when an email account (SMTP) is set on the server by your software provider. Until then email messages wait in the list.
emailSending.example: No SMTP → the night report by email waits in "Messages"; ask the provider to set it up.

dailyReport.title: Night report to the owner
dailyReport.body: Once a day, at the time you set, the day's hisaab is sent to you: phones sold and sales, cash in hand, udhaar given and received, expenses, profit and stock.
dailyReport.example: At 9:30 pm: "Sales Rs. 1,20,000 · Expenses Rs. 3,000 · Galla Rs. 62,000".

dailyReportOn.title: Send the day's hisaab every night
dailyReportOn.body: On: the night report is sent by WhatsApp or email (whichever you tick). Off: it is not sent, but you can still send it by hand.
dailyReportOn.example: WhatsApp on → every night at 9:30 the hisaab reaches 0321 5550002.

reportTime.title: Report time
reportTime.body: The time of day the night report is sent, in shop time.
reportTime.example: 21:30 → sent at 9:30 pm after the shop closes.

sendNow.title: Send today's hisaab now
sendNow.body: Sends today's report to your WhatsApp or email right now, without waiting for the night.
sendNow.example: Leaving early at 6 pm → tap it to get the hisaab so far.

reminders.title: Udhaar reminders
reminders.body: The app can remind customers who owe you on WhatsApp, once a day at a set time, only if their account has not moved for some days, and not again until that many days pass.
reminders.example: After 7 days: Bilal owes Rs. 12,000 and paid nothing for 9 days → he gets a polite reminder at 11 am.

remindAuto.title: Remind customers automatically
remindAuto.body: On: every day at the time below, customers who owe you and whose khata has not moved for the set days get a WhatsApp reminder. Off: you send reminders by hand only.
remindAuto.example: On → no need to call 15 customers; the app reminds them.

remindAfter.title: When the account has sat for
remindAfter.body: Days since the customer's last bill or payment before a reminder goes. The same customer is not reminded again until this many days pass.
remindAfter.example: 7 days: Bilal last paid on the 1st → reminded on the 8th, then not before the 15th.

remindTime.title: Reminder time
remindTime.body: The time of day automatic reminders go out, in shop time. Pick a polite hour.
remindTime.example: 11:00 → reminders reach customers at 11 am, not late at night.

toCustomer.title: To the customer
toCustomer.body: Messages that go to the customer or seller: the sale bill, a receipt when they pay, and a slip to a person who sold you a phone.
toCustomer.example: Sale on WhatsApp → Bilal gets his bill on his phone right after paying.

customerOnSale.title: Bill to the customer
customerOnSale.body: On: after every sale the customer gets the bill by WhatsApp or email (if his number / email is saved).
customerOnSale.example: Customer with number 0321… buys a cover → he gets "INV-000232 Rs. 800, thank you".

customerOnPayment.title: Receipt on payment
customerOnPayment.body: On: when a customer pays on his khata he gets a WhatsApp receipt with the new balance.
customerOnPayment.example: Bilal pays Rs. 5,000 → "Received Rs. 5,000. Remaining Rs. 7,000."

sellerOnPurchase.title: Slip to the seller
sellerOnPurchase.body: On: a person who sells you a phone gets a WhatsApp slip of the deal — proof of what he sold and for how much.
sellerOnPurchase.example: A walk-in sells you his Redmi Note 12 for Rs. 28,000 → he gets the purchase slip on WhatsApp.

language.title: Message language
language.body: The language of messages sent to customers. "Shop default" uses the print language from Settings.
language.example: Shop prints in English but your customers read Urdu → pick Urdu here.

queue.title: Messages
queue.body: Every message the app made, newest first: sent, waiting (queued) or failed. A waiting WhatsApp message opens with Share; then tap "Mark sent".
queue.example: Reminder to Bilal is "Queued" → Share → send in WhatsApp → Mark sent.

plan.title: Your plan
plan.body: The software plan your shop is on and its state. The colour turns amber when the end is near and red when it has ended.
plan.example: Plan "basic", paid until 30 November, 12 days left.

monthly.title: Monthly fee
monthly.body: What the software costs your shop each month.

paidUntil.title: Paid until
paidUntil.body: The last day your fee covers. Pay before it to keep everything working. Your data is never deleted.
paidUntil.example: Paid until 30 Nov → pay 1 month on 28 Nov → paid until 30 Dec.

payInto.title: Pay into one of these
payInto.body: The software provider's bank and wallet accounts. Tap Copy to copy a number, then pay from your bank app, Easypaisa or JazzCash.
payInto.example: Copy the JazzCash number → send Rs. 2,000 → keep the transaction ID.

report.title: I have paid
report.body: After paying, tell the provider here: amount, months, how you paid and the transaction ID or a screenshot. Your plan is extended when they approve it.
report.example: Paid Rs. 6,000 for 3 months on Easypaisa, ID 01234567890 → Send → "Being checked" → "Received".

amount.title: Amount (Rs)
amount.body: How much you sent. It fills itself as monthly fee × months; change it if you paid a different amount.

months.title: Months
months.body: How many months this payment is for.

method.title: Paid through
method.body: Which of the provider's accounts you paid into.
method.example: You sent it to the JazzCash account → tap JazzCash.

reference.title: Transaction ID
reference.body: The ID or reference number from the payment SMS or app, so the provider can find your payment.

paidOn.title: Paid on
paidOn.body: The date you made the payment.

proof.title: Screenshot
proof.body: A photo or screenshot of the payment. It helps the provider approve faster.
proof.example: Screenshot of the JazzCash "Transaction successful" screen.

code.title: Renewal code
code.body: A code the provider sends you on WhatsApp after payment. Paste it here to extend your plan at once — it works even without internet.
code.example: Code received → paste → Renew → "Paid until 30 Dec".

codePaste.title: Paste the code
codePaste.body: Paste the whole code exactly as received. A code works only once.

backup.title: Backup my data
backup.body: Downloads every list (stock, khata, sales, purchases, expenses…) as Excel files in one zip. Works even when the plan has ended.
backup.example: Once a month: Backup → keep the zip on your computer or Google Drive.

history.title: Your payments
history.body: Every fee payment you reported and its state: being checked, received or not accepted. Print the receipt of a received one.
history.example: October Rs. 2,000 · Received → tap the receipt number to print it.

move.title: Move money between accounts
move.body: Moves money from one of your accounts to another — the galla to the bank, or the bank to the galla. It is not a sale or an expense: only the two balances change.
move.example: Deposit Rs. 1,00,000 from the galla in HBL → galla −1,00,000, HBL +1,00,000, profit unchanged.

transfers.title: Money moved
transfers.body: The latest moves between your accounts, with who did them. A crossed-out one was reversed.

to.title: To
to.body: The account the money goes into.

moveAmount.title: Amount
moveAmount.body: How much to move, in rupees.
moveAmount.example: 100000 → Rs. 1,00,000 leaves the galla and lands in the bank.

kind.title: Type
kind.body: What kind of account this is: cash (a galla or drawer), bank, Easypaisa or JazzCash.
kind.example: Second counter drawer → Cash. Meezan account → Bank.

name.title: Account name
name.body: A short name you will recognise when you choose where money goes.

accountNo.title: Account / wallet no.
accountNo.body: The bank account or wallet number, for your own reference.

opening.title: Opening balance
opening.body: The money already in this account on the day you add it. After that the balance moves only with sales, payments, expenses and transfers.
opening.example: HBL already has Rs. 2,00,000 → type 200000; tomorrow's online sale of Rs. 38,000 makes it Rs. 2,38,000.

book.title: Cash book
book.body: Every entry in and out of this account, newest first, with the balance after each one. Crossed-out entries were reversed.

profit.title: Profit
profit.body: For the days you choose: what you sold, what those things cost you, your expenses and the real profit left. Tax and money the owner took out are shown apart.
profit.example: This month: net sales Rs. 12,50,000 − cost Rs. 10,60,000 − expenses Rs. 50,000 = Rs. 1,40,000 profit.

top.title: Best sellers
top.body: What sold the most in the chosen days: phones grouped by model, other items by name, with how many, the amount and the profit on them.

estimate.title: Estimate
estimate.body: A guess of the next 7 days' sales from the same weekdays of the last 4 weeks, and how many days each model's stock will last at the last 30 days' speed. A guess, not a promise.
estimate.example: Next 7 days ≈ Rs. 3,10,000. Infinix Hot 40: 2 left, sells 1 a day → runs out in 2 days → "Buy more".

old.title: Old stock
old.body: Phones in stock today grouped by how many days they have been in the shop: 0–15, 16–30, 31–60 and over 60, with their buying value.
old.example: 60+ days: 4 phones worth Rs. 1,80,000 → money stuck; think about a lower price.

types.title: Stock by type
types.body: Your stock split into phones, tablets and watches: how many, their value at cost and at asking price, how many are used, non-PTA, not lock-checked and older than 60 days.
types.example: Tablets: 6 units, cost Rs. 2,10,000, 1 lock not checked.

prices.title: Price changes
prices.body: Every change of a phone's asking price and every sale under the asking price in the chosen days, with who did it, who approved it and by how much.
prices.example: Ali sold an A15 asking Rs. 38,000 for Rs. 37,000 → listed as "Sold under asking −1,000".

books.title: Balance sheet tab
books.body: Your shop's books in two pages: the balance sheet (what you have, what you owe, your share) and the trial balance (every account, debit and credit). Made from the ledger, never typed by hand.
books.example: Your accountant asks for the balance sheet of 30 June → pick 30-06 and open Balance sheet.

grossSales.title: Sales before discounts
grossSales.body: All sales in the days chosen, before discounts and returns are taken off. Cancelled bills are not counted; tax is not included.

discounts.title: Discounts
discounts.body: Money taken off bills for customers in these days.
discounts.example: 20 bills with Rs. 500 off each → Rs. 10,000.

salesReturns.title: Sales returns
salesReturns.body: The value of things customers brought back in these days (returns and exchange refunds).

netSales.title: Net sales
netSales.body: What you really sold: sales after discounts and returns, without tax and without cancelled bills.

cogs.title: Buying price of what was sold
cogs.body: What the phones and items you sold had cost you. Only what was sold counts, not what is still on the shelf.
cogs.example: Sold 30 phones that cost you Rs. 10,60,000 in total.

grossProfit.title: Gross profit
grossProfit.body: Net sales minus the buying price of what was sold — the profit before shop expenses.

operatingProfit.title: Profit after expenses
operatingProfit.body: Gross profit minus the shop's expenses (each category is listed above it). Money the owner took out is not an expense.

otherIncome.title: Repair & other income
otherIncome.body: Money earned from repair work and other income in these days. It is added to the profit.

netProfit.title: Net profit / loss
netProfit.body: What the shop really earned in these days: profit after expenses plus repair and other income. If it is below zero it is a loss.
netProfit.example: Rs. 1,40,000 + Rs. 15,000 repairs = Rs. 1,55,000 net profit.

taxCollected.title: Tax collected
taxCollected.body: Sales tax taken from customers on bills in these days. It belongs to the government, so it is not in your sales or profit.
taxCollected.example: 18% on Rs. 2,00,000 of taxed bills → Rs. 36,000 to deposit with FBR.

ownerTook.title: Owner took out
ownerTook.body: Money the owner took from the shop for home or personal use. It lowers the cash, but it is not a shop expense, so profit does not change.
ownerTook.example: Owner took Rs. 50,000 for home → profit stays Rs. 1,55,000; galla is Rs. 50,000 less.

lists.title: Download lists
lists.body: The full list of sales, purchases or expenses for the chosen days, as Excel or to print, for your accountant.
lists.example: Download this month's expenses → send to the accountant on WhatsApp.

next7.title: Next 7 days (estimate)
next7.body: Expected sales for the coming 7 days: each day is the average of the same weekday over the last 4 weeks. Last week and the week before are shown to compare.
next7.example: Your last 4 Saturdays averaged Rs. 60,000 → this Saturday ≈ Rs. 60,000.

runOut.title: Which phone runs out
runOut.body: For each model: sold in the last 30 days, in stock now and days left at that speed. "Buy more" when it lasts 7 days or less; "Not selling" when you have stock but sold none in 30 days.
runOut.example: A15: 15 sold, 3 in stock → 6 days left → Buy more. Nokia 105: 4 in stock, 0 sold → Not selling.

ageBucket.title: Days in shop
ageBucket.body: How many phones have been in stock this many days, and what they cost you. The longer a phone sits, the more money is stuck in it.

typeCost.title: At cost
typeCost.body: What the units of this type in stock cost you in total.
typeCost.example: 12 watches bought for Rs. 1,20,000 in total.

typeRetail.title: At asking price
typeRetail.body: What the units would bring if all sold at their asking price.
typeRetail.example: 12 watches asking Rs. 1,50,000 → Rs. 30,000 possible profit.

typeUsed.title: Used
typeUsed.body: How many of these units are second-hand (not new / box-packed).

typeNonPta.title: Non-PTA / JV
typeNonPta.body: Units not registered with PTA (or JV). A SIM will stop working in them after the grace time, so they sell for less.
typeNonPta.example: 3 non-PTA phones → tell the buyer before selling.

typeLock.title: Lock not checked / still on
typeLock.body: First number: used units whose iCloud / Google / FRP lock was never checked. Second: units with a lock still on — they cannot be sold until it is cleared.
typeLock.example: 1 / 1 → check one tablet now; get the other one's iCloud removed by the seller.

typeSlow.title: Older than 60 days
typeSlow.body: Units of this type that have been in stock more than 60 days.
typeSlow.example: 2 watches over 60 days → put them on offer.

priceRows.title: Who changed prices
priceRows.body: The first list adds up each person: how many asking-price changes, how many sales under asking and by how much in total. Below it every single change or sale, with who approved it.
priceRows.example: Ali: 3 changes · 2 under asking · −2,500 → open the rows to see which phones.

sticker.title: Repair sticker
sticker.body: A small sticker for the customer's phone with its job number and details, so it is never mixed up with another phone on the bench or at a lab. The barcode is the job number: scan it and the job opens.
sticker.example: Ahmed's Samsung A54 comes in: print the sticker REP-000012 · Ahmed · A54 · Screen · Ready 05-11 and stick it on the back.

stickerFields.title: What goes on the sticker
stickerFields.body: Tap a field to put it on or take it off the sticker. Your choice is remembered on this phone. The phone's screen lock is never printed.
stickerFields.example: For lab trips pick Job no., Barcode, Phone model, Problem and Lab; for the counter add Customer and Mobile no.

send.title: Send to a lab
send.body: When your own technician cannot fix it, give the phone to a repair lab / technician in the market and record it here: who has it, since when, what they must do and their rate. One lab at a time.
send.example: iPhone 11 needs a board repair: send it to "Zain Mobile Lab, Hall Road", quote Rs. 4,500, back in 2 days.

atLab.title: At the lab now
atLab.body: This phone is with an outside lab. It shows since when, the expected day and the lab's quote. Turns red when the lab is late.
atLab.example: Sent to Ali Repair Lab on 01-11, expected 03-11; on 04-11 it shows "Late".

trips.title: Lab trips
trips.body: Every time this phone went to a lab: which lab, sent and back dates, fixed or not, and the charge. Nothing is ever deleted.
trips.example: Ali Lab 01-11 → 03-11 not fixed Rs. 500; Zain Lab 03-11 → 05-11 fixed Rs. 4,000.

problem.title: What should the lab do
problem.body: The work you are giving the lab, in your words. It shows on the job and in the lab's record.
problem.example: "Change screen, keep the old frame" or "check board, no power".

quoted.title: Lab's quote
quoted.body: The rate the lab told you before starting. Only for the record; the real charge is typed when the phone comes back.
quoted.example: Lab says Rs. 4,500; when it comes back it charges Rs. 4,000: you type 4,000 then.

expected.title: Expected back
expected.body: The day the lab promised to return the phone. After it, the job and the lab show "Late" so you can call them.
expected.example: Promised Thursday; on Friday the home of repairs shows it late.

outcome.title: Did the lab fix it?
outcome.body: Fixed: the job becomes "ready" and the customer gets the ready message. Not fixed: the job stays open; you can send it to another lab.
outcome.example: Ali could not fix the board → Not fixed → send it to Zain Lab.

charge.title: Lab's charge
charge.body: What the lab charged for this trip, even if it could not fix it (checking fee). On a customer's phone it is a cost of the repair; on your own phone it is added to that phone's cost.
charge.example: Lab charged Rs. 4,000 for the screen: your repair bill Rs. 9,000 → profit Rs. 5,000.

paidNow.title: Paid to the lab now
paidNow.body: Cash given to the lab when you collected the phone. The rest goes to the lab's khata and you pay it later from its khata.
paidNow.example: Charge Rs. 4,000, paid Rs. 1,000 now → Rs. 3,000 on the lab's khata.

cancel.title: Cancel trip
cancel.body: Use it when the phone was marked sent by mistake or the lab never took it. The trip stays in the history as cancelled, with your reason.
cancel.example: You chose Ali Lab but gave it to Zain: cancel with "wrong lab" and send it to Zain.

labs.title: Repair labs
labs.body: The labs and technicians in the market you send phones to. Each has its record: phones sent, fixed, not fixed, days taken, charges, and what the shop owes it.
labs.example: Zain Mobile Lab: 12 sent, 10 fixed (83%), 2 days on average, shop owes Rs. 6,500.

labPage.title: A lab's record
labPage.body: Everything about one lab: what the shop owes it, how many phones it got and fixed, how long it takes, and every phone with its dates and charge.
labPage.example: Ali Repair Lab: owes Rs. 500, 3 phones sent, 1 fixed, 2 not fixed, 3 days on average.

owe.title: Shop owes the lab
owe.body: The lab's charges not yet paid, from its khata. Pay it from the lab's khata with "Money paid".
owe.example: Charges Rs. 4,500, paid Rs. 1,000 → shop owes Rs. 3,500.

sent.title: Sent
sent.body: How many phones went to this lab (cancelled trips not counted).

atLabShort.title: At lab
atLabShort.body: Phones with this lab right now.
atLabShort.example: 2 at lab: an iPhone 11 and a Redmi Note 12.

late.title: Late
late.body: Phones still at the lab after the day it promised. Call the lab.

notFixed.title: Not fixed
notFixed.body: Phones this lab returned without fixing.

fixRate.title: Fixed %
fixRate.body: Out of the phones that came back, how many were fixed. Compare labs before you choose one.

avgDays.title: Avg days
avgDays.body: On average, how many days this lab keeps a phone.
avgDays.example: Back in 1, 2 and 3 days → 2 days on average.

charges.title: Charges
charges.body: All the lab's charges for phones that came back.

tab.title: Balance sheet tab
tab.body: Your shop's books in two pages: the balance sheet (what you have, what you owe, your share) and the trial balance (every account, debit and credit). Made from the ledger, never typed by hand.
tab.example: Your accountant asks for the balance sheet of 30 June → pick 30-06 and open Balance sheet.

asOf.title: As of
asOf.body: The reports show everything up to the end of this day. Pick an older day to see the books as they were then.
asOf.example: Pick 31-12-2025 → the balance sheet as it was on the last day of the year.

sheet.title: Balance sheet
sheet.body: Three boxes: what the shop has (money, people who owe you, stock), what it owes (people you owe, tax to pay) and the owner's share (money put in, profit so far, minus what the owner took). Has always equals owes + owner's share.
sheet.example: Has Rs. 9,50,000 = owes Rs. 1,50,000 + owner's share Rs. 8,00,000.

trial.title: Trial balance
trial.body: Every account with its balance on the debit side (what you have or spent) or the credit side (what you earned or owe). The two totals are always the same; an accountant uses it to check the books.
trial.example: Galla Rs. 40,000 debit · Sales Rs. 3,00,000 credit · Cost of goods sold Rs. 2,40,000 debit …

has.title: What the shop has
has.body: Money in the galla, bank and wallets, the udhaar people owe you, and the stock at its buying price.

owes.title: What the shop owes
owes.body: Money you still have to pay dealers and people (udhaar and len-den taken), and tax collected on bills that is still to be paid.

owner.title: Owner's share
owner.body: What the shop is worth for the owner: the money and stock you started with or put in, plus the profit so far, minus what you took out for yourself.

check.title: Balanced
check.body: The app checks that what the shop has equals what it owes plus the owner's share. It always should; if it ever does not, tell support.

profit.title: Profit so far
profit.body: All profit since the shop started on the app, up to this day: the same figure as the Profit tab for that whole time. Owner drawing is not counted as an expense here.
profit.example: The Profit tab from the first day to today shows Rs. 2,50,000 → the same here.

data.q: Is my data safe? Can other shops see it?
data.a: No. Every shop's data is separate and backed up every night. Only your staff, with the roles you give them, can see your shop.

phone.a: No. It runs on any Android phone (app or browser) and on iPhone / laptop in the browser. A thermal printer is optional.

offline.a: Keep selling. Sales, stock and payments wait on the phone and are sent when the connection returns.

staff.q: Can my salesman see the buying price?
staff.a: Only if you want. Owner, manager, salesman and technician each see what you allow.

cancel.a: Yes. Pay month by month; your data stays yours and can be downloaded as Excel at any time.

scanner.a: Any USB or Bluetooth scanner that types like a keyboard — most do, and they cost about three to eight thousand rupees. Plug it in and scan, no setup. Without one, the phone camera reads IMEIs and barcodes too.

android.a: Yes. Download it from this page (Download the app) and install it on any Android phone. The same account also opens in any browser on a laptop or iPhone.

verify.q: How does it check a used phone?
verify.a: When you buy a used phone you scan the seller's CNIC, note the PTA status and the IMEI; tablets and watches also need the iCloud / Google lock check. Until the check is done the phone cannot be sold; skipping needs a reason that the owner sees.

consent.a: The person selling you a used phone signs a declaration on the screen that the phone is his and not stolen. It is saved with his CNIC, the IMEI and the date, and can be printed any time.

yearly.a: Yes. Pay for a year at once and get 12 months for the price of 10 — two months free. Monthly payment is also there.

sale.s: Sell a phone or item in a few taps: cash, online, cheque, from abroad, udhaar or installments.
sale.e: Bilal buys an Infinix Hot 40 for Rs. 34,500, pays Rs. 20,000 on Easypaisa: the bill prints, Rs. 14,500 goes on his khata, the phone leaves stock.
sale.x1: One sale writes the bill, its lines and one balanced ledger entry (sales, tax, cost of goods, cash / bank / party).
sale.x2: Each phone gets an immutable "sold" event; stock and its cost are derived, never typed.
sale.x3: Below the asking price or below cost needs the owner / manager PIN (price rules per shop).

purchase.s: Buy phones and items from a dealer, or a used phone from a customer, paid now or on the dealer's udhaar.
purchase.e: Rehman Traders sends 2 Tecno phones at Rs. 28,500 each, you pay Rs. 40,000: Rs. 17,000 is on his khata, both phones are in stock with a barcode.
purchase.x1: Each line opens a device (IMEI-unique per shop) or an item batch at its landed cost.
purchase.x2: Ledger: stock at cost against cash and the supplier's account; returns to the dealer are reversing entries.
purchase.x3: A used phone from a customer needs the ID check (CNIC) before it can be sold.

stock.s: Every phone with its IMEI, PTA status, condition, price and full history from purchase to sale.
stock.e: Search 4512: the iPhone 13 whose IMEI ends in 4512 opens with when it was bought, from whom, its price changes and who it was sold to.
stock.x1: Status comes from a state machine (in stock, sold, at a shop, in repair, returned…); every change is an event row.
stock.x2: The history screen is built only from those events, so it can never disagree with the books.
stock.x3: Tablets and smart watches are the same device record with a type and a spec sheet.

verify.s: Before selling a used phone, check the seller: CNIC, phone of the seller, IMEI not blocked.
verify.e: Usman sells you a used Redmi: you scan his CNIC, note the PTA status; the phone shows "ID check done" before it can be sold.
verify.x1: A device carries a verification status (pending / done / flagged); a pending one blocks the sale.
verify.x2: Skipping it needs a reason ("I know this person") and is listed in the owner-only security audit.
verify.x3: The CNIC photo is stored privately per shop.

khata.s: One page per person: everything sold to or bought from them on udhaar, every payment, and the balance.
khata.e: Bilal's khata: two phones on udhaar Rs. 46,000, paid Rs. 26,000 → you will get Rs. 20,000; WhatsApp him a reminder in one tap.
khata.x1: Balances are derived from an append-only ledger; nothing is ever edited — a correction is a new reversing entry.
khata.x2: Ageing by the oldest unpaid bill, overdue only after a promise date.
khata.x3: A statement downloads as PDF / Excel for any period.

lending.s: Money you give a person or take from them with no bill, kept apart from bills, with a return date and reminders.
lending.e: You lend Tariq Rs. 25,000, back by the 5th; he returns Rs. 10,000. The card shows Rs. 15,000 open; on the 6th a WhatsApp reminder goes out.
lending.x1: A payment with purpose "lending" in the same khata, posted under its own ledger type so every report keeps it apart.
lending.x2: Open len-den is derived (unallocated lent − borrowed); "adjust against bills" moves no money, only bill status.
lending.x3: Return-date reminders run in the night job, at most every 3 days.

payments.s: Galla, bank, Easypaisa, JazzCash and cheques each have their own balance; every payment lands in the right one.
payments.e: A customer sends Rs. 10,000 on Easypaisa: the Easypaisa balance goes up, not the galla. Move Rs. 1,00,000 from galla to HBL in one tap.
payments.x1: Each account is a ledger account; transfers are their own entries and are never income or expense.
payments.x2: Online / cheque / remittance details (TID, bank, rate) are stored with the payment.
payments.x3: The day close compares the counted galla with the expected one and keeps the difference.

returns.s: A customer returns a phone (full refund or with a cut), you return one to the dealer, or swap old for new.
returns.e: A customer returns a phone of Rs. 10,000; you give back Rs. 9,000 and keep Rs. 1,000: the phone is back in stock, Rs. 1,000 is other income.
returns.x1: A return is a new document reversing the sale's share; the original bill is never changed.
returns.x2: The phone gets a "returned" event and is sellable again.
returns.x3: Exchanges post the difference in one entry.

repairs.s: Take a phone in, fix it or send it to a lab in the market, print its sticker, give it back with the bill.
repairs.e: Ahmed's iPhone 11 screen: you take Rs. 3,000 advance, send it to Zain Lab (Rs. 8,500), it comes back fixed; Ahmed gets a "ready" message.
repairs.x1: A job has a status flow; every lab trip is its own row (sent, back fixed / not fixed, cancelled) with full history.
repairs.x2: The lab's charge goes to its khata; on a customer's phone it is a cost of the repair, on the shop's phone it is added to that phone's cost.
repairs.x3: The sticker's barcode is the job number; the screen lock is never printed.

items.s: Chargers, cables, covers, glass: bought by the dozen or box, sold by the piece, with low-stock alerts.
items.e: Buy 3 dozen cables at Rs. 1,200 a dozen: 36 pieces at Rs. 100 each. Sell 6: the stock shows 30 and the profit is right.
items.x1: Every incoming movement opens a batch; outgoing ones empty the oldest first (FIFO) or use the average cost, per shop.
items.x2: Minimum price, wholesale price for dealers, promo price, and an own GST %.
items.x3: Adjustments need a reason; nothing on an item is ever deleted.

installments.s: Sell on monthly installments with a guarantor; see who is due today and who is late.
installments.e: A phone of Rs. 60,000, Rs. 15,000 now and 6 installments of Rs. 7,500 on the 10th; a reminder goes a day before.
installments.x1: The plan only says how the udhaar is paid back; the money stays in the customer's khata.
installments.x2: Due / late is derived from payments made against the plan.
installments.x3: Reminders are queued by the night job.

expenses.s: Rent, bills, salaries, tea: write them in categories; close the day by counting the galla.
expenses.e: Electricity Rs. 6,200 and tea Rs. 800 today; at night you count Rs. 45,200 in the galla against Rs. 45,000 expected: +200 is saved.
expenses.x1: An expense is a ledger entry against the chosen account; a correction cancels and re-posts.
expenses.x2: Owner drawings are kept apart and are never an expense.
expenses.x3: Expenses feed profit after expenses in every report.

audit.s: Profit, cash, udhaar, stock, sales, purchases, staff, repairs and len-den for any period, with print and Excel.
audit.e: This month: net sales Rs. 7,18,800, gross profit, expenses, real profit; who sold what; which phones are 90 days old.
audit.x1: Read-only: every figure is derived from the ledger, documents and device events, and can be drilled down to the bill.
audit.x2: Periods, an "as of" day and the previous period; reconciliation checks that the books balance.
audit.x3: Cost and profit only for the owner and manager; the security feed only for the owner.

staff.s: Owner, manager, salesman, technician: each sees only what their work needs. Attendance and an activity log.
staff.e: Kashif (salesman) sells and adds stock but never sees the buying price or the shop's profit; Imran (manager) sees reports.
staff.x1: A role → capability matrix is checked on the server for every request, not only hidden in the screen.
staff.x2: Every action is in an audit log with who and when.
staff.x3: Price-rule overrides need the owner / manager PIN.

barcodes.s: Every phone and item gets a barcode; print price stickers and repair stickers; scan with any scanner.
barcodes.e: Scan a sticker at the counter: the phone is added to the sale. Scan the shelf: the stock count shows what is missing.
barcodes.x1: A barcode is given inside the purchase transaction and never changes; uniqueness spans phones, items, IMEIs and SKUs.
barcodes.x2: Code 128 / EAN / QR; any USB / Bluetooth scanner works as a keyboard.

help.t: Urdu, Roman Urdu, English — and a "?" everywhere
help.s: The app shows one language at a time; every field, card and tab has a "?" with an explanation and an example.
help.e: Not sure what "Net sales" means? Tap the "?": "Sales after discounts and returns — sold Rs. 1,20,000, one came back Rs. 40,000 → Rs. 80,000".
help.x1: All text comes from translation files; the bills and messages follow the shop's language.
help.x2: 1,100+ help terms, each with title, explanation and example in three languages.
help.x3: A test fails the build if any "?" misses a language or an example.

devices.s: Works on any phone browser, as an Android app, on a laptop with keyboard shortcuts, or on one Windows PC without internet.
devices.e: Internet goes: the sale waits on the phone and is sent once the connection is back. At home you check the audit on the laptop.
devices.x1: A PWA (installable web app) and a Capacitor Android app from the same code.
devices.x2: Offline sales are queued with an idempotency key so they are sent once.
devices.x3: The one-PC Windows install keeps its own database and checks in with the provider.

security.s: Your shop's data is only yours; every change is recorded; nothing is deleted.
security.e: A salesman cancels a bill: the owner sees it in the security feed with who, when and why.
security.x1: Every table is scoped by shop; no query can read another shop's rows.
security.x2: Money is exact (decimal, never floating point); the ledger and device events are append-only.
security.x3: Fingerprint / PIN login, phone OTP for a forgotten password, daily backups.

landing.uniqueTitle: Everything a Pakistani mobile shop needs — together in one app
landing.uniqueSub: Other software is either for a general store, only online, or only in English. This one is made for the used-phone market: phone app, online, offline, verification and the seller's consent, in your language.

android.d: Install it on your shop phone: big buttons, the camera scans IMEI and CNIC, fingerprint login.
android.p2: Barcode and CNIC scan with the camera

online.d: Open it in any browser — phone, laptop or desktop — and see your shop live from home.
online.p2: Staff on their own phones, each with a role

offline.d: Internet gone? The sale is saved on the phone and sent the moment the connection is back. Or run it on one Windows PC without internet.
offline.p1: No sale is lost or sent twice
offline.p2: One-PC Windows install with nightly backup

consent.d: When you buy a used phone, the seller signs the declaration on the screen — saved with the phone, his CNIC and the date.
consent.p1: Signature, CNIC photo and IMEI kept together
consent.p2: Print the declaration any time it is needed

verify.d: Before you sell a used phone: the seller's CNIC, PTA status, IMEI checks, and the iCloud / Google lock on tablets and watches.
verify.p1: A phone with a check pending cannot be sold
verify.p2: Skips need a reason and reach the owner

langs.d: The whole app in the language your staff reads — and a "?" with an example on every field, in any of the three.
langs.p1: Bills and WhatsApp in the shop's language
